News.title: Secret Service swarm White House after reported security breach as ‘man demanding to talk to president’ is detained
News.content:
Next

A MAN has been arrested by the Secret Service outside the White House after a reported security breach.

Law enforcement and members of the military swarmed the corner of 16th and H, by Lafayette Park on Saturday afternoon after a car reportedly went onto the sidewalk next to the surrounding security fence.



The suspected driver was reportedly demanding to speak with Donald Trump as he was placed in handcuffs.

The President is currently in Camp David for the weekend and is not at the White House.



An independent White House reporter shared footage on X showing a convoy of Secret Service SUVs arriving at the scene.

“Secret Service officers and the members of military at the security perimeter present but ‘not at liberty to say’ what exactly is going on,” she reported.

No official statement has yet been issued by the Secret Service or the White House.

News.title: Terrifying moment teen stabs her teacher who desperately tries to fight her off after row over exam’s grade
News.content:
Next

THIS is the harrowing moment a teenager stabbed her teacher with a hunting knife after her mathematics exam.

Footage shows Betânia de Almeida fighting for her life at the Santos Peres State High School, in the Brazilian state of Pará.



At first, the girl is seen twiddling with her hair before whipping out the blade and lunging at her victim.

There was no one to help Almeida as she dodged the repeated attacks in the otherwise empty classroom.



She is seen wrestling with the student, who eventually appears to stab her.

The girl nearly gets Almeida a second time near her face before she frees herself from her grip and bolts from the classroom to seek help.

The student, who is in the 11th grade, was arrested at the scene of the attack on September 11.

The knife used in the attack was found inside the classroom, after being thrown into a bin.



She later told officers that she attacked Almeida because she disliked her, according to a Pará Civil Police report.

The victim was rushed to Cameta Regional Hospital, where she received stitches and was discharged Saturday.

Miraculously, her wound was not deep and the knife had not punctured any of her organs.



The school condemned the attack in a statement posted on Instagram, describing it as “violence that goes beyond the limits of a disciplinary case.”

“Aggression against teachers is unacceptable within the school environment,” it added.

It remains unclear if the girl will suffer any consequences after the attack.

Brazil faces high rates of school violence, leading the world in aggression against educators according to global studies.

More than half of Brazilian teachers have reported such situations in the classroom, according to research from the Ministry of Education.



In basic education, the number reaches 61%, and in higher education, 55%.

News.title: Tributes paid to ‘loving son’, 28, stabbed to death on millionaires’ row in London as cops launch murder probe
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

URGENT MANHUNT Tributes paid to ‘loving son’, 28, stabbed to death on millionaires’ row in London as cops launch murder probe







Next

A HEARTBROKEN family have paid a moving tribute to a “loving partner and son” who was stabbed to death on millionaires’ row in London.

Reece Salmon, 28, was attacked on Lloyd Baker Street, Clerkenwell, shortly before 11.20pm on Wednesday.



He was found with stab wounds and rushed to hospital, where he tragically died the following day.

In a heartbreaking statement, Reece’s family said: “We are utterly devastated by this loss.



“Reece was a loving partner and son, and he leaves behind many friends and loved ones.

“It is impossible to put our loss into words.”



The residential street is lined with million-pound homes, with properties selling for as much as £2.25million in the past year.

Police have launched a murder investigation, but no arrests have been made.



A Section 60 order has been authorised across Caledonian Road, Clerkenwell and Hoxton.

The order gives officers enhanced powers to stop and search people and vehicles.

The order runs from 4pm on Friday until 6am on Saturday.

Chief Superintendent Jason Stewart, who leads local policing, said: “This is a tragic incident, and our thoughts remain with the family and friends of the young man who has lost his life.

“You can expect to see additional officers in the area providing visible reassurance and working with partners to keep the public safe.



“The victim was found in a residential street, and members of the public may have information of vital importance to our investigation.

“If you can help, please come forward.”

Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 101, quoting reference CAD 8475/16SEP.

News.title: At least six injured after driver ploughs into festivalgoers in Canada as fleeing suspect arrested
News.content:
Next

AT LEAST six people have been injured after a driver ploughed into festivalgoers in Canada.

The vehicle hit multiple people at the St-Tite Western Festival in Quebec City, Canada around 4:30am local time Saturday morning.



According to local police, a male suspect then fled the scene but was found and arrested at around 5:30am.

Six people have been injured and hospitalized, but their conditions are currently unknown.



A man in his twenties is in custody and being interviewed by investigators, according to local outlets.

A safety perimeter has been erected around the site and traffic will be redirected as an investigation continues.



Three Quebec political party leaders were all expected to attend the festival on Saturday.

Coalition Avenir Québec leader Christine Fréchette issued her condolences saying, “My thoughts are with the victims, their loved ones, and all those affected by the events that took place at the Western Festival in St-Tite.

“The ongoing investigation will determine the causes of this act.”

Meanwhile, Pierre St-Pierre Plamondon, leader of the Parti Québécois, called it a “distressing scene.”



“My thoughts are with the injured individuals, their loved ones, and all those who witnessed the distressing scene in Saint-Tite,” he wrote on X.

“Thank you to the first responders who acted quickly. Quebecers should be able to enjoy places where they can gather and celebrate safely.”

Festival chiefs have said that Saturday’s events will go on as planned.



“An isolated incident beyond our control occurred early this morning on Saint-Joseph Boulevard,” organizers said.

“Our thoughts are with those involved and their families. We wish them a speedy recovery.”

“The safety of our festival-goers, volunteers, and staff remains our top priority. The Festival is a festive event where everyone should feel safe. That’s why every effort is being made to ensure this.”

The Minister of Homeland Security has said “all resources are being mobilized” and that “few details are known at this time.”

This is breaking news. More to follow…

News.title: Explosions warning & residents told to keep windows closed after massive fire tears through scrapyard in Epping
News.content:
MAJOR INFERNO Explosions warning & residents told to keep windows closed after massive fire tears through scrapyard in Epping







Next

A HUGE blaze has broken out at a scrapyard in Essex as authorities warn of explosions and urge residents to keep their windows closed.

Emergency services descended on the inferno in Epping, Essex, just before 7.30am with the site containing a “large number of vehicles”



Around 40 firefighters are battling the flames in Thornwood as dramatic images show smoke pouring into the air.

Residents have subsequently been warned to avoid the area and to keep their windows and doors closed.



Because it is a vehicle scrapyard, the fire service urged locals not to panic about explosions which they say are contained at the site.

An investigation will be launched to determine the cause of the blaze.

A spokesperson for Essex County Fire and Rescue said: “Around 40 firefighters are at the scene of a scrap yard fire in Thornwood affecting a large number of vehicles.

“There is smoke coming from the incident, if you live or work nearby please keep all your windows and doors shut.”

Group Manager Steve Wintrip added: “Crews are currently dealing with a large scrap yard fire.

“There is a lot of smoke coming from the scene so if you live or work nearby please keep all your windows and doors shut.



“The fire is under control and road will remain closed for some time while we continue to deal with the incident for the rest of the day.”

News.title: ‘Show off’ Uber Eats driver who killed student, 21, in crash as she walked home arm-in-arm with pal is jailed for 9yrs
News.content:
DRIFTING HORROR ‘Show off’ Uber Eats driver who killed student, 21, in crash as she walked home arm-in-arm with pal is jailed for 9yrs







Next

A SHOW-OFF driver was “drifting and skidding” around a town centre when he lost control and killed a student.

Natasha Thorp, 21, was walking arm-in-arm with her best friend Cerys Cartwright after what had been a “perfect” night out when tragedy struck.



The university student was hit by Saleh Mahmoud Taha Hassan as he careered off the road in his Toyota Corolla shortly before midnight.

Natasha sadly died from a traumatic head injury caused by blunt force trauma.



Her friend Cerys, also 21, was seriously injured in the horror collision and suffered a broken foot.

The pair had been walking along Brassington Avenue in Sutton Coldfield on August 22 last year after leaving the ASH pub and heading towards The Station.



Cerys told Birmingham Crown Court she and Natasha were in good spirits and walking arm-in-arm “as we typically do”.

Natasha was closest to the road, with Cerys on the inside, when Hassan lost control of his car at 11.53pm.



CCTV captured the 20-year-old repeatedly “drifting and skidding” around the A5127 and even circling a roundabout several times.

At one point he lost control but managed to regain it.

But rather than stop, Hassan then asked his passenger to film him drifting the car.

He was later clocked travelling at 46mph on the 30mph road before he lost control again while leaving the roundabout.

His Toyota veered towards the pavement and smashed into Natasha and Cerys.



Witnesses rushed over to help the stricken women, while one man confronted Hassan and repeatedly punched him before police arrived.

Cerys, who had been Natasha’s best friend for ten years, later told the court: “You are to blame.”

She described Natasha as “full of life” and a “ray of sunshine”, saying their night out had been “perfect” until the moment everything changed.

Natasha’s devastated dad described his daughter as “one in a million” who had “her own unique style”.

He said: “When she walked into a room it was like someone had switched a light on.”



Hundreds of tributes and flowers were left at a shrine for Natasha at Gracechurch Shopping Centre following her death.

Nearly 1,000 mourners attended her funeral to say goodbye to the much-loved 21-year-old university student.

Hassan, of Viscount Road, Sutton Coldfield, had passed his driving test less than two months before the crash.

He was not insured to drive that night, despite having carried out Uber Eats deliveries earlier in the day.

The court also heard an examination of his Toyota found a brake defect which would have been obvious to him while driving.



Hassan pleaded guilty to causing death by dangerous driving, causing serious injury by dangerous driving and causing death by driving while uninsured.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Judge Dean Kershaw described the CCTV footage of the collision as “horrific”.

Hassan was jailed for nine years and four months and banned from driving for 12 years and eight months.

News.title: Brutal storms batter top Brit holiday hotspot with water tornadoes and torrential rain as streets turn to rivers
News.content:
Next

BRUTAL storms have battered a top Brit holiday hotspot with water tornadoes and torrential rain, turning streets into rivers.

A powerful weather front swept from north to south across Spain’s Costa Blanca, in the province of Alicante, on Saturday morning – just 48 hours after a UK man died in flash floods near Barcelona.



Up to 50 litres of rain per square metre was unleashed along parts of the coast in just a few hours.

The deluge was accompanied by lightning striking trees, booming thunder and sudden flooding, turning roads into rivers.



Footage shows dozens of cars stranded in muddy waters while containers are swept into the path of traffic.

Another video shows water pouring inside a bar terrace, submerging chairs and tables.

Holiday hotspots like Alicante and Benidorm were also hit by the freaky weather conditions.

Near neighbouring Denia, a spectacular water tornado – called a waterspout – was also spotted tearing through the sea.



And in Orihuela, firefighters were deployed after a palm tree was hit by lightning and caught fire.

The Spanish national weather agency AEMET described the storms as highly localised but very intense, meaning rainfall amounts varied sharply even between nearby coastal communities.

The agency issues an orange alert for wind, rain and storms, which was later dropped.



Currently, there is an active yellow alert for Lorca, Cartagena and San Javier.

The storms came just days after a British man died in flash floods in the town of Olivella, around 20 miles from Barcelona.

Rescuers recovered the “lifeless body” of the man about 1,500ft from his car after it was swept away by a stream, authorities said.

Thursday’s deluge disrupted travel across Catalonia and Valencia, with flights cancelled and roads submerged.

Authorities further warned that popular holiday destinations Benidorm, Ibiza, and Magaluf will be hit in the coming days.



Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez warned of “very complicated situations” as authorities urged against any travel.

The horrific weather comes after Spain’s hottest summer on record.

Wildfires erupted throughout the nation as astonishing clips showed the extent of the devastation.

News.title: Shock moment ‘inappropriate old man’ leaps on female rider’s motorbike & grabs her waist before she slaps him on ear
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment an “inappropriate old man” jumped onto a female rider’s motorbike and grabbed her waist before getting slapped.

Ellie, from Salford, was left horrified when a random bloke ran into the road and hopped onto her motorcycle without her consent.



The 32-year-old had no idea the man was approaching her vehicle until he grabbed onto her hips.

The primary school worker claims her “survival instincts” kicked in when she gave him a “good whack”.



The shocking footage was captured on a bike helmet camera in Manchester city centre on September 12.

Ellie, accompanied by her friend Charlotte, who filmed the ordeal, was stopped in traffic on Oldham Street.

Dressed in all black with a black helmet, the biker revs her vehicle as she gets ready to start moving again.

The pair sat there patiently waiting to go when a man ran over from his group and hopped on her green Kawasaki ER-6F.



The group of men stood and laughed after he scurried back to them following the “whack” to the head.

Ellie was then seen holding out her palm afterwards incredulously after the shock incident.

Ellie said: “Never would have happened if I was with some of the guys.



“A man jumping onto a woman’s bike without consent is f**king weird.

“I was so focussed on not dropping the bike I genuinely didn’t even process how inappropriate the whole thing was until afterwards.

“Gave him a good whack though, so at least the survival instincts kicked in.”

Ellie shared the outrageous footage online, where the clip racked up over 387,000 likes.

She captioned it: “Someone come get their grandad. He’s out here touching women and bikes.”



The post was flooded with viewers slamming the man’s wild antics.

One person wrote: “He wouldn’t do that to a man.”

Another viewer added: “You didn’t hit him hard enough.”

One other person said: “Getting assaulted in broad daylight.

“Unfortunately not an uncommon experience for us women.”

Another commented: “The way his friends are all laughing in the background too. It’s vile.”

One person added: “This is disgusting oh my god, where do these men get the audacity?”

News.title: Folkestone hotel fire: Sleeping guests evacuated as fire rips through hotel in overnight chaos
News.content:
An overnight fire at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone has led to hundreds of guests being evacuated and the local council opening a welfare centre at Three Hills Sports Park

Fire crews battling a blaze at a Kent seafront hotel this morning have issued an "avoid the area" warning to the public.

Hundreds of guests staying at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone have been evacuated from the site following the overnight blaze, according to Folkestone and Hythe District Council.

The fire is believed to have started at around 1am on Saturday, with locals taking to social media to share images of the incident from afar. The cause of the fire has not yet been established.

Kent Fire and Rescue Service said 26 fire engines were used at the height of the blaze while crews wearing breathing apparatus worked to extinguish the fire.

A spokesperson for Folkestone and Hythe District Council said: "A fire is currently ongoing at the Folkestone Grand Burstin Hotel. We are operating a welfare centre at Three Hills Sports Park for people being evacuated from the site, where we are providing support to those affected.

"We are supporting all emergency services involved in the response and their efforts to get people to safety."

News.title: Folkestone hotel fire being treated as suspicious, say police
News.content:
Folkestone hotel fire being treated as suspicious, say police

Police said a fire at a major seaside hotel, which forced around 280 people to evacuate, was being treated as suspicious

View 5 Images Police tape at the Grand Burstin Hotel on the Folkestone seafront (Image: Cover Images)

A blaze that ripped through a hotel on the Kent seafront is being treated as suspicious, police said.

‌



Around 280 people were evacuated from the Grand Burstin Hotel in The Harbour, Folkestone, just after 1am on Saturday where a fire is believed to have started in the basement, Kent Fire and Rescue Service said. Emergency services rushed to the scene and a welfare centre was set up by Folkestone and Hythe District Council.

‌



Kent Police, on Saturday afternoon, shared that a probe into the circumstances was launched while adding that officers believe the fire may have been caused deliberately. No injuries relating to the fire have been reported.

‌



At least 16 dead as huge fire rips through nursing home with residents trapped READ MORE :

View 5 Images Fire damage on the walls of the hotel (Image: Cover Images)

Kent Fire and Rescue Service said 26 fire engines were used at the height of the fire while crews wearing breathing apparatus were working to extinguish the blaze.

The hotel overlooks Folkestone's harbour and has 550 rooms, according to the Britannia Hotels website. Officers are in attendance to assist with traffic flow while crews from Kent Fire and Rescue Service work to fully extinguish the fire.

‌



View 5 Images Emergency services rushed to the scene at around 1am (Image: Cover Images)

Folkestone and Hythe District Council posted on X and said: "A fire is currently ongoing at the Folkestone Grand Burstin Hotel. We are operating a welfare centre at Three Hills Sports Park for people being evacuated from the site, where we are providing support to those affected.

"We are supporting all emergency services involved in the response and their efforts to get people to safety.

‌



View 5 Images Around 280 people were evacuated from the hotel (Image: Cover Images)

"Our advice to residents living nearby is to: close all windows and doors; avoid the area and do not attempt to approach the hotel; follow the instructions of emergency services; keep roads clear to allow emergency vehicles to access the area. We will provide further updates as information becomes available."

In an update at 5:30pm, Kent Fire & Rescue said: "An investigation is underway to establish the cause of the fire at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone, which is being treated as suspicious."

‌



It added that four fire engines, a height vehicle and the technical rescue unit were at the scene, while firefighting operations were ongoing.

View 5 Images A welfare centre was set up by Folkestone and Hythe District Council (Image: Cover Images)

A spokesperson for Britannia Hotels Group said: "We can confirm there has been an incident at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone and we are taking immediate action to ensure the safety and wellbeing of all guests and team members.

Article continues below

"Emergency services are on site and we are fully co-operating with the authorities to support those affected and assist with the ongoing response."

Anyone who may have witnessed the incident or might have relevant CCTV or dashcam footage from the area, particularly from 10pm on Friday to 12.30am on Saturday, is urged to call Kent Police on 01843 222289 quoting 46/155727/26.

News.title: British tourist claims holiday 'ruined' and asks hotel for refund after mosquito bites in Crete
News.content:
British tourist claims holiday 'ruined' and asks hotel for refund after mosquito bites in Crete

A Brit reportedly asked for part or all of his hotel stay to be refunded after sending the a photo of bites on his leg

View 2 Images A tourist reportedly asked for a refund due to a mosquito bite (Image: Getty Images)

A British tourist reportedly left a hotel and asked for a refund after a mosquito bit them in Crete.

‌



The traveller reportedly demanded a partial or full refund after they sent an image of their leg covered in bites to the hotel. The Brit supposedly also asked for the mattress and room to be looked at by a certified health company and have the results of that inspection sent to them, according to local reports.

‌



The tourist claimed the mosquito bites ruined his holiday and made him feel "terrible" but an inspection of the hotel room reportedly did not find any issues.

‌



Animal bite infections surge after Britain's lockdown pet boom READ MORE :

View 2 Images The Brit had travelled to Crete, Greece (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

This incident, which happened on the Greek holiday island last month was shared by an adviser to the Region of Crete, Kyriakos Kotsoglou. The adviser said the tourist, after receiving the inspection report, left the issue and said he would travel back to Crete next year, according to Ekathimerini.

Kotsoglou said: "The issue is to avoid a negative development that could damage the reputation of your destination and to make the visitor feel that you have listened to and respected them."

‌



This comes after a German tourist won a payout after being unable to get a sun lounger, because other holidaymakers had reserved them with towels.

The man took his tour operator to court, in Hanover, Germany, and was paid out £850 two years after his 2024 holiday.

A court heard the man, who was on holiday with his family, got up at 6am and spent 20 minutes trying to find a sunbed, but they had all been taken. He argued that because a reservation system was allowed meant sunloungers were unusable.

‌



He added that the resort had a ban on reserving the sunbeds but said they did not enforce their own rule. This man had paid €7,186 (£6,211) to take his wife and two children to the holiday island of Kos.

The judge ruled the family of four was entitled to a refund on their package holiday, saying it was "defective".

This comes after a rise in cases of the potentially deadly West Nile Virus in several European holiday hotspots this summer.

Article continues below

In July, around 38 deaths from the West Nile Virus were reported in Italy with some cases found in Florence and Verona.

Cases were also reported in the early summer in Romania and North Macedonia. The West Nile virus was first identified in the West Nile district of Uganda in 1937 and has since spread to Europe.

News.title: BBC forced to apologise live on air during Arsenal humiliation at Brighton
News.content:
BBC forced to apologise live on air during Arsenal humiliation at Brighton

Live coverage of Brighton & Hove Albion beating Arsenal on BBC Radio 5 Live had to be interrupted for an apology soon after Pascal Gross scored for the Seagulls

View 2 Images The BBC briefly interrupted live commentary of Arsenal against Brighton & Hove Albion (Image: Clive Rose, Getty Images)

BBC Radio 5 Live felt obliged to apologise during their live commentary of Brighton & Hove Albion beating Arsenal in the Premier League. The broadcaster said sorry shortly after Pascal Gross put his side ahead in Sussex with a superb strike from distance in off the near post.

‌



Gross, 35, opened the scoring before Charalampos Kostoulas extended their lead with a similarly impressive effort. Chema Andres then headed in a third just before the hour mark against their out-of-sorts opponents.

‌



As a Saturday 3pm kick-off, the match was not broadcast live on UK television. However, there was live radio coverage.

‌



Arsenal torn apart by Brighton on horror afternoon for reigning champions - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Soon after the opening goal, 5 Live issued an apology. Following a brief update from another Premier League match, commentator Ian Dennis said: "Apologies for any inappropriate language that you may have heard, that might have been picked up from our effects mic here on BBC Radio 5 Live."

Alan Shearer spoke glowingly of Brighton on-air during Sports Report. He said: "It should have been more, the chances Brighton created, they were that good.

"They absolutely battered Arsenal. How many times have we said that recently? From start to finish today, Brighton were magnificent; every single one of them played their part.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal were abject against Brighton & Hove Albion (Image: Clive Rose, Getty Images)

"They were strong, they were fit, they went after Arsenal. They had no fear, and it worked brilliantly for them; it should have been six or seven goals.

"Every time they chased down the ball, they got it absolutely spot on. They did it as a team; they didn't do it individually. They thought 'we respected Arsenal, but we're not going to give them any space to play'.

‌



"The organisation was great, and that just doesn't happen on its own, and you've got to give Fabian Hurzeler credit for that." Dennis' co-commentator, Curtis Davies, was also full of praise for them, while being equally critical of Arsenal.

He said of Brighton: "The work ethic, the dynamism, the football quality that they showed, to the decisiveness they showed in areas of the pitch, it was always correct. We spoke about this Brighton side before coming into the game, where they scored a lot of goals.

Article continues below

"They came up against a tough Arsenal side with a strong defence. That defence today was nowhere near what it's used to being. The disappointment will be a set-piece goal conceded, Arsenal will have a real long look at themselves.

"On the other side of it, [Bart] Verbruggen had one big save to make. They didn't lay a glove on Brighton and didn't make anything of their attacking situations."

News.title: Warnings pupils are missing out as support staff pulled from duties to cover for teachers
News.content:
Warnings pupils are missing out as support staff pulled from duties to cover for teachers

EXCLUSIVE: A UNISON report found almost 39% of school support staff covered classes in place of teachers as part of their role, including staff in welfare and technical roles

View 2 Images Support staff are being asked to cover lessons instead (Image: PA)

Pupils are “losing out” because support staff are being asked to cover lessons instead, new research has shown.

‌



A UNISON report found almost 39% of school support staff covered classes in place of teachers as part of their role, including staff in welfare and technical roles.

‌



For teaching assistants (TAs), the figure was as high as 67%, with 38% of these saying it meant pupils missed a scheduled support session with them.

‌



More than a third (36%) said providing cover meant pupils they would normally support missed out on essential classroom help, while 29% said pupils with an education, health and care plan missed one-to-one support.

Schools urged to provide a minimum of one lesson outside per week under legislation READ MORE :

View 2 Images UNISON raised concerns about school staffing (Image: Getty Images/Maskot)

It also found 73% believed specialist sessions such as therapy were either unlikely or impossible to be rescheduled.

‌



Led by University of Greenwich researcher Rob Webster, the data is based on a survey of more than 8,000 school support staff in England.

UNISON warned most support staff received no additional pay for covering classes, and the union is now calling for ministers to review the role of support staff.

UNISON head of education Mike Short said: “Support staff are showing up for pupils every day, but they’re also being used to plug classroom staffing gaps. Children and young people are losing out as a result.

‌



“When teaching assistants and others are pulled into covering lessons, children can miss out on vital classroom support, interventions and one-to-one help. This is especially concerning for pupils with special educational needs and disabilities.

“Staff are being asked to take on extra responsibility without enough resources or, in many cases, additional pay.”

University of Greenwich lead researcher Rob Webster said: “The findings suggest that cover by teaching assistants and other support staff is masking wider workforce pressures.

‌



“Schools cannot keep compensating for teacher shortages by diverting these staff from the vital work pupils and schools depend on them to do.

“The growing reliance on support staff to cover lessons is another sign that the government needs a comprehensive response to the ongoing teacher recruitment and retention crisis.”

Responding, a Department for Education spokesperson said: “School support staff do an incredible job supporting our brilliant teachers and we’re determined to make sure that the dedication of the schools workforce is rewarded and supported.

Article continues below

“The number of teaching assistants has increased and we’re establishing the School Support Staff Negotiating Body to recognise the vital role that support staff play. Alongside this we’re backing our teachers and we are seeing more remain in the classroom or rejoin the profession.

“There’s more to do but we’re determined that school staff thrive.”

News.title: Man dies after falling from building in Liverpool city centre with police referred to watchdog
News.content:
Man dies after falling from building in Liverpool city centre with police referred to watchdog

A man in his 20s died after falling from a building in Liverpool city centre, Merseyside Police said

View Image Emergency services were called to Low Hill in Islington, Liverpool, on Friday afternoon (Image: Liverpool Echo)

A man in his 20s has died after falling from a building in Liverpool city centre.

‌



Emergency services were called to Low Hill, Islington, shortly after 1pm on Friday to reports of concern for the safety of a man on the roof of a building.

‌



Merseyside Police said the man subsequently fell and was taken to hospital, where he sadly died on Saturday. His family are being supported by specialist officers.

‌



Police said there are no suspicious circumstances surrounding his death.

"Due to police attendance at the scene shortly before the man sustained his injuries, a mandatory referral has been made to the IOPC [Independent Office for Police Conduct], which is standard practice in such events," the force said.

Article continues below

Paramedics and fire crews also attended the scene, where a large cordon was put in place to block traffic, the Liverpool Echo reports.

News.title: 'Show-off' UberEats driver 'drifting' around ring road killed pedestrian
News.content:
'Show-off' UberEats driver 'drifting' around ring road killed pedestrian

Saleh Mahmoud Taha Hassan, 20, had been 'drifting and skidding' around Sutton Coldfield when he lost control of his Toyota Corolla and ploughed into Natasha Thorp and Cerys Cartwright

View 2 Images Saleh Hassan, 20, was jailed for nine years and four months (Image: BPM Media)

A 'show-off' Uber Eats driver has been jailed after he struck and killed a young woman who was walking on the pavement.

‌



University student Natasha Thorp, 21, was on a night out with her best friend in Sutton Coldfield, West Midlands on August 22 last year when she was hit by an out-of-control Toyota Corolla driven by 20-year old Saleh Mahmoud Taha Hassan.

‌



A group who witnessed the crash immediately came over and helped the victims, while one person went straight for Hassan and punched him repeatedly before police arrived. Ms Thorp was pronounced dead at the scene by emergency services.

‌



Cerys Cartwright, 21, who was walking arm in arm with Natasha when the car swerved onto the pavement, suffered serious injuries, including a broken foot.

View 2 Images Natasha Thorp's family described her as 'one in a million' (Image: BPM Media)

Family plea after dad found dead on school field and e-bike pulled from canal READ MORE :

Hassan, from Sutton Coldfield, had only passed his test less than two months earlier and was not insured to drive that night, despite having made UberEats deliveries earlier that evening.

‌



On Friday, he was jailed for nine years and four months at at Birmingham Crown Court, and banned from driving for 12 years and eight months. Hassan had previously pleaded guilty to causing death by dangerous driving, causing serious injury by dangerous driving and causing death by driving while uninsured.

Prosecutor Nicholas Berry, recounting Ms Cartwright's memory of events, said: "Both she and Ms Thorp were in good spirits and walking along Brassington Avenue linking arms as they typically do. Ms Thorp was walking closest to the kerb and road. Ms Cartwright on the inside.

"The next thing Ms Cartwright was able to remember was waking up on the floor and hearing voices around her. She describes there coming a stage when she saw emergency services working on Ms Thorp."

‌



Ms Thorp's cause of death was recorded as a traumatic head injury caused by unsurvivable blunt force trauma, reports Birmingham Live.

Ms Cartwright, speaking from the witness box at the sentencing hearing, told Hassan 'you are to blame', as he listened via a video link from a booth at HMP Brinsford in Staffordshire.

She said she had been enjoying the 'perfect' night out with Ms Thorp, her best friend of 10 years who she described as 'full of life' and a 'ray of sunshine'.

‌



In a statement read to the court, Natasha's family said: "Tash was our daughter, a sister, a girlfriend, a granddaughter, a niece, and a friend to so many. No words will ever be able to express just how much we miss our dear Tash.

"Tash has been described as one in a million, as having her own unique style, and once met never forgotten. When she walked into a room it felt like someone had switched the light on. She could turn ordinary evenings into unforgettable memories.

"We will never know how her life would have turned out, what life she would have created. Not a single day goes by when we are not brought to tears thinking about our gorgeous girl.

‌



"We have lost someone that could walk into any room anywhere, and regardless of where that was and who was in there, fill that place with joy and chatter and laughter. We will miss Tash in everything we do."

Hassan had been driving his Toyota Corolla with his friend between Birmingham and Tamworth on the day of the incident, the court heard. He had carried out a few UberEats deliveries, helped his mother with a flat tyre and attended a mosque.

CCTV captured him 'drifting and skidding' around the A5127, as well as going around a roundabout multiple times. This saw him lose control of the car, only to regain it, after which he friend in the passenger seat to film him drifting the car.

‌



As he left roundabout he had circled multiple times, he lost control again, veering towards the pavement and into Ms Thorp and Ms Cartwright. The crash in Sutton Coldfield town centre unfolded at at 11.53pm, and Hassan had been clocked doing 46mph on the 30mph road beforehand.

An examination of the Toyota also revealed a defect in the brakes which would have been obvious to him while driving around, the court heard. Ben Williams, defending, said Hassan's 'idiotically reckless behaviour' was 'utterly out of keeping with his ordinarily positively good character'.

He told the court Hassan had achieved excellent A-Level grades and had planned to go university himself, as well as set up his own business. The barrister added he had written a letter to the victims' families acknowledging the 'devastating consequences' of his own actions.

‌



Mr Williams emphasised Hassan had expressed remorse privately, commenting himself that he deserves to go to prison. Judge Kershaw described CCTV footage of the collision as 'horrific'.

Passing sentence, he said: "It was an irresponsible, reckless and deliberate piece of driving that took away the life of Natasha Thorp and seriously hurt Cerys."

"There is no other way I can see this can be described in a way other than showing off. There is nothing that can be described as driving that was successful. It was simply stupid. The reason for this crash was you making a conscious decision to slide and skid the wheels of that car.

Article continues below

"You decided you wanted to have it recorded. That tells me you were showing off. There was no other purpose otherwise to have it recorded. You didn't want to record it to examine your driving afterwards and learn from it. You were recording it to be boastful.

"It is some sort of twisted reality - it is not a thing at all to be proud of."

News.title: Strictly's Karen Hauer says she 'doesn't miss' show as she speaks out after leaving
News.content:
Strictly's Karen Hauer says she 'doesn't miss' show as she speaks out after leaving

Strictly Come Dancing professional Karen Hauer was the longest-serving pro on the show before she was axed in a cull last year - and she has now spoken out about her life away from Strictly

View 3 Images Karen opened on her life away from Strictly Come Dancing

When Strictly foxtrots back on to our screens tonight, it will be the first time in 14 years without longest serving female pro dancer Karen Hauer, who shimmied her way through more than 100 numbers on the show.

‌



Karen announced her departure on social media in March and she is not the only high profile departure too. Longtime hosts Claudia Winkleman and Tess Daly have also left, as have pro dancers Gorka Márquez, Nadiya Bychkova, Luba Mushtuk and Michelle Tsiakkas.

‌



But Karen will be rooting for the new hosts, Emma Willis, Josh Widdicombe and Johannes Rabede. She said on social media, at the time: “The new series is so exciting. I'll definitely be watching my friends and I'm really looking forward to seeing Johannes, Emma and especially Josh. I danced with him on the Christmas Special dressed as penguins.”

‌



View 3 Images Karen was the longest serving pro dancer on Strictly Come Dancing

Now, Karen has spoken out for the first time since announcing that she was leaving the show. Karen admitted she doesn't miss the show and is relishing her time away after more than a decade on the dance floor.

Speaking to the Daily Mail, Karen reflected: "For 14 years I was locked in, and that's what I wanted... You can't go in halfway and that's what all the pros do, and that's why it's so intense.

‌



She continued: "I have some great memories from Strictly, but do I miss being in it? No. I like having a little less stress and a little bit more time. I know the process and I know how hard it is. I love seeing the new trailers and it's great seeing that energy, but I'm loving my time now. I feel very positive."

Karen, who was in the show from 2012 to 2025, has already started her new chapter - playing teacher Mavis in Devonshire Park Theatre's production of the Richard Harris comedy, Stepping Out in Eastbourne until the end of April, before taking it on tour until the end of September. She will then be playing the Wicked Queen in Snow White at The Princess Theatre, Torquay, in December and January.

Giving no dramatic reason for going, she simply says it was “the right time” to go, adding: “There's a time when you just have to go, ‘okay, well, that's a wrap.’ Now I have free time. I don't know what's going to happen in five years. So, I'm literally living the best life that I can right now, and not overthinking about the future.”

‌



The Venezuelan-American, who is a Latin dance specialist and World Mambo Champion, decided to keep her decision quiet from everyone, including her fellow pros, except her very closest pals, as she knew they would try to convince her to stay.

When we caught up with Karen in May, she explained: “I didn’t say anything because I know it would have been hard for them to digest and they’d have been like, ‘No, definitely no, not you,” she laughs. “I kept it within my tightest circle. But you know what? When I announced it, I’ve never felt such an outpouring of love. So many people were reaching out to me, and just being so kind.”

Away from work, Karen – who split from her third husband in 2023 – found love again two years ago with former rugby coach Simon Davidson. Smiling, she says her favourite thing to do when she’s not working is spend quality time with her handsome other half – and their four adorable rescue dogs.

‌



View 3 Images Karen has moved on from the show but wishes everyone the best still

“I have an amazing support network of friends, my family, my dogs, my partner at home,” she says. “He just turned 40, I’m 44, and there’s a different mindset when it comes to that stage of life – the enjoyment of life and making sure we’re taking care of each other.

“Our lives are very chaotic and we both travel a lot, so when we get back together, we have that total peace at home with our dogs. Just enjoying the little things in life is really important for both of us.”

News.title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets
News.content:
"The officer asked me to hand over my badge. He said that it was disabled," MS NOW reporter Akayla Gardner said. "I asked why I was not able to get inside. He said it was above him."

Gardner added that while her and her colleague's badges were disabled, an MS NOW producer was still able to scan her badge to get in, though she was not given an explanation as to why the producer's badge still worked.

CNN reporter Betsy Klein said a Secret Service agent told her her badge had been deactivated.

Later on Saturday morning, Politico said its reporter Cheyenne Haslett was denied entry and Secret Service revoked her pass.

All three outlets have spoken out against the decision, accusing Trump of violating their constitutional rights to free speech and freedom of the press.

An MS NOW spokesperson said in a statement that the White House "belongs to the American people and the decisions made inside are funded by our tax dollars".

MS NOW said it "intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy".

Politico Editor-in-Chief Jonathan Greenberger said in an internal email, shared in the outlet's Playbook newsletter, that the company stands by its reporters and will "vigorously defend" their First Amendment rights.

And CNN said, "We have a right under the US Constitution to do our reporting without hindrance or interference from the government and this ban is an illegal assault on this fundamental right."

In his announcement, Trump did not mention specific stories or reporting from the three outlets that prompted the move, but later said "it's really just cumulative stories over the last few years".

Trump added that there "may be others to join them", but has not given a directive banning additional news outlets. When later asked by a reporter what he meant by others to come, Trump responded: "Others to come in terms of fake news? Well, you know, the New York Times is fake news, the Washington Post is fake news."

Several groups dedicated to the freedom of the press have called out Trump's White House ban as illegal and unconstitutional.

A major group that provides legal services to the media - the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press - said it expected Trump's ban to be struck down quickly by the courts because it was "flatly unconstitutional".

"The First Amendment is clear that once the White House invites in some journalists, it can't ban others because it doesn't like their reporting," said Bruce Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, which provides legal services to the media.

It's the latest in a series of moves by the administration to target media outlets Trump says are critical of him, including legal action against US and international outlets like The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, and the BBC.

Some of the lawsuits have resulted in media organisations agreeing to pay multimillion dollar settlements. Trump's lawsuit against the BBC is ongoing.

Additional reporting from Bernd Debusmann Jr and Max Matza.

News.title: Major seaside hotel fire treated as suspicious
News.content:
In an update at 15:00, the fire service said that nine fire engines remained at the scene "dampening down any remaining hotspots".

Station manager Lawrence Pater said the "very severe" fire had raised concerns about the structural integrity of the building, and that it was seeking advice from inspectors.

Folkestone & Hythe District Council has set up a welfare centre at the Three Hills Sports Park and nearby residents have been advised to avoid the area of the fire and close windows and doors.

"We are supporting all emergency services involved in the response and their efforts to get people to safety", the council said.

South East Coast Ambulance Service said it assessed a number of people at the scene and one person was taken to hospital with minor injuries.

A spokesperson for Britannia Hotels Group, which runs the Grand Burstin Hotel, said it was "taking immediate action to ensure the safety and wellbeing of all guests and team members".

"Emergency services are on site and we are fully cooperating with the authorities to support those affected and assist with the ongoing response", it added.

News.title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins
News.content:
Sir Ed Davey said the Liberal Democrats are "a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform" as the party's conference began in Brighton.

The Lib Dem leader sought to strike a more combative stance as he faced down criticism from his own MPs that the party was struggling for relevance and being too polite about problems.

On the first day of the autumn conference, Sir Ed warned an "unholy alliance" between Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch and Farage could turn the UK into a "Trump satellite state".

Addressing speculation about a possible snap election, he said the party was ready to fight and would build its so-called orange wall even higher by winning more than its 2024 record of 72 MPs.

Sir Ed's attention-grabbing stunts helped raise the party's profile ahead of the last election, but recent polling showed 43% of respondents were unclear what the Liberal Democrats stand for, with just over half describing them as "weak".

South Cotswolds MP Roz Savage criticised Sir Ed's leadership ahead of conference, urging the party to rediscover its "insurgent spirit" rather than being the "polite custodians of a system that leaves people feeling powerless".

Speaking on the pebbles of Brighton Beach, Sir Ed dismissed those concerns and told reporters the Liberal Democrats would fight to stop a Reform government.

"One of the things that makes us unique is that we are a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform," he said.

"Many of the seats he needs to get himself into No 10 are seats that we will defend and indeed win - and we are also able to take seats off the Conservatives, because I really fear that Kemi Badenoch will give the keys to No 10 to Nigel Farage, so we have got to stop the Conservatives as well.

"We have got an historic opportunity to win many more seats and a moral responsibility to stop Reform."

He added a manifesto working group had already been set up in case of an early election "so we'll be ready if it comes early, but, you know, it still could be up to three years away".

Sir Ed insisted his party has a "distinctive position" in British politics, and will use the four-day conference to position it to take on the challenge from Reform as well as its typical rivals the Conservatives, talking up their focus on the NHS and goal of re-joining the EU single market and customs union.

The Lib Dem leader highlighted how six former Conservative cabinet ministers were among 25 Tories to have defected to Reform in the last two years, claiming they were now competing with each other to see who can divide the country more, rather than looking to fix the country's problems.

"An unholy alliance between Farage and Badenoch is the only way either can get into power," he said.

"Together, they want to turn Britain into a Trump satellite state which would trash our NHS, turn our communities against each other, cause untold damage to our environment, and trample over traditional British values of fairness, tolerance, and decency.

"A bigger Orange Wall is the only thing that can stand between Britain and this dangerous experiment, and we will not let them pass."

Davey also attacked the Labour government as having no plan for growth, failing to support families struggling with the cost of living and taxing small businesses "to the brink".

Ahead of a speech to party members, Davey urged Liberal Democrats not to look away from injustice or "human dignity under attack" but to fight back.

News.title: Smoke seen near Riyadh airport after air raid alerts in Saudi capital
News.content:
An AFP news agency journalist reported that firefighters could be seen trying to extinguish the flames of a burnt-out fuel tank belonging to state oil and gas company Aramco.

The Saudi Civil Defence had sent out phone alerts overnight warning of potential danger in Riyadh and other regions, before issuing an all-clear on Saturday morning.

Residents told AFP on condition of anonymity that they had heard what sounded like a round of explosions echoing through the city after the alerts.

"I heard the alarm, then my windows shook," said a resident of northern Riyadh, 27. "It was definitely scary. I was not expecting this."

On Friday, the Houthis announced that they had thwarted Saudi attacks on the Yemeni capital Sanaa which they said bore the hallmarks of an Islamic State operation.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya al-Sarea said Saudi Arabia had carried out 300 strikes across Yemen during the past week.

He warned the reported attacks on Sanaa would "not go unanswered".

The Houthis are locked in a civil war with Yemen's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia.

They have attacked targets inside Saudi Arabia on several occasions in recent months, and said this week that they were responsible for downing a Saudi fighter jet over Yemen.

According to an unconfirmed report from AFP, quoting military sources on both sides of Yemen's civil war, fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces claimed 48 lives on Saturday.

The Houthis said 31 of their fighters had been killed while government sources said their side had lost 17 soldiers, according to the news agency.

On Friday, the International Organization for Migration, a UN body, reported that the number of people displaced as a result of recent fighting had passed 104,796, external.

The Houthis recently seized control of the strategic port city of Mokha and Perim Island, a gateway to a key shipping route used by the Gulf state to export to Asia and Europe.

The group said the naval blockade was in retaliation for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled north-western Yemen.

Saudi vessels have relied on that stretch of the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.

On Friday, investment banking giant JP Morgan said it was struggling to predict how oil prices would be impacted by the war, telling investors in a rare note that "we simply don't know how to model the endgame".

News.title: Watch: Earl Spencer says he is telling the truth about a phone call with Charles after Diana's death
News.content:
Princess Diana's brother said King Charles "went ballistic" during a phone call with him in the days after his sister's death.

Earl Spencer spoke exclusively with the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg about claims he has made in a new book, alleging the then-Prince of Wales said "we'll forget her soon enough" during an argument over whether Princes William and Harry should walk in Diana's funeral procession.

In a strongly-worded response to the book claims, Buckingham Palace said the King was "mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss".

Read more about Laura Kuenssberg's interview with Earl Spencer.

News.title: Bitter row over Diana book brings back unhappy times for royals
News.content:
At issue is Earl Spencer's account of a conversation with the then Prince Charles after the death of Diana, with the prince accused of telling Earl Spencer: "We'll forget her soon enough."

He is accused of sounding "giddily elated" and like a "lottery winner" after the news of her death.

Buckingham Palace hit back with a response, which although dressed in courtier-like politeness, was essentially saying the conversation had never happened like that.

The King was said to be "mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways that others do not recognise".

Anyone who has lost someone knows how feelings can run high, people can hear different things about the same conversations - and families can fall out, or come together, in the wake of a death.

Psychotherapist Nick Hatter says he doesn't have a view on which version of events is correct, but he says that during traumatic events memories can be "distorted". A phone call doesn't have any of the visual clues or body language to give a fuller picture, he adds.

Hatter says there can be very different and unpredictable responses to grief, including a condition known as "bereavement mania" where someone can seem inappropriately hyper or even euphoric after the loss of a loved one.

The first opinion poll on who to believe has been published by YouGov - and it suggests a very split view, with 31% believing Earl Spencer's allegations, 36% suspecting it's not true and 33% saying they don't know.

Low thinks the book is unlikely to change many opinions, as "people have settled into their camps about how they regard Charles, how they look back on the Diana years".

There could also be a feeling that it's "tawdry" to rake up these claims so many years later, he says.

That's echoed by historian and author Sir Anthony Seldon who says Earl Spencer showed great courage at the time of Diana's funeral, but says his memoir is a "sad and unnecessary publication".

Royal commentator Richard Palmer says the book threatens to take the royals back to the difficult days of 1997.

"This book and the run-up to next year's 30th anniversary of Diana's death threaten to undermine the Royal Household's three decades of work to rehabilitate Charles and Camilla's image," he says.

Veteran broadcaster David Dimbleby, who led the BBC's coverage of Diana's funeral, said it seemed "odd" Earl Spencer would release the book now.

"Why 30 years later for God's sake you should do it... you have to ask him," he said on Radio 4's Today programme, adding he wished the appetite for the "cycle of gossip" would decline and instead that focus would shift to what kind of monarchy the country needed.

News.title: When a cherished tree began withering away, locals suspected a killer in their midst
News.content:
Every summer, Seoul turns a deep green, growing dense and lush under humid skies.

But this year, one tree was visibly suffering.

"Green leaves were falling to the ground, which shouldn't happen at that time of year," recalls Jung, who lives near the streetside ginkgo in Buam-dong, a largely residential neighbourhood in the north of Seoul.

The tree is beloved by locals, who believe it has occupied its spot for more than 100 years. So Jung couldn't ignore what she was seeing. With each passing day, her curiosity turned to concern.

A rotting carpet of familiar fan-shaped leaves soon surrounded the tree, a sight so alarming Jung and her neighbours formed a crew of amateur detectives to solve the mystery: what was ailing their hardy ginkgo?

The whodunnit engrossed Buam-dong and piqued the country's interest, making national headlines. But the attention unsettled Jung, who spearheaded the campaign but has since requested anonymity - we are using a pseudonym.

"Imagine a grandfather who silently embraces you every day, listens to you, and has always been strong and full of life," she says. "Suddenly, he begins to die.

"How heartbreaking would that be?"

So began one community's fight to save a cherished symbol of their neighbourhood. Their unlikely enemy, who they believe plotted a surreptitious attack, was a museum built to honour a pioneering, nature-loving Korean artist.

News.title: Daisy Edgar-Jones: I try and bury my emotion when it comes to love
News.content:
Daisy Edgar-Jones has been well cast in her new film.

She plays Elinor, the rational elder sister in Sense and Sensibility, opposite the younger, more romantic sister Marianne.

Speaking to the BBC, Edgar-Jones says that in her personal life, she really is like her character.

"When it comes to love, I think I am very much more Elinor in every sort of way," she says.

"I definitely lead a lot with my head and try and push aside, bury my emotion."

But she notes that one of the joys of the film is seeing Elinor learn to enjoy a "wilder, passionate side" of herself. "And I feel like I learnt to do that too," she says.

Best known for starring in hit TV series Normal People with Paul Mescal, Edgar-Jones, 28, is now taking on a lead role in the latest adaptation of Jane Austen's book.

Ahead of its release, sheâs been talking to me about whether we really need another Sense and Sensibility film (spoiler: yes. âThe more the merrier, in my opinion.â)

She also told me why young people today can still see themselves in Jane Austen's stories - and gave me her take on whether her friend and former co-star Mescal should be the next James Bond.

News.title: 'I'm telling the truth': Earl Spencer defends Diana book claims about Charles in BBC interview
News.content:
Reacting to the rare statement from the Palace, Earl Spencer said: "Well, is he furious? Is he furious or is he embarrassed?"

Speaking to the BBC at his Althorp estate, he added: "I've only ever had two calls on the line with Prince Charles at any stage of my life.

"I was hyper alert to what he was saying and those are precisely the words that he said and I promise that to you now. Genuinely, that is what he said. I don't hear him saying he didn't say that."

Pressed on whether he had evidence to back up the claim, he said he told family and friends at the time what had been said "because it was so monstrous".

In response to the Palace disputing his account, Earl Spencer, who shares his first name with the King, said: "They've sort of smudged that one, haven't they? They've said that recollections may vary."

When asked which Charles the public was meant to believe, he said: "I'm telling the truth."

Buckingham Palace declined to give a response to Earl Spencer's fresh comments.

The remarks may bring a renewed focus to the war of words between the Palace and the King's former brother-in-law.

News.title: Billionaire Man United owner says he has lost confidence in the UK
News.content:
One of Britain's richest people, Sir Jim Ratcliffe, says he has lost confidence in the UK, describing the country as "on the slide".

The founder of petrochemical giant Ineos, who also owns a large stake in Manchester United, said the UK was in decline due to a combination of high taxes and high immigration.

He told the BBC failing to invest further in North Sea oil and gas amounted to "insanity" and warned gas storage was so low that the UK could "run out of gas" if there was a cold snap this winter.

In response to the billionaire's criticism, the government said it was working to deliver growth and that business investment had increased in the last two years.

A spokesperson said they did not foresee any problems with gas supply: "We have a diverse energy mix and are confident in our security of supply."

Sir Jim, whose wealth is estimated to be around Â£15bn, has prompted controversy in the past with his comments on immigration. He was a supporter of Brexit but has been a tax resident in Monaco since 2020.

The businessman's UK exit has been followed by other high-profile billionaires, including steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal and most recently hedge-fund boss Chris Rokos.

Sir Jim said the politics of envy was driving people away from the UK.

"In America they applaud people who create wealth," he said. "Unfortunately the UK has got a bit of a green eye towards wealth at the moment."

He said for him to return to the UK "things would have to get better".

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he will take a "pragmatic approach" to oil and gas, but one of the biggest decisions facing the government, whether to give the go-ahead to further development of the oil and gas fields at Rosebank and Jackdaw, is still waiting to be resolved.

Sir Jim criticised the hesitation and suggested high taxes on North Sea operators were threatening the sector's viability. Tax on energy company profits is being reformed, but won't be fully implemented until 2030.

Ineos operates the Forties pipeline which transports about 30% of the UK's North Sea oil.

"You would expect [the government] to exploit our natural resources and we're clearly not doing that. We're shutting it down.

"If you tax everybody to death, they're all going to leave. And that's what's happening."

Recent climate data combined with record heatwaves have given weight to the argument against further exploitation of fossil fuels. However, political pressure has grown on the government to proceed with Rosebank and Jackdaw to support UK jobs, tax revenues and boost energy security.

Sir Jim backed those calls, saying it was "absurd" to import more energy than necessary.

The government spokesperson said that oil and gas would play an important role in the UK "for decades to come", but they added: "The transition to homegrown clean power is the only way to deliver energy and financial security for families and businesses."

News.title: Parents could lose benefits or face prison for child's crimes, minister says
News.content:
Parents could lose their benefits or face prison sentences for their children's crimes under reforms to the youth justice system, a minister has said.

Youth Justice Minister Jake Richards told the Times newspaper the system "should hold parents to account in a proportionate way for ensuring that they play their role in keeping communities safe".

His comments come after the government set out plans in May to strengthen and expand Parenting Orders, which can currently compel parents or guardians to address their child's behaviour by attending counselling sessions or face fines.

Richards said prison sentences would only apply "in the most extreme cases" and would be up to judges' discretion.

He described the proposed changes in England and Wales as part of a "carrot-and-stick" approach.

"Parenting orders are going to make sure that parents are more involved in the process by which we try to turn around young offenders," Richards told the Times.

"Yes, that will have some stick. It could be custodial, or docking benefits - ultimately it will be up to a judge. But we want them to be more involved and that comes with responsibilities as well."

Critics of the proposals say engaging with parents on a voluntary basis is generally more effective in building trusting relationships and providing support.

Jess Mullen, chief executive of the Alliance for Youth Justice which represents more than 70 organisations that advocate for children, previously questioned how putting parents in prison would provide "stability or support for the child".

Andrew Neilson, director of campaigns at the Howard League for Penal Reform, told the BBC: "Reforming parenting orders in this way risks being ineffective at best and counter-productive at worst.

"Criminalising parents is unlikely to help children who need support, and putting them behind bars would only put further strain on a failing prison system that is already bursting at the seams."

When the government white paper was announced in May, then Justice Secretary David Lammy said that strengthening parenting orders would mean "there are real consequences for parents and carers who wilfully fail to support efforts to address their children's behaviour."

He told BBC Breakfast at the time that if a parent was struggling, then the "judge can intervene to make sure that the young person is getting the support that they need and the parent is doing the best that they can".

He also said he expected the power to jail parents to be used "very, very rarely".

Courts are currently required to consider issuing a Parenting Order where a child under 16 has been convicted of an offence.

They can also consider an order for 16 and 17-year-olds if they believe this would help prevent further offences.

The term of the order must not exceed 12 months and breach of a parenting order is a criminal offence with a maximum Â£1,000 fine, according to the Sentencing Council.

However, government statistics show the use of parenting orders has declined in recent years, from more than 1,000 orders in 2009/10 to just 33 in 2022/23.

The government's youth justice reform plans come after Phase One of the Southport Inquiry report found "catastrophic" failures by the parents of the Southport killer Axel Rudakubana and various agencies meant clear chances to prevent the 2024 child murders were missed.

In the interview with the Times, Richards also rejected calls from lawyers to raise the age of criminal responsibility from 10, saying it would undermine "public faith" in the justice system and it was "not a priority at all".

In June, the Bar Council, the representative body for barristers in England and Wales, said the threshold should rise to 14 due to criminalisation at such an early age not being an "effective, proportionate or just response".

The United Nations has previously pointed out the UK has some of the lowest ages of criminal responsibility in the world and that it should rise it to the UN recommendation of at least 14.

On Thursday, ministers met with local leaders and experts in Manchester to discuss how devolution could help reform youth justice.

Additional reporting by AndrÃ© Rhoden-Paul & Shelley Phelps, political correspondent

News.title: Temperatures could peak at 26C as summerlike warmth returns next week
News.content:
Temperatures could peak at 26C next week as late summer warmth returns to parts of the UK.

Southern areas will experience the highest temperatures, but most locations will be warmer than normal for late September.

Warmth could last all week for some in England and Wales, but it might only be a short-lived boost for Scotland and Northern Ireland.

The high pressure, which is responsible for the warmth, will also mean little rain for places continuing to experience drought conditions.

News.title: Michael Marra announced as new Scottish Labour leader
News.content:
He went on to thank his opponents, Joe Fagan and Monica Lennon, and praised them for their ideas about how the party needed to change.

He said: "Joe argued for a politics rooted in people and place, for less control in the centre and more control for local communities. That should be the case in our country and in our party.

"Monica was right to say we need to reconnect with the trade union movement that birthed the Labour party.

"Her record delivering change through parliament is also a template for how Labour should behave in opposition â robust in our criticism of the SNP, yes, but also making our own change."

Marra continued: "Scots know what we are against. They can't tell you what we are for... Social justice. Eradication of poverty. Good work. Good housing. Good public services. The good life for working people. An economy where everyone has a fair chance in life, which redistributes power, wealth and opportunity."

News.title: A village familiar with tragedy mourns Noah Woods
News.content:
Canon Yvonne Tulloch founded the charity Ataloss after the death of her husband in 2008. As chief executive, she campaigns for more support for those navigating grief.

She said that as a society, we are not good at acknowledging grief - preferring to convince ourselves that we will live until old age; because of this, emotions can be suppressed and come to the fore following high-profile cases.

"We assume it's next of kin who will be the grievers and, while that is correct, it is not the whole picture.

"There are these ripples, there will be people who will grieve who we wouldn't assume would be doing so.

"Because we've been so poor at understanding grief, what can happen even more is when there is a tragedy that is near to us it makes us think it could have been us - particularly when it involves a child and you're a parent who can relate to it."

Tulloch added this can be "confusing" because those removed from a tragedy can feel they do not have a right to grieve.

She said: "Those who helped with the search have done so because they felt helpless. Equally there will be those who did not help and feel they should have done more.

"In most cases people will have made their decision for sensible reasons and you have to release yourself from guilt and realise you did the best you could."

For the family, there is a balance between appreciating the community support, but not being overwhelmed by it, she said.

"The important thing is not to isolate the family because you do not know what to say.

"People fear saying the wrong thing, but it takes nothing more than acknowledging somebody and saying, 'I'm so sorry, I just want you to know I care'.

"It can mean even more coming from a stranger."

Annie Owen, who volunteers at Ipswich and East Suffolk Samaritans, said that in the modern world, the overload of information can anaesthetise people to many tragedies.

"But for this pure innocent child, there is nowhere to put our reactions or our grief," she said.

Owen said it was important that people do not "beat themselves up" over what they did or did not do.

"So if anybody can find the way of looking at themselves and just thinking, this hurts right now because I'm decent, because I'm caring, because I have a heart. And I think that's a way of easing ourselves through it."

If you, or someone you know, have been affected by child bereavement, details of help and support in the UK are available at BBC Action Line

News.title: Police release CCTV of missing Lillia's last sighting
News.content:
The latest sighting at 10:36 at Piccadilly bus station on Monday follows a previous one earlier that morning when Lillia was seen boarding the number 36 bus from Salford.

Ch Supt Helen Critchley said: "Officers are making every effort to locate Lillia, and our team have been working through hours of CCTV footage and exploring every avenue to try and find her.

"I can now confirm that our last known current sighting was of Lillia at Manchester Piccadilly bus station at 10.36am on the morning of Monday 14 September.

"We can also share that she exited the number 36 bus at Piccadilly, with her boarding it in Salford.

"That bus service travels from Bolton through Salford and into Manchester city centre.

"If anyone has any information regarding Lillia's whereabouts or movements from this bus â or you were on the bus at the time she was also on there or when she got on in Salford or off in Piccadilly â please contact us via 101 or the Major Incident Portal below."

News.title: 'Fast, furious and dangerous' - a city's quad bike menace
News.content:
Sitting in his Birmingham city centre apartment, one resident says he can often hear them before he sees them.

The sound of revving engines is followed by groups of quad bikes and off-road motorcycles weaving through traffic, performing wheelies and riding through some of the busiest streets in the city.

"It's only a matter of time until something serious happens," he said.

Videos shared on social media over recent months have captured groups of riders travelling through areas including Hurst Street, Bristol Road and Corporation Street, often with faces covered and no visible number plates.

One video filmed by the resident showed a pedestrian narrowly avoiding being struck as a group rode through the city centre.

"I've watched them and they go through red lights, they just totally ignore the red lights," he said.

"People still cross when the pedestrian lights are green, but they don't even slow down to check.

"They're zigzagging in the middle of cars. No number-plates. It's bad because nobody sees any action happening and it's only a matter of time until something serious happens."

News.title: Bungling thieves caught on CCTV attempting to steal supermarket cash machine
News.content:
Two men who tried and failed to steal a cash machine from a supermarket in Carlisle, Cumbria, were convicted within hours of the attempt.

Tjay O'Neil, 35, and Dean Smith, 33, targeted the ATM at Morrisons on Kingstown Road shortly after 6.30am on Tuesday 15 September. The botched theft was captured on CCTV.

The pair appeared in court the following day, where they pleaded guilty in the face of overwhelming evidence against them, including the footage, the Crown Prosecution Service revealed in a post on social media.

Both men will be sentenced at Carlisle Crown Court on 14 October 2026.

News.title: Brighton v Arsenal LIVE: Mikel Arteta responds as champions thumped 3-0 in huge Premier League shock
News.content:
Mikel Arteta said Arsenal could have no complaints after they were thrashed by Brighton ( Reuters )

Mikel Arteta admitted Arsenal could have no complaints as they suffered their heaviest Premier League defeat in over three years against brilliant Brighton, who continued their superb start to the season with a deserved 3-0 win against the defending champions.

Arteta’s side arrived on the south coast looking to equal an 123-year club record by winning their first eight matches of the new season but were handed a reality check as they suffered the first defeat of their title defence.

The visitors started slowly and were stunned by first-half goals from the in-form Pascal Gross and the teenage striker Charalampos Kostoulas. Brighton, who were celebrating their 125th anniversary, continued where they left off in the second half as Chema Andres rose to head in a corner before the hour-mark.

Arteta acknowledged that Arsenal had to learn a “big lesson” and said: “I think they deserved to win the game. It started by us not doing the basics right for long periods, especially a lot of the first half. That set the tone of the game. I’m very disappointed.”

Fabian Hurzeler’s Brighton, who were the last side to beat Arsenal in the Premier League by three goals, in May 2023, have scored the most goals in the Premier League this season and on Wednesday knocked Manchester United out of the Carabao Cup.

Hurzeler praised a “special day” for Brighton and said: “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It's always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against.”

News.title: AI actress suffers glitch during bizarre Piers Morgan TV interview
News.content:
A Piers Morgan interview with a popular AI actress took an odd turn after the computer-generated avatar began speaking Chinese.

Tilly Norwood, a character created by production company Particle6 who describes herself as the world’s first AI actress, was in conversation with Morgan and actor Tom Conti on Piers Morgan Uncensored when talk turned to her new feature film Misaligned.

When asked by Conti whether her co-stars on the project were human or AI, Norwood began a reply before pausing and unexpectedly switching to Cantonese, leaving Conti dumbfounded.

An account ostensibly run by the AI character later played off the moment on social media, saying: “You try speaking 30+ languages and see if you don't show off occasionally.”
