England’s stunning 39-match winning streak is over after they were held to a 26-26 draw by Canada in a rematch of last year’s Rugby World Cup final.

The Red Roses had won every game they had played since a defeat in the 2022 World Cup final and still extended their unbeaten streak to 40 matches, but were unable to deliver the killer blow in an entertaining clash at Exeter’s Sandy Park, in their first meeting with Canada since beating them in the 2025 showpiece.

For Canada, it was a first draw against the Red Roses on English soil, a confidence boost ahead of the next two Tests at home.

England captain Meg Jones said afterwards: “It was amazing Test-match rugby, which is what we want. We want a battle and for it to be competitive.

“We have another two shots at them and get to go again next week.

“Our last pass and discipline let us down. We always look to get better.”

The two sides faced off in the first of three autumn meetings, with John Mitchell’s side also heading to Toronto and Ottawa next month.

Just shy of a year on from the Red Roses’ 33-13 victory at Twickenham, this was a much closer affair, with the two sides scoring four tries apiece in a gripping clash.

England came from behind twice in the first 25 minutes, with Claudia Moloney-MacDonald and Hannah Botterman replying to Lizzie Gibson and player of the match DaLeaka Menin.

Moloney-MacDonald scored a second to put the Red Roses in front for the first time, having had another disallowed, but Menin cancelled that out shortly before half-time, with the score 19-19.

The two sides were equally hard to separate after the restart, with Bryony Field putting England back in front before Olivia Apps scored under the posts, and despite a wave of pressure from the hosts in the closing stages. Canada clung on to end their winning streak.

Menin said: “It was a big challenge, I am a little tired. We didn’t get exactly what we wanted, but it was a great game of rugby.

“We really wanted to prove something here. This is just the start of this journey.”

Mitchell’s side are back in action against New Zealand at Twickenham next week.

An Australian jockey and a pair of teenage brothers from Essex are among those in with a chance of taking on Luke Littler for a shot at winning £501,000.

Thousands of amateur darts players travelled to Manchester for the final round of auditions for the new Netflix show ‘Beat Luke Littler’.

Zac Spain, known as Zachariah the Electrifier, came from Melbourne and it was worth the air miles as he made it through a rigorous three-stage qualification process, which involved getting the seal of approval from 16-time world champion Phil Taylor.

open image in gallery Essex brothers Alfie and Lewis Cook made it through to the next stage (Tom Dymond/Netflix)

He is now in contention for selection for the live show on October 30, which will be hosted by Gary Lineker, with producers deciding who makes the cut.

Twenty successful applicants will get the chance to take on Littler in a one-off leg of 501, with half a million pounds on the line.

Spain said: “I’ve travelled from Melbourne, so I got here at 5.40am this morning to make sure I was at the front of the queue.

“Being a professional jockey, I am used to pressure, and I think with my darting ability I can definitely win a leg against Luke. That’s all it takes.”

Alfie (14) and Lewis Cook (16) are also under consideration for selection after they both passed the auditions.

“It’s been a brilliant experience – my tummy is still doing front flips from all of it,” Alfie said.

open image in gallery Thousands of amateur darts players brave the rain (Tom Dymond/Netflix)

“We don’t really care what everyone else thinks, we proved that we can be good enough and it’s just a leg. Everything can happen and I know we can do it.”

Thousands did not come through the progress, though, including Samriddh Jain, who came from Mumbai.

He failed, but at least had an afternoon at a League Two football match to fill his day.

“I flew here from Mumbai for this audition. I am not the best darts player, but my entire premise around doing this was to share my experience and bring some focus to the sport of darts across India.

“I thought I put up a pretty decent performance, unfortunately, I didn’t make it to the next round.

“At least I get to go and watch Salford City versus Swindon Town this afternoon before I leave Manchester.”

A huge fire at an iconic hotel is being treated as suspicious, police have said, as they appeal for witnesses and anyone with dashcam footage to come forward.

Emergency services raced to the Grand Burstin Hotel in The Harbour, Folkestone, to tackle the blaze, which fire crews said started in the basement in the early hours of Saturday morning.

About 280 people were evacuated as dramatic pictures showed plumes of smoke billowing over the harbour. Residents living nearby have been urged to close all windows and doors and “avoid the area” as firefighters continue to tackle the blaze.

A blaze broke out at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folklestone ( PA Archive )

No injuries relating to the fire have been reported.

In an update on Saturday evening, a Kent Police spokesman said: “A fire in Folkestone is being treated as suspicions, with detectives seeking witnesses and dashcam footage.

“Kent Police was called at around 1.20am on Saturday 19 September, to a report of a fire at a hotel in Marine Parade, Folkestone.

“Officers are in attendance to assist with traffic flow while crews from Kent Fire and Rescue Service work to fully extinguish the fire.

“Enquiries into the circumstances are underway and officers now believe the fire may have been caused deliberately.

At its height, 26 fire engines were at the scene, the fire service said.

Folkestone and Hythe District Council posted on X earlier on Saturday saying: “A fire is currently ongoing at the Folkestone Grand Burstin Hotel.

“We are operating a welfare centre at Three Hills Sports Park for people being evacuated from the site, where we are providing support to those affected. We are supporting all emergency services involved in the response and their efforts to get people to safety.

“Our advice to residents living nearby is to: close all windows and doors; avoid the area and do not attempt to approach the hotel; follow the instructions of emergency services; keep roads clear to allow emergency vehicles to access the area.

“We will provide further updates as information becomes available.”

Kent Fire and Rescue Service said 10 fire engines remained at the scene on Saturday afternoon.

“Crews wearing breathing apparatus have worked hard to bring the fire under control and are now dampening down any remaining hotspots,” the service said in an update.

“It’s believed the fire started in the basement of the property, but the cause is not yet known. Around 280 people evacuated the building, and a welfare centre has been organised by Folkestone and Hythe District Council.

“No fire-related injuries have been reported.”

It added: “Members of KFRS’ Volunteer Response Team are on-hand to offer advice and support, and The Salvation Army is providing welfare to crews. Road closures remain in place while emergency services continue to work at the scene.”

A spokesperson for Britannia Hotels Group said: “We can confirm there has been an incident at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone and we are taking immediate action to ensure the safety and wellbeing of all guests and team members.

“Emergency services are on site and we are fully cooperating with the authorities to support those affected and assist with the ongoing response.”

Anyone with information about the fire or dashcam footage from the area between 10pm on 18 September and 12.30am on 19 September, is urged to call Kent Police on 01843 222289 quoting 46/155727/26.

Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall alleged that West Ham forward Taty Castellanos spat at him during the meeting of the London rivals at The Den on Saturday.

The incident came in the 65th minute of the derby and as goalkeeper Marschall delayed releasing the ball from his hands while his side were leading 2-0.

The West Ham forward Taty looked to close Marschall down before he picked up the ball, before the players appeared to get involved in an altercation in the penalty area.

open image in gallery Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall speaks with referee Paul Tierney during the match against West Ham ( Getty )

Marschall then appeared to point towards his jersey, gesturing that he was spat at. TV footage of the incident was inconclusive.

Lions boss Alex Neil confirmed the allegation afterwards, saying: “I believe so. Fil was saying to the referee throughout the game when that happened, at that point.

“Obviously I’m so far away so it’s hard for me to see what happened, but I wouldn’t presume Fil would say that without cause, if you like, so I don’t know. I’m sure the referees and the authorities, whoever, will look at it and if it warrants that it needs dealt with, I’m sure they will.”

Recommended Millwall and West Ham arrest update after 400 police officers deployed to heated London derby

Castellanos could face a six-match ban if the Argentine is found to have spat at Marschall.

Hammers boss Nuno Espirito Santo said: “I didn’t see, so I’m not going to comment on any allegations. I didn’t see it. And that’s not what we should be speaking about [in] this game, this game has much to speak about, it was a very intense game for both fans.”

Millwall and West Ham were meeting for the first time in 14 years, following the Hammers’ relegation to the Championship, with a large-scale Metropolitan Police operation planned in east London.

Millwall dominated the first half at The Den and led the Championship leaders 2-0 when the flashpoint occurred.

open image in gallery West Ham United’s forward Taty Castellanos ( Getty )

Marschall had the ball in his hands when he was closed down by West Ham forward Taty. Confusingly, referee Paul Tierney then appeared to signal a corner after Marschall went over the eight seconds permitted to restart play.

West Ham quickly took the corner, with Taty crossing for fellow half-time substitute Pablo to finish into the empty net, but referee Tierney halted the play and summoned both captains to the penalty box and instead signalled for Marschall to restart play.

Argentine forward Taty then closed down Marschall for a second time, with the goalkeeper delaying the restart before picking the ball up, which is when the alleged spitting incident reportedly took place.

Sky Sports reported that Marschall delayed releasing the ball because he claimed that Taty had spat at him, with the Millwall coaching staff reporting the allegations to the fourth official on the touchline.

The incident was also something of a turning point in a pulsating east London derby, with West Ham recovering from an awful start to salvage a 2-2 draw at The Den.

West Ham’s Mohamadou Kante pulled one back from 25 yards in the 74th minute before Konstantinos Mavropanos grabbed the equaliser in the 80th minute when he headed in a cross.

Kante was then sent off for pulling down Millwall’s Kyrell Lisbie when he was the last man and Lisbie was through on goal, but the 10 men of West Ham held on to claim a point.

Meanwhile, a total of six arrests were made after 400 police officers threw a “ring of steel” at The Den on Saturday, to ensure there was no repeat of the violence which has marred this fixture in previous seasons.

The force said the match took place “without significant disruption” across south east London, adding a total of six arrests were made as of 4pm on Saturday.

Arsenal’s 100 per cent start to their Premier League title defence ended in emphatic fashion as Brighton secured a stunning 3-0 win against Mikel Arteta’s dumbstruck side.

Arsenal arrived at the Amex Stadium with ambitions of equalling a 123-year club record of eight straight victories to start a season, but that piece of history looked in doubt right from the kick-off, with a rampant Brighton side delivering a masterclass against the champions.

Pascal Gross blasted Brighton ahead after 31 minutes before Charalampos Kostoulas doubled the hosts’ lead on the stroke of half-time.

Arteta sprinted down the tunnel in the hope of masterminding a half-time speech which would revive his side’s fortunes.

But Brighton remained on top after the interval and they served Arsenal a dose of their own medicine when Chema Andres headed home from a corner shortly before the hour mark.

A disjointed Arsenal were never at the races and Arteta will now have 21 days to stew over a shock result, which will abruptly end any suggestion of his side cantering to a second league title in as many seasons.

For Brighton, surely the best result of manager Fabian Hurzeler’s career – just days after a brilliant Carabao Cup comeback win at Manchester United – catapults them up to third in the table, just two points off the Gunners.

Arteta might have rotated his side for their win at Ipswich earlier in the week, but here he fielded his strongest side – one that simply could not live with their inspired opponents.

After just seven minutes Bruno Guimaraes, making his first Premier League start for his new employers, gave the ball away, and Kostoulas tried his luck from range.

open image in gallery Charalampos Kostoulas fires home Brighton’s second goal (Gareth Fuller/PA).

David Raya got fingertips to the Brighton man’s shot, but it was a sign of things to come.

Arsenal were pegged in by the relentless Seagulls and the hosts’ deserved breakthrough arrived.

Gabriel and Riccardo Calafiori allowed Gross far too much time to shoot and his fine 20-yard strike pinged in off Raya’s near post.

A case could be made for Raya being Arsenal’s MVP last season, but the Spaniard should have done better to divert Gross’ long-range strike away from danger.

The largely anonymous Bukayo Saka fluffed his lines when he failed to get any meaningful contact on a fine Arsenal counter-attack and Brighton raced straight up the other end to increase their advantage.

Calafiori was out of position and, when the ball fell to Kostoulas, the visitors failed to put any pressure on the Greece forward. He unleashed an unstoppable low strike from 22 yards and Raya was beaten again.

open image in gallery Chema Andres (centre) celebrates his side’s third (Gareth Fuller/PA).

It was virtually the last kick of the first half and Arteta sprinted for the dressing room ahead of a pivotal team-talk, with Arsenal’s 100 per cent record hanging in the balance, and then some.

And Andres all but ended any hope of a comeback when he leapt unmarked from a corner to head a third for Brighton with 57 minutes on the clock.

Brighton went in search of a fourth and they nearly had it when Pascal Struijk’s header, again from a corner, dropped just wide of Raya’s post with the goalkeeper swinging at fresh air.

Kai Havertz might have landed a consolation for Arsenal in the closing stages, but Bart Verbruggen was equal to the one-on-one – the keeper’s only real test of the match – while substitute Matt O’Riley could have marked a match to celebrate Brighton’s 125-year anniversary with a fourth, but Raya was on hand to spare any further embarrassment.

News.title: Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash
News.content:
Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

News.title: Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Red Roses’ 39-match winning streak brought to end in Canada draw
News.content:
The Red Roses’ extraordinary win streak of 39 consecutive Tests stretching back to the 2022 Women’s Rugby World Cup final is over. Canada, paragons of aggression, physicality and willpower at a packed Sandy Park, managed to hold an error-strewn England to a draw. The hosts’ unbeaten streak continues, but the winning run came a cropper in the middle of the WXV Global Series, in what was the first meeting of the two sides since last year’s World Cup final.

England face New Zealand at the Allianz Stadium next weekend followed by two further Tests against their Devon opposition in Canada. On this showing, the Canadians will fancy their chances in either Ottawa or Toronto, given that they pushed the greatest team that the women’s side of this sport has seen to the limit. Canada did have a scrum in the final play, deep in their own half, but the visitors chose to stick with the draw rather than twist for the win. Notwithstanding the boos that rang out at full time, this felt like a victory for the Canadians and, given the resources at England’s disposal, a defeat for the Red Roses.

But the record books will show that it was neither. And, no matter the pre-match belief of England head coach John Mitchell, Canada are not on the same level as professionalism and funding as his side. Mitchell had brought back nine players, many of whom featured in last year’s World Cup final victory, after the thrashing of Australia last week with the expectation that the history of 2025 would repeat itself. Canada had other ideas.

England’s downfall came at the set-piece, where their line-out malfunctioned and their scrum never gained dominance. Zoe Harrison looked a class above at fly-half and some of her tactical kicking, alongside captain Meg Jones, was immaculate. Claudia Moloney-MacDonald finished her tries energetically but, truthfully, England just looked a touch off the pace and a touch clunky, not trusting some of their connections, which had always looked so instinctive. Canada, by contrast, upped their game wonderfully, with Sophie de Goede, two-try tighthead DaLeaka Menin – of the Exeter Chiefs parish – and Olivia Apps, last season’s Premiership Women’s Rugby player of the season, all shining.

News.title: All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper
News.content:
It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

News.title: GPs summoned in Frankfurt as third malaria death reported
News.content:
While malaria is treatable if caught early, the patients were likely not considered to have the disease because they lacked travel history to countries where malaria typically circulates, meaning treatment was delayed.

“This is why we alerted the medical people in Frankfurt, if you have odd cases presenting at your clinic, please also consider that there might be malaria around,” Dr Tinnemann said.

“There is this assumption that people who get sick with a nasty fever in places like Frankfurt and elsewhere that have not travelled cannot have malaria, and we don’t bother to investigate. That’s got to stop. That’s why these people die,” Joe Lines, Professor of Malaria Control and Vector Biology at the London School of Tropical Hygiene and Medicine, told The Telegraph.

Before the two cases in Schwanheim – both of which occurred at least 3 miles from the airport where the first malaria cases were reported – investigators were working on the hypothesis that just a single mosquito was responsible for the outbreak, but the new cases have cast doubt on that theory.

“We expect mosquitoes to live between one and three weeks on average,” said Dr Tinnemann.

“We had five cases in the beginning of July, then another in August - at that point, there was a good chance that potentially it could just be one bug. But now it seems at least there must be one other,” he said.

Frankfurt’s public health board have now shipped blood samples from all eight patients to a specialised lab in Antwerp, Belgium, where scientists can carry out DNA analysis to indicate if the infections came from one or multiple mosquitoes, and are awaiting results.

As temperatures warm, experts fear that several tropical mosquito-borne diseases – including malaria, dengue fever, Zika virus, and chikungunya could become established across Europe.

Earlier this month, a colony of Aedes aeypti mosquitoes – the bugs responsible for transmitting dengue and Zika virus – were found breeding in a residential area in East London for the first time.

Airfinity, the disease-monitoring company, said of the malaria outbreak in Frankfurt: “the risk to the wider public remains low but non-zero.”

“Continued vector surveillance, rapid diagnosis, and ready access to antimalarials are critical to prevent further severe outcomes.”

News.title: Global fund utilises AI to tackle malaria, TB, and HIV amid aid cuts
News.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is helping to soften the blow from aid cuts, according to one of the world’s biggest development funds.

The Global Fund, which raises and invests billions of pounds to reduce the burden of HIV, tuberculosis (TB) and malaria globally says new AI-driven products like portable pregnancy scanners are helping to mitigate the funding gap.

“[We] have adapted pretty quickly to the changes in the funding environment; it has undoubtedly had negative impacts on health outcomes [...], but in some ways, the resilience of life-saving services has been remarkable,” Peter Sands, the executive director of the Global Fund, told The Telegraph.

The Global Fund is managing a $6 billion (£4.4bn) shortfall for the period 2026 to 2028 and has been forced to make difficult decisions to continue their work, it confirmed this week.

The gap comes as Western governments shift money from foreign aid to defence. The UK reduced its contribution to the fund by 15 per cent last year to £850 million, down from £1 billion.

But Mr Sands said investments in tools to tackle infectious diseases – including those driven by AI – are starting to pay off.

“Innovation is absolutely part of the answer when money is short. One of the few ways you can get to make the money go further is to have a better tool, a better way of doing things,” Mr Sands said.

News.title: Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players
News.content:
Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

News.title: Fiji declares national crisis as HIV epidemic escalates
News.content:
“The rollout has been slow and frustrating, and Fiji will pay for it in terms of lives lost,” said Prof Lisa Maher, an epidemiologist at the Kirby Institute in Sydney who is supporting Fiji’s response. “This is the only thing that will turn the epidemic around and stop people dying, and stop onward transmission of HIV to the general population.”

But the emergency declaration should provide political cover to introduce the needle and syringe programme, with a Cabinet subcommittee now created to remove barriers to action.

“The government is signalling that it is prepared to act in this particularly important and controversial area,” said Prof Maher. “It’s not coincidental that the draft bill [to legalise the distribution of needles and syringes for certain groups] now looks likely to go before parliament, after being blocked for 10 months… So it’s not just symbolic.”

Dr Jason Mitchell, head of Fiji’s HIV taskforce, added: “Since the government announced [the crisis], it has followed with some very rapid actions in progressing the needle and syringe programme. So that is being fast tracked through the necessary channels, and the government is determined to get that out in the next couple of weeks.

“We’ve gotten to the point where we really needed to take some really strong action,” he told The Telegraph. “This is the government realising that there have been challenges, and they need to step it up.”

It is hoped that the declaration will also turbocharge other elements of the response – for instance the scale-up of the post-exposure prophylaxis (Prep) scheme, which was introduced in May – as the virus gains a foothold in the broader population.

Although there has been a major focus on testing, treatment and education, UNAIDS still estimates that only 39 per cent of an estimated 9,100 people living with HIV in 2025 knew their positive status. Just 22 per cent were accessing antiretroviral treatment, and 117 people died in 2025, compared to 25 in 2021.

Fans walked out when Spurs went 3-0 down thanks to goals from Johan Manzambi in first-half stoppage time plus strikes after the break from Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia.



It took their miserable record to just three Premier League wins in their 25 on home soil – including none in three this season.

De Zerbi said: “We played well in the first half, we didn’t score, but [we were] too fragile.

“Because we can’t lose this game, in this way, absolutely. We can’t concede the second goal. We can’t lose balance, just because in the first half we are losing.”

De Zerbi repeated the excuse about the players’ poor “physical condition” that he has used many times already this season during the bad start.

THIERNO BARRY kept the good times rolling for the side that is fast turning crisis into celebration.

The Toffees began the campaign in a doom loop after a shambolic close to the transfer window that left boss David Moyes with only 18 senior outfield players and Barry as the only striker.



Moyes was not a happy man and neither were any of the faithful but Everton are now unbeaten in seven games.

Abdul Fatawu also helped to further lift the blues. With Ipswich Town still very much punching hard he was sent off in the 67th minute for the blatant dive that produced his second yellow card.



The action started in whirlwind style – and it just kept blowing.

Barry drove at the opposition box, creating space for Harrison Armstrong to deliver the kind of visionary pass that underlined the 19 year old midfielder’s vast potential.



Brennan Johnson turned brilliantly then right-footed wide from a dozen yards.

Jarrad Branthwaite, just included in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad, was anything but international class with a no-look pass in midfield that offered Emerson a perfect opportunity.

But Jordan Pickford, sporting a new shaven – headed look, showed just why he’s the Three Lions No 1, with razor-sharp instincts to hook away with his feet.

Barry often looked a distraught figure last season as he missed chance after chance following his £27.6M arrival from Villarreal although he did claim eight goals.

A FORMER Premier League star resigned as a National League manager during his press conference.

The ex-midfielder spent nine seasons in the top flight with Newcastle and Fulham.



But just four months after being appointed Hartlepool United boss, Lee Clark has walked away from the job.

Pools beat Barrow on the opening day of the National League season.



But since then, they have lost six of the next eight in the league – and both in the National League cup.

That included a 3-1 defeat at home to Worthing earlier on Saturday.



The result left Hartlepool 19th in the National League.

And Clark decided enough was enough and called time on his brief stint at Victoria Park.

He then announced his resignation during his post-match interview – after chants of “sacked in the morning” from the home fans.

Clark said: “There was no reaction to the result [2-1 defeat to Altrincham midweek] or the performance, all I want to say is I resign from my position with immediate effect.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I wanted to give this club and the fans something to be proud of, what they deserve, I haven’t been able to do that unfortunately.

“I know what this club means, I said it at the start when I got the job, I was excited to take it and I wanted to be the man that got them back where they need to be and deserve to be.

“It hasn’t worked out, you’ve heard the reaction of the supporters, I took a long time out of the game and I wasn’t going to be coming back and getting an atmosphere like that.

“It’s not going to change and it’s not nice for the family and friends to listen to that.”

A Hartlepool club statement added: “Hartlepool United Football Club can confirm that Lee Clark has resigned from his position as Head Coach with immediate effect.

Tynesider Clark came through the academy at St James Park, starting and ending his 16-year playing career with the Magpies.

Clark started his managerial career with three years at Huddersfield and also took charge of Birmingham for two-and-a-half seasons.

Sports.title: Newcastle 2 Hull 1: Toon cling on to hand Tigers first defeat of season despite Wissa penalty miss

NEWCASTLE desperately clung on and survived a late onslaught to end Hull City’s unbeaten run.

A bad-tempered clash ended with Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic confronting Toon’s coaching staff after his side’s 2-1 defeat.



But despite the post-game confrontations, opposite number Matthias Jaissle breathed a huge sigh of relief after getting away with one.

Toon looked to have produced the perfect response to their tonking at Leeds by blowing the Tigers away early doors.



Instead, despite securing the points, more questions and answers remain after a shocking second half showing.

The early promise surrounding Jaissle’s start in charge was in desperate need of resuscitation after his men were bullied at Elland Road.

But an electric start from Joe Willock and Lewis Hall sent shockwaves through the stunned Tigers.

However, Yoane Wissa‘s failure to convert a penalty almost proved costly as Mohamed-Ali Cho set up the nervous finish.

Stinging from the criticism in the aftermath of Monday’s 4-1 thumping in West Yorkshire, it took less than seven minutes for the feel-good factor to return.

Despite pleas for patience with his newly-assembled young squad, those would not have stopped the storm clouds gathering over Tyneside with a defeat here.

Fortunately, it was Newcastle’s old guard, led by architect Harvey Barnes, who blew them away despite Jaissle’s huge injury list.

Dan Burn, Ewen Jaouen (both ankle), Joelinton (thigh) and William Osula (foot) were already crocked and out.

And with Anthony Elanga (hamstring), Jacob Ramsey (thigh), Nico Gonzalez (concussion) and Amar Dedic (hamstring) joining them on the casualty list this week, the pressure was mounting.

You could even feel the nerves within the Toon Army making their way up to the famous cathedral on the hill when the team news dropped and there was no sign of Tino Livramento either.



That meant midfielder Lewis Miley filled in at right-back while Joe Willock dropped deeper to shield their vulnerable backline alongside 18-year-old Dutchman Sean Steur.

It was a daunting task, especially against a physical Hull team aiming to become the first promoted side to avoid losing any of their opening five Premier League matches since Portsmouth in 2003-04.

But Newcastle’s fears were eased in the third minute, and by the seventh they had evaporated.

It was exactly the start German Jaissle, 38, will have dreamed of.



Winger Barnes drove straight at Hull’s defence after they failed to clear, slipping it to Willock to pull the trigger past John Egan’s lunge and into Tzolakis’ net.

The Greek, who had amassed three clean sheets in his first four top-flight appearances, was still shell-shocked when the hosts doubled the lead.

Hall won it off Oli McBurnie on halfway to start the move and kept running.



He laid to Barnes, who again surged forward, before getting it back and firing past the static Tzolakis.

St James’ was rocking but, as ever, they never do anything easy this Newcastle lot.

The Mags had recorded just two clean sheets in their last 20 league games with only Crystal Palace and Chelsea conceding more Prem goals than them in 2026.

Toon’s goalie Lukas Hornicek almost gifted the visitors an instant way back.

After turning into trouble inside his box, Mohamed Belloumi pinched the ball off him, but luckily the Czech recovered in time to block the forward’s shot.



A fantastic tackle from Miley prevented Sorba Thomas with a tap-in from Matt Crooks’ cross.

Though it should have been game over moments before the break.

Miley nicked the ball off Thomas, who fell over and stopped Murphy from latching on to it by pulling at the winger’s ankle.

It felt big.

Despite Sven Botman coming close with a header from Hall’s free-kick, the away side came out with a belief they could get something.

They got all the encouragement they needed as they latched on to Botman’s poor clearance only for the lively Belloumi to curl over.



But the Tigers sunk their teeth in when given another bite of the cherry.

Belloumi took advantage of Miley’s miscontrol and found sub Cho, who held off Botman to slot past Hornicek.

Toon were tiring fast as Belloumi forced Newcastle’s keeper into a flying stop from distance.

Hearts were in mouths again when Tim Iroegbunam smashed a half-volley an inch wide of the far top corner as pressure continued to mount.

Sports.title: Brighton 3 Arsenal 0: Dreadful Gunners suffer shocking defeat as Gross, Kostoulas and Chema net in Seagulls rout
Sports.content:
Next

ON the day Brighton celebrated their 125th anniversary, their brilliant team delivered a performance for the ages.

In their entire history, Brighton will not have had many weeks like this and battering the champions was the cherry on top of their cake on what was a fabulous occasion.



The club was formed at the Seven Stars pub in Ship Street and had those businessmen been handed a crystal ball of what was to come in between beers, they would have been pretty pleased with themselves.

Yet even ahead of this game, no-one expected this. Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas stunned Arsenal with two goals in the first half before Chema Andres added the third in what was a thoroughly un-Arsenal like performance.



Brighton fans will long talk about this day, which came on the back of a 5-0 thrashing of Coventry and a 3-2 win at Manchester United.

In contrast, here was a real warning for Arsenal. A right old kick up the backside just before the international break.

If the first two goals were not bad enough, due to some lazy Arsenal defending, a stunned-looking Mikel Arteta will have nightmares about the third with Andres scoring with an easy header from a corner.

When the third went in before the hour, Arteta decided there was no point berating his team anymore.

He dropped his head towards the floor and trooped back to his dugout, knowing there was no way he could stop a shocking performance on the back of seven successive victories.

It was Arsenal’s first Premier League defeat since the 2-1 loss to Manchester City in April when Declan Rice famously said “it’s not done”.



Well, this season is certainly not done. It’s just starting and Arsenal will probably win the title again, anyway.

But here was a tap on the shoulder that even if a team drops their levels by five per cent against a dynamic team like Brighton, they will not get beaten but battered.



However, rather than just criticise Arsenal you have to praise Brighton who were bloody excellent

A classic performance from a club whose clever business in the transfer market – in an era when many teams have lost the plot – represents everything that is right about the modern game.

With the club celebrating their big day, in front of a record Amex crowd of 31944, Brighton’s players wore retro shirts – without stripes – marking the kit from their first season.

Yet it is fair to say that the current squad, with its players from18 different countries, is a bit different to the one back in 1901.

In March, after a 1-0 home loss to Arsenal, Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler said: “Only one team tried to play football today.” On this occasion, It was certainly the case here and Hurzeler will have loved every minute.



Brighton started well, pressed high and forced Arsenal into mistakes. Bruno Guimaraes, making his first Premier League start for Arsenal, gave the ball away which led to an early Brighton chance, but David Raya got his fingertips to the shot from Kostoulas.

And so their first goal was thoroughly deserved. It was a brilliant piece of football with Gross playing a part in the build-up before executing a fine, curling shot which Raya was unable to get a hand to.

Christos Tzolis backed off both Gross and Yasin Ayari in two different moments.



Ezri Konsa did not get close enough to Kostoulas who played a quick pass to Gross who took advantage of Riccardo Calafiori not getting close enough.

Remarkably, Kostoulas was given exactly the same amount of room when making it 2-0 just as the clock struck 45 minutes.

Bukayo Saka was guilty of missing an easy chance but he sent a tame half-volley into the arms of Bart Verbruggen and 15 seconds later, the ball was in the back of the other net.



Much to Arteta’s anger, Diego Gomez was given room to jog deep into Arsenal territory unchallenged and he found Kostoukas who, like his team-mate 14 minutes earlier, took two touches to pick his spot before sending a shot into the corner.

On this occasion, Arsenal’s other centre-back, Gabriel Magalhaes had to do much better.

Whatever Arteta said to his players at half-time did not make any difference,and you could not believe you were watching an Arsenal team defending a corner.

A couple of players were unmarked but it was Spanish defensive midfielder Andres who rose easily above Calafioro to score at the far post

Struijk should have punished more poor marking from a corner with the fourth but it hardly mattered and Raya delivered a good save from Matt Riley.



At the end, Brighton’s fans sang ‘are you Tottenham in disguise’ and ‘can we play you every week.’

RECOMMENDED STORIES

For Arteta, the international break has probably come at a good time. His players can fly off to their respective countries and return for the October 10 home game with Leeds with this game out of their heads. Hopefully.

As for Brighton, they will not have wanted this special day to ever end.

Sports.title: Six fans arrested at Millwall vs West Ham after fiery derby draw as cops deploy 400 officers to police clash
Sports.content:
Next

COPS have arrested six people at the heated Dockers derby clash between fierce rivals Millwall and West Ham today.

The points were shared between the two London clubs who had not met in a competitive fixture since February 2012.



Konstantinos Mavropanos rescued a point late on for West Ham to make it 2-2 in what was the 100th meeting between the East London rivals.

Hundreds of police officers were out in force today with the Dockers derby without question one of the fiercest rivalries in the game.



The Met Police deployed a whopping 400 officers across South East London as supporters of both sides descended on The Den,

The force has now issued a statement at 4pm on Saturday confirming six people have so far been arrested for a number of offences.

These included assaulting an officer, tailgating, and entering or attempting to enter a stadium whilst intoxicated.

All six people remain in custody, said the force.



Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage at around the same time on September 18.

The Met Police added: “As a reminder, a Section 35 dispersal order remains in place until 23:59hrs tonight, allowing officers to remove anyone causing disorder.”

Pictures after the full-time whistle showing mounted riot officers with batons raised struggling to keep the groups apart.

But rival fans were largely frogmarched to local stations without incident to begin their journey home after a pulsating match, as police enforced strict order to avoid violence.

Some bystanders were seen watching on gobsmacked as a few unsavoury scenes unfolded from a minority of supporters.



Officers had earlier formed a ring of steel around London Bridge station and other routes out of The Den after fears of fan trouble.

There were ugly scenes at full-time on the pitch too, as players squared up and had to be separated.

Millwall and West Ham have a fiery relationship which extends beyond the pitch, back to the bustling industry of East London in the late 1800s.



Stewards and authorities were already on high alert today in case any of the grim scenes of the past threatened to repeat themselves.

Prior to today’s clash, Millwall had 38 wins to West Ham’s 34, as well as 27 draws in the Dockers derby.

Since their first meeting in 1899, the pair have carved out a reputation as having one of English football‘s fiercest rivalries, and even spawned notorious depictions in films such as Green Street and The Firm.



Millwall were formed as Millwall Rovers in 1885 from workers of the J.T Morton Canning and Preserve Factory on the Isle of Dogs, East London – a company which provided sailing ships with canned goods for their travels.

West Ham‘s earliest form emerged a decade later, with Thames Ironworks FC forming out of workers of the Thames Ironworks and Shipbuilding Company in nearby Canning Town.

Understandably, their fanbases at the time were largely made up of workers from the local shipyards and factories in what became known as the Dockers derby.

The pair would meet for the first time in 1899, with Millwall – now Millwall Athletic – taking a 2-1 victory in a qualifying round for the FA Cup.

The clash would kick off a flurry of activity between the two, with the sides clashing sixty times over the next 16 years, including seven fixtures in 1902 alone.



The rise of their respective hooligan firms in the 1970s and 1980s did little to calm down the tension that had continued to bubble over since their early clashes.

Things hadn’t calmed down by 2009, when things would this time bubble over at West Ham’s former stadium Upton Park.

The rivals had been drawn against each other at the venue in the second round of the League Cup.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Goals from Zavon Hines and Junior Stanislas saw the Hammers leave 3-1 victors after extra-time, but not before a number of pitch invasions marred the match.

Things escalated even more after the match, with the unsavoury scenes spilling out of the ground, resulting in a number of injuries and one visiting fan being stabbed.

Sports.title: Portsmouth hit back to hold Blackburn
Sports.content:
Colby Bishop scored a fortuitous late leveller as Portsmouth drew 2-2 with Blackburn at Fratton Park.

John Mousinho made three changes from Pompey's dour 0-0 draw at Charlton with Bishop among those making way.

Tony Mowbray was also forced into making a change from Blackburn's win against Millwall as Yuri Ribeiro missed out with a hamstring issue and Harry Pickering came in.

The visitors started the brighter and Sam Morsy fed the ball through to captain Todd Cantwell inside the box, forcing the game's first corner via a deflected shot aimed point-blank at Daniel Bielica.

It was Pompey though who opened the scoring when Zak Swanson volleyed home past Rovers keeper Balazs Toth after Tyrese Shade's cross from the left was only half-cleared by Sean McLoughlin.

Image: Ryoya Morishita celebrates after scoring for Blackburn against Portsmouth

That lead lasted just seven minutes until Oladapo Afolayan netted his third goal in two games by converting a right-footed strike into the near post, making the most of a chipped ball played to him from the centre of the field by Pickering.

Bielica was forced into action again to scramble away Afolayan's flick-on from close range and then straight down the other end, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen scuffed an effort high and wide after a well-worked move which began with the receiving of a 40-yard diagonal switch from Madiodio Dia.

Abu Kamara was denied a first goal back in Pompey colours when Pickering timed a sliding challenge inside the penalty area well to clear the danger as the winger was preparing to shoot.

Home captain Marlon Pack received the game's first yellow card following a tackle in midfield on Rovers goalscorer Afolayan five minutes before the interval.

After surviving 10 minutes of Pompey dominance in the opening stages of the second half, Rovers took the lead for the first time in the game through Ryoya Morishita's drilled effort into the far corner, set up by Afolayan.

Mousinho's misery with injuries was further compounded by the forced withdrawal of Conor Shaughnessy, who pulled up unchallenged and had to be replaced after an hour.

His side did however claw their way back into the game when substitute Bishop inadvertently deflected in Kavuma-McQueen's right-footed effort after the Chelsea loanee did superbly to keep the opportunity alive for the hosts

Pompey had chances to snatch a third through Kamara and Bishop but were unable to find that late winner as the points were shared.

Both Mousinho and Mowbray will be relatively satisfied to head into the first international break of the season with a draw.

Sports.title: England swat aside Sri Lanka to return to top of T20 world rankings
Sports.content:
England returned to the top of the T20 world rankings as they earned arguably their most emphatic win yet in a series of drubbings dished out to Sri Lanka, beating the tourists by eight wickets at Emirates Old Trafford.

Off the back of 119-run and six-wicket wins in the opening two games, Harry Brook's side clinched a 3-0 series sweep as his 33 off 21 balls, plus Jos Buttler's unbeaten 62 off 32 fired the hosts to their 125-run target in a mere 9.4 overs.

Aneurin Donald (13 off 6) could only manage a brief cameo with the bat for the third time in the series - stumped off Tharindu Ratnayake - while Brook was run out just shy of victory, one that Buttler clinched with a stunning one-handed six over deep midwicket to make it 15 wins in a row for England against Sri Lanka in T20 internationals.

Score summary - England vs Sri Lanka, third T20, Emirates Old Trafford Sri Lanka 124 all out in 18.5 overs (put into bat): Pathum Nissanka (36 off 24 balls), Kamindu Mendis (35 off 28); Sonny Baker (2-17), Jofra Archer (2-23), Will Jacks (2-31) England 1262-4 in 9.4 overs (target 125): Jos Buttler (62no off 32 balls), Harry Brook (33 off 21), Aneurin Donald (13 off 5); Tharindu Ratnayake (1-28) Full scorecard Watch the first ODI of the three-match series between England and Sri Lanka on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Main Event from 12pm (12.30pm first ball).

The visitors had earlier been bowled out for a paltry 124 in 18.5 overs after being inserted by England, with Sonny Baker (2-17), Jofra Archer (2-23) and Will Jacks (2-31) picking up a couple apiece as the wickets were generously shared around.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jos Buttler produced a classy catch to help England take their first wicket against Sri Lanka

Pathum Nissanka (36 off 24) had briefly given cause for optimism - despite the early wickets of Lahiru Udara (10), to a strong catch from Buttler in the swirling wind, and Kamil Mishara (2) - as he cleared the rope on three occasions in the opening powerplay.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Harry Brook's brilliant catch dismissed Pathum Nissanka, during England's third T20 against Sri Lanka

Nissanka was a touch unlucky to ultimately perish in the seventh over, with Brook taking a terrific, diving catch at midwicket off one nailed out of the middle of the Sri Lankan opener's bat.

Skipper Charith Asalanka's innings was a sedentary 16 off 14 deliveries before being run out by Jacks - only just - after he nearly missed the stumps altogether with his take at the non-striker's end.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tom Banton missed a great opportunity for a catch against Sri Lanka, as he unfortunately slipped on a drainage line at Old Trafford

Kamindu Mendis (35 off 28) struck a couple of heavy-handed blows, but he too was lacking in support and the Sri Lankan collapse was well and truly in force by the time he picked out Jacks on the deep midwicket fence.

The tourists lost their last six wickets for 17 runs in less than five overs, with Wanindu Hasaranga's dismal departure - hit wicket off Archer after nearly swinging himself off his feet - pretty symptomatic of Sri Lanka's struggles in the series.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wanindu Hasaranga's powerful swing ended up knocking a bail off the stumps

And they have got little time to rectify things for the three-match one-day international series which follows and gets under way in Durham on Tuesday.

Brook: No 1 ranking an 'amazing' achievement

England captain and player of the series Harry Brook:

"Being back at world No 1 in T20s is an amazing achievement and one everyone should be really proud of.

"Everyone stepped up, especially lads who haven't played as much.

"For Sonny Baker to bowl three overs in the powerplay in two games is an amazing achievement, not going for many runs and taking wickets.

"We want to be a side when the conditions aren't in our favour where we are still able to manufacture a win.

"That might not be the prettiest but we are doing it extremely well and are trending in the right direction."

Broad: England look well-oiled

Sky Sports Cricket's Stuart Broad:

"England have been superb. They look a much better team than Sri Lanka but look well-oiled and seem to know what they are doing.

"Even players you might not feel are in the best 11 - remember, England are missing Phil Salt, Sam Curran and Jacob Bethell through injury - appear like they know what they are doing.

"With clear roles and responsibility, you get good performances and that's what nearly every player has produced in this series."

Sports.title: McIlroy two off pace as Manuel Elvira and Celli share Wentworth lead
Sports.content:
Manuel Elvira and Filippo Celli share the lead heading into the final round of the BMW PGA Championship after they both made birdies on the 18th to move one ahead at Wentworth.

However, 20 players will go into Sunday within four shots of the lead, including Rory McIlroy, who produced a box-office finish, sending the patrons into delirium on the 18th by making an eagle to move within two shots of the pace-setting duo at 11 under par.

McIlroy equalled four other players - Adam Scott, Joaquin Niemann, Davis Bryant and Kristoffer Reitan - to finish tied for sixth on the leaderboard through 54 holes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy makes an incredible final-hole eagle on day three of the BMW PGA Championship

In windy conditions, Spain's Alejandro Del Rey and American duo Johannes Veerman and JJ Spaun had all been tied with Celli and Elvira at 12 under par late in the third round.

Del Rey and Veerman had enjoyed epic days on the course, each shooting low scores of eight-under 64 to shoot up the leaderboard.

However, Celli rose to make four birdies on his back nine to card a third-round 69, while Elvira struck a four-under 68 as the pair jumped ahead of the chasing pack.

Plenty of other high-profile players also remain firmly in contention at the top of a bunched leaderboard, with Robert MacIntyre impressing to go five under through what was a flawless, bogey-free back nine, as he rose to tied-11th at 10 under par, alongside Ludvig Åberg, Ryan Fox, Matt Wallace and Sam Bairstow.

More to follow...

Sports.title: Preston denied by comeback from 10-man QPR
Sports.content:
Paul Smyth scored a 90th-minute equaliser for 10-man QPR as they came back from two goals down to draw 2-2 with struggling Preston.

Johnny Kenny's first goals for North End - including an opener after 64 seconds - left them in a great position in their first match since the sacking of boss Paul Heckingbottom.

But Kwame Poku pulled a goal back for Rangers midway through the second half and Smyth's late strike rescued a point for the west London side.

A run of six defeats from seven games left Preston bottom of the Sky Bet Championship, and this week cost Heckingbottom his job.

Image: Johnny Kenny celebrates after scoring for Preston at QPR

But Irish striker Kenny, a recent signing from Celtic, put them in control at Loftus Road, scoring from the first attack of the game and then doubling their lead after Rangers' Dennis Cirkin had been sent off.

First-team coach Jason Euell, placed in caretaker charge following Heckingbottom's exit, could not have wished for a better start.

Stan Mills' long ball should have been routinely dealt with by Jimmy Dunne near the halfway line, but the R's skipper hesitated and Kenny robbed him before racing through and slotting past goalkeeper Pierce Charles.

Worse followed for Rangers on the quarter-hour mark when Cirkin was shown a red card after clattering into Leo Leroy.

Andrew Hughes should then have made it 2-0 but headed Alfie Devine's cross wide of the target when unmarked.

That was a let-off for Rangers, but they were punished for more sloppy defending in the 26th minute.

Mills burst into the box from the right-hand side, Ronnie Edwards and Nicolas Madsen attempted to stop him but got in each other's way and Kenny met the resulting loose ball with a low first-time shot into the far corner of the net.

That left QPR battling against the odds, but they did create openings, the first of which came just before half-time when Poku was just unable to connect with Kealey Adamson's cross.

Rangers continued to attack after the break and Edwards volleyed wide, substitute Koki Saito also fired past a post, and both Madsen and Amadou Mbengue sent shots over the crossbar.

They were rewarded for their persistence with a goal after 66 minutes - winger Poku's first for the club.

Dunne was crowded out as he tried to flick on Smyth's long throw but Poku skillfully created some space for himself near the edge of the penalty area and thumped a low shot past Daniel Iversen.

Preston then had to cling on, with both teams hitting the woodwork as Rangers searched for an equaliser.

Callum Lang's header from Andrija Vukcevic's cross hit the top of the bar and, at the other end, Alfie Lloyd hit the bar shortly before being denied by Iversen at point-blank range.

Iversen could do nothing about Smyth's 20-yard rocket but did produce another fine save in the final seconds, this time to deny Madsen.

Sports.title: Swansea go top after victory at Lincoln
Sports.content:
Swansea moved to the top of the Sky Bet Championship after Stephen Eustaquio's first goal for the club earned a 2-1 victory at Lincoln at the ProAmpac Stadium.

After an insipid first-half display, the Swans were able to turn the game on its head after the break and, barring a big win for West Brom over Wolves on Sunday, will head into the extended international break top of the pile.

They lead the division by two points, ahead of Middlesbrough, after ending the Imps' five-match unbeaten run, despite them leading at half-time through Reeco Hackett's penalty.

Swansea goalkeeper Lawrence Vigouroux was worked in only the second minute when he got down to save Hackett's low shot after his defence had struggled to clear a corner.

His opposite number, George Wickens, was almost caught unaware when Swansea midfielder Elijah Just attempted to lob him from 45 yards, but he got back to prevent the ball sailing over him.

Hackett then had another opportunity for the Imps when he battled his way into a shooting position, but his strike went into the side-netting.

Vigouroux was fortunate he did not present the home side with the lead in the 22nd minute when he pushed the ball straight to Hackett just outside the area, with the Chile international very relieved to catch the attacker's underhit lob.

Lincoln were then awarded a penalty in the 39th minute when Josh Tymon bundled into the back of Freddie Draper, and Hackett got the goal his first-half performance merited by confidently dispatching from 12 yards.

It was a lead the hosts deserved as they went into half-time, but having been subdued in the first 45 minutes, Swansea came out for the second half firing.

They were level within two minutes of the restart when Melker Widell worked his way to the byline down the right before pulling the ball back for Moussa Yeo to convert from close range.

The turnaround was rapidly completed in the 51st minute when Canada midfielder Eustaquio received the ball from Just before his shot from outside box took a big deflection beyond the helpless Wickens.

Having looked in control before the break, the Imps seemed to lack ideas as they looked to prevent a first league defeat in nearly a month.

The Swans, meanwhile, almost made the game safe when Widell bent an effort narrowly wide from just outside the area.

Widell then almost had a second assist of the afternoon when he moved the ball to the right for Ronald whose shot was beaten away by Wickens as the visitors' second-half resurgence earned all three points.

Sports.title: Burnley still winless after Derby strike late to earn point
Sports.content:
Burnley were denied a first league victory since February as Mohammed Fuseini's dramatic stoppage-time equaliser earned Derby a 1-1 draw at Turf Moor in the Championship.

The Ghana winger, signed on loan from Belgian club Union Saint-Gilloise on transfer deadline day, drilled in an angled shot on the run, via the inside of the far post, for his first Derby goal.

Zeki Amdouni's 34th-minute far-post header looked to have given Burnley a much-needed victory to ease the pressure on their new head coach Nicky Hayen, already facing questions over his future despite only having taken charge in July.

Switzerland forward Amdouni bounced his far-post header into the net after goalkeeper Josh Vickers had flapped at a Lucas Pires corner.

Image: burnley

But Fuseini's equaliser leaves Burnley winless and bottom of the Championship, having failed to gain three points from a match Hayen had described beforehand as "must-win".

Hayen had made six changes to try to revive a team beaten at Swansea last weekend - dropping goalkeeper Max Weiss and former Manchester City defender Kyle Walker, and bringing back winger Marcus Edwards, re-registered after being left out of Burnley's 25-man EFL squad at the start of the month.

Derby, themselves in the bottom three and with a long injury list, created the first two chances just after the quarter-hour mark. Midfielder David Ozoh's shot from outside the penalty area was deflected wide, and from the resulting corner delivered by Joe Ward, defender Dion Sanderson met the ball at the far post but could only head the ball back across goal.

Amdouni then headed Burnley in front with the game's first effort on target, but Derby could have drawn level three minutes before half-time. Former Blackburn forward Sammie Szmodics ran clear on to a long pass from Ward but was stopped as he collided with Gregoire Coudert.

With the goalkeeper down, Ryan Hedges' follow-up was blocked by Igor Julio, before Carlton Morris played the loose ball wide to Szmodics, whose shot from a tight angle was cleared from inside the six-yard box by Anel Ahmedhodzic.

Ozoh threatened an equaliser 50 seconds after half-time with a run down the left, which ended with a fierce angled shot that Coudert beat away at his near post, and Hedges then drove a good chance wide from 12 yards as Burnley failed to deal with a long throw.

Burnley, having ridden those scares, began to create pressure as they sought a second goal, and substitute Largie Ramazani was only denied by a fine Sanderson block after Jacob Bruun Larsen had exchanged passes with Pires to set him up.

Coudert made an excellent save low to his left to push away Bobby Clark's 20-yard drive inside the final quarter of an hour, but Derby drew level when Rhian Brewster sent fellow substitute Fuseini away to equalise.

Sports.title: Wrexham beat Southampton after late own goal
Sports.content:
Wrexham secured a smash-and-grab 2-1 victory against wasteful Southampton courtesy of Keven Schlotterbeck's late own goal.

Phil Parkinson's men headed into Saturday's clash reeling from a 6-0 hammering at West Ham and desperate to kickstart their campaign with a first home Championship win of the campaign.

Kieffer Moore headed Wrexham into the lead during an opening period the visitors dominated and James Ward-Prowse's first goal since his return to saw Southampton level shortly after the break.

Saints pushed after Daniel Peretz prevented Moore scoring an outrageous strike from the halfway line, but the Welsh side edged a late win as Schlotterbeck turned in Jacques Ekomie's cross.

"You only win when you're spying," bellowed triumphant Wrexham fans just days before Southampton boss Tonda Eckert faces a Football Association hearing over the 'Spygate' scandal.

Wrexham co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac made a light-hearted social media jibe about the saga in the lead-up a game their side started on the backfoot.

Finn Azaz all too easily forced an early save and the hosts found in-form Southampton striker Cyle Larin a handful.

The Canada international attempted an audacious attempt from just inside the hosts' half and lifted another effort over, having failed to convert a variety of crosses sent his way.

Wrexham were being outplayed, yet Southampton's inability to take their chances allowed Parkinson's side to land the first blow.

Callum O'Hare forced a great save from Peretz and Southampton were found wanting from the resulting corner. Ben Whiteman sent over the 35th-minute set-piece and towering Moore powered home a header.

Saints were unable to eke out an equaliser before the break, but levelled five minutes into the second half.

A driven James Bree cross deflected into the path of Ward-Prowse, who followed a blocked initial attempt with a thumping follow-up effort.

That hard work was so nearly undone in the 55th minute when Moore went agonisingly close to scoring the goal of his life.

Picking up an aimless Saints pass, the striker quickly took aim from just inside Southampton's half and saw his shot tipped over by backpedalling Peretz.

Wrexham were furious to see a goal-kick awarded and their mood would have darkened had Anthony Patterson not stopped Ward-Prowse whipping in a free-kick.

Ryan Manning volleyed over as Southampton pushed to take the lead, but Wrexham were keeping the visitors at arm's length.

Parkinson's men kept fighting and their endeavour was rewarded in the 89th minute.

Ekomie made space to send in a low cross from the left that Schlotterbeck turned into his own goal under pressure from O'Hare.

Sports.title: Brighton demolish champions Arsenal 3-0 to mark anniversary in style
Sports.content:
So much for the new Invincibles. Arsenal were brought back down to earth with a shuddering bump by a scintillating display from Brighton as Fabian Hürzeler’s vibrant side celebrated the club’s 125th anniversary in style.

The special edition shirts they wore to mark the occasion will end up being collector’s items after the Premier League champions were ripped apart. Arsenal were attempting to record an eighth successive victory in all competitions to start the new campaign for the first time since 1903 when they were still known as Woolwich Arsenal.

Instead, Brighton – inspired by first-half goals from the veteran stand-in captain, Pascal Gross, and the exciting teenager Charalampos Kostoulas – find themselves two points behind Arsenal and in third place.

New signing Chema Andrés made the points safe from a corner 12 minutes into the second half. Having conceded three goals for the first time since December 2023 in all competitions, Arsenal will be concerned that it could easily have been more against the division’s top scorers – who have racked up 16 in five games.

The home supporters waved blue and white flags before kick off as the players swapped their usual kits for a deep blue limited edition shirt that was inspired by their first season in Southern League Division Two in 1901. That has caused controversy among fans after originally being listed on sale for £150 in a package that included a letter of authenticity from the club owner, Tony Bloom, and a keyring. Given this is the only time they will wear it, those who shelled out will be pleased they did.

What has made Brighton’s goalscoring exploits so impressive is they have managed it almost completely without their first-choice attack due to injury, while last year’s top scorer, Danny Welbeck, was sold to Chelsea in the summer. Georginio Rutter returned as a late substitute, but the damage had already been inflicted by then thanks to Gross and Kostoulas.

Jurriën Timber looked leggy on his first start since March and Bruno Guimarães was disappointing on his first Premier League start for Arsenal. Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy and drive in midfield was sorely missed in the week he was recalled to the England squad.

View image in fullscreen Pascal Gross fires home Brighton’s first goal against Arsenal. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

From the first whistle, Kostoulas – signed last summer for £30m – led Brighton’s fearsome press that provoked Arsenal into a number of uncharacteristic errors, including a misplaced pass from Guimarães that forced David Raya to tip a deflected effort from the 19-year-old around the post. Raya was also guilty of giving possession to the lively Yasin Ayari in a dangerous position. Arsenal looked rattled for the first time this season.

Christos Tzolis could not take a rare opportunity on the break after being picked out by Bukayo Saka and they were made to pay for it just after the half-hour mark. Perhaps wary of the unmarked Ayari to their left, Gabriel Magalhães and Riccardo Calafiori were slow to challenge Gross when he received the ball on the edge of Arsenal’s area from Kostoulas. The veteran picked his spot perfectly off the inside of the post.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ayari came close to doubling the lead five minutes before half-time when he fired into the side-netting before Kostoulas did. Saka had just spurned a great chance to equalise after being set up by Martin Ødegaard and once again Gabriel was guilty of ball watching as the Greek striker thumped the ball past Raya from 25 yards.

Mikel Arteta immediately sent out Max Dowman, who scored two goals against Ipswich in midweek, to warm up. He must have been tempted to throw the 16-year-old on at the start of the second half as Kostoulas went close again for Brighton.

It was too late once Andrés nodded in at the far post from a pinpoint Gross corner. “Are you Tottenham in disguise?” sang the delighted Brighton fans, who could barely believe how easy it all was.

Arteta introduced Dowman with 10 minutes remaining as he emptied his bench. But having been knocked off the top of the Premier League on goal difference courtesy of this heavy loss, there will be plenty of soul-searching during the three-week international break for the Arsenal manager.

Sports.title: Everton hold off Ipswich thanks to Thierno Barry goal despite VAR controversy
Sports.content:
After the trials and tribulations of the transfer window Everton can be content to reach the international break unbeaten and up to fifth courtesy of victory over Ipswich. David Moyes, and Pro Ref, will also be relieved that another controversial call from a video assistant referee did not determine the outcome.

Thierno Barry decided a close-fought contest that turned decisively in Everton’s favour when Abdul Fatawu was sent off for simulation, his second bookable offence, in the 67th minute. Barry had earlier had a second goal ruled out after an offside Brennan Johnson was deemed to have interfered with Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton’s ability to save a ball he made no attempt to save and was nowhere near saving. Unlike the Manchester derby, however, referee Stuart Attwell’s decision would not prove decisive.

There was good fortune to Everton’s lead, not so much in the unorthodox finish by Barry but the fact they managed to preserve it until half-time. A steady stream of unforced errors from previously in-form players – Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Jarrad Branthwaite and Harrison Armstrong among them – left Moyes visibly exasperated and invited pressure from Ipswich.

Everton started brightly and should have opened the scoring when Armstrong pierced the visitors’ defence to find Brennan Johnson. The Wales international spun away neatly from Issa Diop to give himself a clear sight of Christian Walton’s goal, only to drag a poor shot wide. Moments earlier, from the third minute, there had been a moving ovation from both sets of supporters in memory of Noah Woods, the three-year-old from Suffolk who went missing on Tuesday.

A loose pass from Dewsbury-Hall that resulted in Jordan Pickford denying Emersonn was the first sign of the sloppiness to come from Everton. But they also had the compensation of an early lead when Barry scored his fifth goal of the season and his strangest. The striker reacted sharply to divert James Tarkowski’s 25-yard volley into the net after Walton and the lively Jack Clarke had cleared a cross from Dewsbury-Hall. The Ipswich keeper had Tarkowski’s shot covered only for Barry to leave him wrong-footed by chesting the ball into the opposite side of the goal. The striker clearly moved to play the ball with his chest, so gets the benefit of the doubt over his intention.

Abdul Fatawu was a persistent threat down Ipswich’s right flank, making his self-inflicted dismissal all the more galling for O’Neil as his team chased an equaliser. The Ghana international forced a fine save from Pickford after Everton made a hash of clearing his corner and attempted to beat the England goalkeeper from inside his own half having intercepted a cross-field pass by Tarkowski. The long-range effort was drifting wide but Pickford, unaware, took no chances and scampered back to save. Fatawu should also have claimed an assist when floating a cross over the Everton defence to Leif Davis late in the first half. The left back, perhaps surprised to find himself onside and unmarked in front of goal, scuffed his shot badly wide of the far post.

Ipswich started the second half on top with Pickford saving from Julio Enciso and Abdoul Ouattara in quick succession. But it was Everton who converted next when Barry rose between four static Ipswich players to meet Dewsbury-Hall’s corner with a glancing header that sailed in off the inside of the far post. This time fortune was against the hosts and the French forward. Referee Stuart Attwell was sent to the pitch-side monitor to review whether Johnson was offside and interfering with Walton when Barry scored. Johnson was clearly offside but not impacting the goalkeeper’s ability to save the ball. Walton was on the opposite side of the goal to where Barry’s header went in, for a start. His reaction was also telling, as he made no appeal and turned in dismay to collect the ball for the restart. Attwell decreed otherwise. The home crowd responded furiously when the goal was disallowed and replayed on the giant TV screens.

Fatawu foolishly helped Everton recover shortly afterwards. Already booked for hauling down Dewsbury-Hall in the first half, the winger invited a second yellow card when diving to win a free-kick against James Garner. He became only the third player in the last six Premier League seasons to receive a second yellow card for simulation.
