View image in fullscreen Stuart Attwell shows Ipswich Town’s Abdul Fatawu (centre) a second yellow card for simulation. Photograph: Alex Dodd/Shutterstock

Everton had numerous chances for a second goal against Ipswich’s 10 men but Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall and Armstrong all miscued while Walton produced a fine save to deny substitute Tyler Dibling. Their profligacy made for a nervy finale as the visitors piled forward in search of an equaliser. Branthwaite, launching himself in the way of Diop’s goal-bound shot, helped Everton over the line.

Sports.title: Aston Villa grab victory despite late Spurs goals as De Zerbi’s side are booed off
Sports.content:
Spurs have a remarkable ability to find new ways of inflicting pain on their fanbase and they did it again here, petering out from a strong start into humiliating defeat to confirm their worst ever start to a Premier League campaign. On the upside, they did get two goals. They were both late consolations, but beggars can’t be choosers.

Aston Villa were meanwhile ruthless in claiming their first victory of the season. They capitalised in first-half added time to take the lead while Spurs were temporarily down to 10 men. In the second, Unai Emery’s side were robust in defence and clinical on the counter, and supreme strikes from both Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendía decided the contest. With Johan Manzambi the other goalscorer, there were pleasing signs for the Spaniard’s turbo-charged refit of his team.

Zion Suzuki was probably the man of the match and certainly the star of the first half hour. He made a series of saves in the opening phase of the game to deny Spurs the goal they so desperately craved. The highlight perhaps was a double stop from Sávio in the 11th minute, but also worth a mention is the save that denied Archie Gray from a tight angle with his heel. Suzuki made more passes into the final third than any other player on the pitch too, his 14 double the tally of Spurs’ £100m signing Sandro Tonali.

All the Japan international’s saves added up to frustration in the ground and that frustration began to affect the tone of the match. Spurs’ supporters were getting a sense that it might be (another) one of those days, and Villa’s players began to relax a little knowing they had a barrier behind them. With direct passes to Jackson regularly troubling the Spurs defence, a chance would surely fall their way eventually.

View image in fullscreen Tottenham fans leave the stadium with their side three goals behind. Photograph: Shutterstock

That moment ultimately arrived in first half added time and with one half of Spurs’ central defensive pairing – Micky van de Ven – receiving treatment on the touchline. The captain was being mopped up for a cut cheek as Buendía dinked yet another pass over the Spurs defensive line. It was partially dealt with, but Andy Robertson overplayed and in trying to activate a counterattack, slid the ball blind to John McGinn. The Villa captain whipped the ball back into the box, Boubacar Kamara’s shot was deflected and Manzambi was on hand to scoop a shot into the net from six yards out.

Roberto De Zerbi brought on Mohammed Kudus for the wishy-washy Mateus Fernandes at half-time and the mercurial Ghanaian lifted the roof off the stadium within 15 minutes of his arrival as he poked home from six yards out after a Robertson cross, only for the video assistant referee to pull it back for an offside on the Scotsman.

It felt in the moment that that was game over, so fragile was the Spurs sense of confidence. But there was time for Villa to turn the screw, Jackson next to strike with a piece of predatory magic. Latching on to a long kick from Suzuki, Jackson laid the ball off to Manzambi, who quickly returned the pass. The Senegal forward took the ball on his chest, lifted it Gazza-like over the head of Van de Ven and ruthlessly finished right-footed into the bottom corner. Antonin Kinsky got a touch but it wasn’t nearly enough and Jackson celebrated by playing the Roman emperor and turning his thumb down to the camera.

With 10 minutes remaining, and Villa camped out on the edge of the Spurs box, Buendía joined the fun with a perfect long-range effort. With minimal backlift it swept round his marker, out beyond the goal and then back in to smash into the top corner of Kinsky’s net.

Quick Guide Tottenham 2-3 Aston Villa key stats Show • Tottenham have failed to win any of their previous 48 games in all competitions in which they’ve conceded the opening goal (D11 L37), with 37 of those games coming in the Premier League (D8 L29). • This is Spurs’ worst start to a Premier League season after five games, with two points and a goal difference of -6, eclipsing their 2008-09 start (2 points, -3 goal difference). • Conor Gallagher’s goal (pictuted) ended a run of 492 Premier League minutes without scoring for Tottenham Hotspur, while their first league goal of 2026-27 came with their 67th shot. Opta Photograph: Andrew Matthews/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Conor Gallagher, coming off the bench with six minutes of normal time remaining, scored within three minutes of his arrival, while Jan Paul van Hecke reduced the deficit to just one with the last touch of the match. But the boos still rose up as fans contemplated the increasing likelihood of another tormented season. This had been billed as a match between two teams with poor form but high hopes. Villa look to have shed the former, can Tottenham still lay claim to the latter?

Sports.title: Newcastle bounce back from Leeds rout as Willock and Hall see off Hull
Sports.content:
Hull always knew that, sooner or later, they would lose a Premier League game but no one can say that Sergej Jakirovic’s team did not do everything in their power to try and delay that inaugural top tier defeat.

After conceding two goals in the opening seven minutes Hull could easily have folded but Jakirovic’s promoted players are made of sterner stuff than that. Tellingly, they also sensed the fragility of a gifted but injury hit and extremely youthful Newcastle.

Once Matthias Jaissle was forced into switching to an un-loved three at the back system and Mohamed-Ali Cho narrowed the scoreline, the visitors assumed control and it almost seemed a minor miracle that Newcastle clung on for an ultimately morale boosting victory.

Jaissle had harsh words for his players following last Monday’s 4-1 defeat at Leeds and, initially at least, it seemed they exerted the desired effect.

Sure enough, the game had barely begun before Joe Willock lashed the ball beyond Konstantinos Tzolakis. Three minutes were on the clock and it was only the third goal Hull’s £20m Greece goalkeeper had conceded since arriving from Olympiacos during the summer.

That opening goal arrived after John Egan blocked Willock’s initial shot but Hull’s subsequent failure to clear, permitted Harvey Barnes to pick out a midfielder retrieved from the St James’ Park deep freeze by Jaissle.

Four minutes later Barnes was once again the creator as he exchanged passes with the excellent Lewis Hall before the left-back newly recalled to the England squad swept the crispest of shots low into the bottom corner. Significantly, it had all begun with Hall dispossessing Oli McBurnie deep in Newcastle’s half.

Tino Livramento, too, was included in Thomas Tuchel’s latest squad on Friday but the right-back’s chances of joining up with England receded when a hamstring injury collected in training ruled him out here. Livramento was one of eight senior Newcastle players absent through injury but, undeterred, Jaissle’s starting XI were delighting in a spot of tiger taming.

View image in fullscreen Joe Willock slots Newcastle into a third-minute lead from close range. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

Yet as much as Jakirovic’s side struggled to second guess the dynamic Willock and the impressive 18-year-old Sean Steur in the home midfield, they were not subdued entirely. Indeed Hull came close to reducing the deficit when Sorba Thomas was inches away from turning in a Matt Crooks cross at the near post.

When deep in first half stoppage time Thomas tripped over his own feet and ended up hauling the advancing Jacob Murphy back by an ankle, a penalty was awarded. Yoane Wissa stepped up to the spot but saw his rather under-powered kick saved smartly by Tzolakis.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Jaissle’s bench included five academy players including the winger Kyran Thompson, a first year scholar who only left school in the summer, but when midway through the second half Newcastle’s manager finally made a change, he introduced the 34-year-old Fabian Schär in place of a tiring Steur.

This change prompted a switch to a back three, featuring Schär in the sweeping role. That configuration is, as he has made abundantly clear, far from Jaissle’s favourite formation and such feelings on the German’s part probably only intensified when almost immediately Hull scored.

With that re-vamped defence making a hash of clearing its lines after Lewis Miley – newly relocated from right-back to midfield – was caught in possession, enabling Mohamed Belloumi to play in the substitute Ali-Cho. The former England youth international, a summer signing from Nice, duly revelled in whipping a left foot, close range shot past Lukas Hornicek.

From then on Hull blitzed Hornicek’s box with a barrage of crosses, corners and shots from all angles. Newcastle were under siege and their goalkeeper did well to extend a foot and somehow divert the substitute Robinho Vaz’s half volley.

Sports.title: Kanté and Mavropanos rescue late point for West Ham in derby thriller at Millwall
Sports.content:
Welcome back, then, the Dockers Derby. We really must do this again. On a lovely soft September afternoon on the Bermondsey peninsula, watched by an outrage-ready media multiverse, something unexpected happened at the Den. A really good football match broke out.

Not wild or violent. No shameful scenes that nobody (trans: everybody) wants to see. Not in the stands or the streets at least: the only really sour note was an allegation of spitting against West Ham’s Taty Castellanos, which will now presumably be investigated.

Otherwise this was a thrilling, high-quality 2-2 draw between Millwall and West Ham, a game where for the full 90 minutes nothing outside the Den’s rattly corrugated stands seemed to exist, right down to the sleepy London commuter trains chugging past the open corners.

Alex Neil’s evolving team produced a first half of sustained and artful intensity to take a 2-0 lead. West Ham reminded everyone why they were relegated last season by forgetting to turn up, before dominating the second half and scoring twice.

There was even a moment of late drama, controversy and, let’s face it, blatant cheating, as Kyrell Lisbie robbed Mohamadou Kanté then ran through on goal all alone, only to be pulled to the floor by the same opponent. It was an obvious but also essentially useless red card. Lisbie had a fair chance of scoring the winner. A free-kick outside the box was rich reward for an act of cynicism.

In the end a draw was a fair result in a game where football, of all things, was the winner. Half an hour before kick-off the Den was already crackling with a rare kind of energy. But then this is an authentic derby, a game with context and hinterland, albeit that original source of tension hasn’t existed since the docks were abandoned and then rebuilt.

Quick Guide Championship roundup: Swansea go top as Boro save point Show Swansea moved to the top of the table after Stephen Eustaquio’s first goal for the club earned a 2-1 victory at Lincoln. The Swans turned the game on its head after half-time and, barring a big win for West Brom over Wolves on Sunday, Vítor Matos’s (pictured) side will head into the international break top of the pile. Middlesbrough needed a late equaliser from Adilson Malanda to salvage a point and a 2-2 draw at Birmingham. The defender was on hand to punish Birmingham goalkeeper James Beadle’s handling error when the home side seemingly had the game won after coming from a goal down. Burnley were denied a first league victory since February as Mohammed Fuseini’s dramatic stoppage-time equaliser earned Derby a 1-1 draw at Turf Moor. Zeki Amdouni’s 34th-minute far-post header looked to have given Burnley a much-needed victory to ease the pressure on their new head coach Nicky Hayen, but Fuseini’s equaliser leaves Burnley winless and bottom of the table. Paul Smyth scored a 90th-minute equaliser for 10-man QPR as they came back from two goals down to draw 2-2 with struggling Preston. Johnny Kenny’s first goals for North End – including an opener after 64 seconds – left them in a great position, but Kwame Poku pulled a goal back and Smyth’s late strike rescued a point for the west London side. Stoke staged a fine comeback to stun Sheffield United with a 2-1 win at the Bet365 Stadium despite Kalvin Phillips's first league goal for five and a half years. Two goals in the space of 11 second-half minutes from Jack McGlynn and Sam Gallagher enabled the home side to make it four wins in their past five league fixtures. Wrexham secured a smash-and-grab 2-1 victory against wasteful Southampton courtesy of Keven Schlotterbeck’s late own goal. Phil Parkinson’s men headed into the game reeling from a 6-0 hammering at West Ham and desperate to kickstart their campaign, and they edged a late win as Schlotterbeck turned in Jacques Ekomie’s cross. Cardiff’s long wait for a first win on their Championship return is over after Jack Moylan scored twice in their 3-1 home victory over Charlton, while Colby Bishop struck his first goal since April to give Portsmouth a 2-2 draw with Blackburn at Fratton Park. Press Association Photograph: Greig Cowie/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The deep history is real: a battle for work on the docks, a river in between, a club that moved from your actual back yard (the mill wall in question is just over the Thames). Even if these days it’s more a matter of muscle memory, familial tradition, internet blather. Even the docks are quays now. Although there are some really good artisan coffee shops around the place if you look.

Otherwise this was also a self-contained media event. When the West Ham bus arrived at 11.30am it felt like there were more influencers with collar mics, more rubbernecking reporters than actual enraged docker-descendants. Disappointingly for some, perhaps, the only real threat of violence around the ground all day was the danger of an accidental mass entangling from the endless Stone Island shoulder badges on show.

West Ham were always favourites to win here. Their most recent annual turnover was £226m. Millwall are on a tenth of that. Chronic mismanagement gave us this game. Boardroom incompetence made it happen. And playing squads aside, Millwall were hugely focused from the first thunderously claimed loose ball.

View image in fullscreen Camiel Neghli doubles Millwall’s lead from close range in first-half stoppage time. Photograph: Tom Cusden/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Neil has introduced a more fluid passing game in the last year, but this was all about energy and tempo. Early on Zak Sturge left Jarrod Bowen on the floor to vast approving roars, then slid a pass to Taïryk Arconte, who couldn’t get his shot away.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

And with 16 minutes gone Millwall took the lead with a goal that came in stages. First Mads Hermansen made a brilliant one-handed save from Mark Sykes, then another one, leaping up, from Arconte. The ball looped across the six-yard box to Caleb Taylor, who half-volleyed it elegantly into the net.

The Den erupted with a noise so visceral the Lewisham council incinerator at the Cold Blow Lane end (it is, Millwall fans will tell you, a world-class incinerator) must have shivered on its foundations. And they kept on coming. Arconte made and then spurned another good opportunity. Jenson Metcalfe spanked a loose ball from 35 yards that dipped and swerved and pinged back off the crossbar. And in first-half added time it was 2-0, again from a long throw from the right. This time the ball fell to Camiel Neghli, who took a nice touch from under his feet and smashed it into the net.

Quick Guide Leagues One and Two: Russell Martin booed after Leicester draw Show Ten-man Barnsley came from a goal down to rescue a point from a 1-1 League One draw with Leicester, who struggled to break down the hosts despite having a man advantage for more than an hour. Liam Cullen opened the scoring for Leicester, but Reyes Cleary earned a point for the home side, who had Luca Connell sent off in the first half. The 4,300 Leicester fans booed the players and the manager, Russell Martin, at full time. They now have nine points from seven games after relegation. Mansfield came from two goals down to grab a point from a 2-2 draw with Burton. Burton were two goals to the good through Deji Oshilaja’s own goal and Jack Armer’s second of the season, but the Stags responded with Michael Smith’s goal before half-time and Lucas Akins netting against his former club. In League Two, Rochdale lifted themselves off the bottom with a 2-0 win against Oldham. The home side took the lead seven minutes in. Charlie Tasker and Jonny Smith combined down the right, and Tasker’s low delivery in behind the retreating defence was swept into the roof of the net by Dan Moss. Dale delivered a sucker punch when they doubled the lead on 62 minutes. Matt Hudson’s kick towards the halfway line was met by Baba Adeeko, who headed the ball forward for Dajaune Brown to advance into the penalty area, sidestep Donervon Daniels and slam a firm drive into the bottom corner. Walsall scored late in each half to edge past struggling Port Vale 2-0 and heap pressure on the visiting manager, Jon Brady. Vale fans called for Brady’s sacking and booed off their players after Andrew Dallas’s first goal for Walsall sealed victory in the 89th minute, adding to James Connolly’s deft flick in first-half stoppage time. Press Association Photograph: James Holyoak/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Pablo and Kanté came on at half-time and West Ham began to turn the screw. Bowen drew a fine save from Filip Marschall. Arne Engels spanked a shot hard into the head of Jake Cooper, who staggered once, remembered where he was, then just walked it off.

On 74 minutes West Ham pulled one back via Kanté’s powerful low drive. They were hunting this now. Bowen seemed to be running every element of the game. A series of corners were bundled away, until finally Konstantinos Mavropanos headed the equaliser.

Millwall held on until the red card, then West Ham held on to the end. At the final whistle there was even some minor chest-bumping stuff between Bowen and Mathis Servais, traditions preserved, the family line respected, followed by a chorus of “you’ll run out of Bermondsey” from the Millwall fans. It will be more a case of regional trains these days, back to the places beyond the riverside high-rises. But this was a wonderful game, and a fitting tribute to the enduring power of all that.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola makes Bournemouth return still learning on the job at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Alisson made little attempt to sugarcoat Liverpool’s unbeaten start to the season under Andoni Iraola when analysing the draw against Fulham with the club’s in-house media. “Unbeaten with three draws is not something to celebrate too much with this shirt,” said a peeved Liverpool goalkeeper. “We take the clean sheet but we are not happy at all. We need to aim for big things.”

Big things are the target and big things are expected from a Liverpool side containing three £100m-plus forwards. But the learning curve under the new head coach is proving challenging. As it is for the new head coach, too. Big decisions appear unavoidable.

When Iraola faces his former club Bournemouth on Sunday for the first time since ending his impressive three-year reign there last season, he is likely to know more about the opposition players than his own. “It’s going to be a tricky one because they know very well what we try to do,” Iraola said. “But I also know their strengths and weaknesses. It’s going to be strange for me.”

Iraola spent more than two hours debriefing Marco Rose, his successor at the Vitality Stadium, on the Bournemouth squad and staff in June. They had time for a smooth handover because, as Iraola put it, his exit from the club “was so clean” and he decided to stay on the south coast while his two young children finished school. Whether they discussed how Bournemouth became the draw specialists of last season remains private.

No coach or manager oversaw more stalemates in the Premier League last season than Iraola, whose Bournemouth team were held a remarkable 18 times. It was a league high by a comfortable distance. Leeds in second had 14. Ten came at the Vitality, 52.63% of their home league fixtures, and Bournemouth ultimately missed out on the fifth and final Champions League spot by three points from a Liverpool team that stumbled over the line under Arne Slot.

Over the course of his last 38 league games, Iraola has drawn 21 times. That is a joint record in the Premier League alongside Mark Hughes, whose identical run across 38 games came with Manchester City and Fulham between October 2009 and February 2011. Hughes had a seven-month break between those two jobs, however, making Iraola the first Premier League coach to draw 21 of 38 matches in a continuous sequence.

The sample size at Liverpool is too small for conclusions, admittedly. Iraola is also still searching for balance and assessing his options, as changes in both full-back positions and central midfield have demonstrated regularly. But the 44-year-old knows full well that a draw with Liverpool is far more damaging to his current employer’s aspirations than his previous one. Three from four league games so far have enabled Arsenal and Manchester City to quickly establish an ominous six-point gap over the 2025 champions. The audible groans that greeted the home draws against Nottingham Forest and Fulham confirmed Anfield’s patience has not recovered from last season’s travails.

“That’s totally fair,” Iraola said of the contrasting reactions to a draw at Liverpool and Bournemouth. “But it’s something that I knew before coming here. When you draw 2-2 at Newcastle with Bournemouth it is probably a good result, but I understand that with Liverpool it is not a good result. The goals of the team are different and the expectations are different as well.”

Fulham was a step backwards, according to Iraola, after two steps forward against Ipswich and Atlético Madrid. A younger, fresher Liverpool team restored momentum with Tuesday’s Carabao Cup win over Tottenham. Elements of that performance were as timely for Iraola as the result. Having demanded greater effort from his forward line following the Fulham draw – and then rested Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz against Spurs – youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell, Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni all made tireless contributions to the cup win in their absences.

View image in fullscreen Rio Ngumoha, in action against Atlético Madrid, has has shown his quality as one of Liverpool’s rising stars. Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Academy players appeared more attuned to Iraola’s methods and instructions than their expensive elders. With Liverpool’s midfield balance also under scrutiny and Wirtz following a good Champions League performance with an indifferent Premier League display, as was often the case last season, Iraola may spend the extended international break wrestling with some big calls depending on how his Bournemouth return unfolds. He has shown himself unafraid of making them.

“For me the demands on the players and positions are the same,” Iraola insisted on Friday. “I don’t give different instructions to one player because he is more expensive than another player who has cost us less money. The demands are always the same. But I also have to adjust to the things that some players can do and others cannot do.

“The strengths and weaknesses of players are different, so we have to always adapt the team to try and maximise the collective side of this. In Bournemouth we had players who could run forever and other players who could not do it. It was not like everyone in Bournemouth was running. Some of them were faster, others were slower, some of them scored more goals, some are good at set pieces. There is no standard player. I feel all the players here are doing everything to try to win and to try and get where we want as quickly as possible. But sometimes I need to adapt too to the players that we have.”

Iraola was asked if he would love 11 players with the mentality of Koumas. “That is a cheating question,” he said, laughing. “I love the desire of Koumas, I love what he gives, but every player has different weaknesses and strengths. He is a good example especially for the players coming from the academy, he is grabbing his opportunity and doing everything to try to gain minutes. But I also have to work with Koumas a lot in other areas. There are things he has to improve.”

Everyone at Liverpool, it seems, is learning on a job that demands the finished article.

Sports.title: Harry Kane smashes record for fastest to 100 Bundesliga goals in 98th game
Sports.content:
Harry Kane broke the 49-year-old record for the fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals in Bayern Munich’s 7-0 victory on Friday over Union Berlin, his 98th league game for the club.

Cologne’s Dieter Müller set the previous mark in 1977, but it took him 129 matches and with the England captain scoring at better than a goal a game Kane setting the record had been inevitable for some time. Since his arrival, in 2023, Kane has scored 152 goals in 154 appearances in all competitions, including 61 in 51 games last season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

He blasted home a 39th-minute penalty to take the record before nodding in a Michael Olise cross early in the second half to send Bayern top of the table before the other weekend matches.

The feat stole the spotlight from Olise, who scored his first Bayern hat-trick, and Jamal Musiala, who scored a goal worthy of winning any game.

“I’m very proud to have now scored 100 and 101 Bundesliga goals. I haven’t been around that long. I’ve loved every second of it,” Kane told Sky Germany. “With Michael, Lucho [Luis Díaz] and Jamal I naturally get chances and today was no exception.

“So I just want to thank the team, the club, the coach, and the staff – everyone who has helped me achieve this. Let’s keep going like this. I can only say that I’m enjoying every minute of it. Just like today.”

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi brands Tottenham the most fragile team he’s coached in 14 years
Sports.content:
"In my 14 years as a coach, I've never seen a team like us."

Roberto De Zerbi has been left in disbelief at how 'fragile' his Tottenham side is after their misery continued on Saturday.

3 De Zerbi watched on as his Spurs side were beaten yet again at home on Saturday Credit: AFP

Spurs were beaten 3-2 by Aston Villa to drop into the Premier League relegation zone on an embarrassing afternoon.

De Zerbi's side looked to be heading for a 3-0 loss, which would have seen them go five games without scoring a single goal after seeing Mohammed Kudus' tap-in ruled out by VAR.

But late strikes from Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke made the result look a lot more respectable on paper.

In reality though, it was another very rough day for Tottenham, who spent over £300million on transfers over the summer - and their manager seems as confused as their fans.

What has De Zerbi said about Tottenham's defeat to Aston Villa?

Speaking post-match, De Zerbi admitted that he is baffled by his own players following their third loss of the season.

"It's a mental aspect for sure, but they have the right mentality," the Italian told talkSPORT. "They work very well, they are good players.

"It's difficult to explain because, in my career, 14 years as a coach, I've never seen one team like us. So fragile, so inconsistent.

"You're good, or you're bad. You can't be very good in the first 30, 40 minutes, and then concede like this in this way.

"It's tough to accept for me."

De Zerbi has managed nine clubs in his 14 years on the touchline, but he is facing the toughest challenge of his career at Spurs.

3 Spurs' boss has been left in disbelief at how his side continue to disappoint Credit: Getty

What else did De Zerbi say?

The Tottenham manager was also asked if he could explain the 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon.

To which he admitted: "Listen, I'm a coach, but I do not have all the answers...for your question, I have no answer.

"I can say what I think, what I've seen today and I saw my team in the first half play very well, we had chances to score.

"We didn't score and then we conceded the first goal...we have to stay closer and stay stronger, more compact.

"In the second half, after Kudus' goal, I don't know if the players lost energy...now we have to explain another defeat."

De Zerbi added: "Maybe the communication between the players [is the problem], maybe the leaders have to be stronger.

3 De Zerbi has been unable to explain how his squad aren't able to put together a good performance Credit: Getty

"We need leaders to drive and lead the team...I don't know, I want to speak with the players when I stay with them.

"With Newcastle it was the same, in Liverpool it was the same, with Everton it was the same...we have to find the solutions."

Spurs have played 14 games in total under De Zerbi, winning on just four occasions and losing six in all competitions.

His points-per-game average in North London is 1.14, which is his lowest since 2018 when he was Benevento boss.

Across all of his matches at Tottenham, his side have conceded 19 goals and only managed to score 16.

This season, their two goals in the loss to Aston Villa are their only goals in the Premier League after five games, of which they have failed to win one - losing three and drawing two.

Sports.title: Ex-England manager returns to Sheffield Wednesday after 38 years in special role
Sports.content:
Ex-England manager returns to Sheffield Wednesday after 38 years in special role

Howard Wilkinson has been given a unique new role at Sheffield Wednesday.

The ex-England caretaker boss has been named among three new Lifetime Presidents at the League One club.

3 Howard Wilkinson (right) has been rewarded by boyhood club Sheffield Wednesday Credit: PA

Wilkinson joined Lord David Blunkett and Clive Betts in the new role and fans immediately gave their seal of approval to the decision.

Sheffield Wednesday announced the news before their fixture against Stockport on Saturday giving fans a reason to celebrate a key figure in the club’s history.

Wilkinson enjoyed a successful stint in charge of the Owls before later taking over at Leeds United in 1988.

His greatest club achievement came in 1992 when he guided Leeds to the First Division title.

The feat makes Wilkinson the last English manager to win the top flight.

It was there that Wilkinson made the decision to sell Eric Cantona to Alex Ferguson's Manchester United for £1.2m.

The forward went on to fire the Red Devils to four Premier League titles in five seasons.

Wilkinson was an FA figurehead

Wilkinson later became the FA’s Technical Director and played a crucial role in the planning and opening of England’s national Football Centre.

He also enjoyed multiple spells as England caretaker boss.

His first stint came in 1999, following Glenn Hoddle’s departure, taking charge of a friendly against France.

3 The title-winning manager played a leading role at the FA Credit: Shutterstock

3 Wilkinson enjoyed to short spells at England caretaker boss Credit: Getty

A year later, he returned after Kevin Keegan quit the post and oversaw a goalless draw against Finland.

He also had a spell in charge of England Under-21s before resigning in June 2001.

But his affiliation with Sheffield Wednesday was arguably his strongest connection across his long career in football.

The club said the new honorary positions recognise their 'significant contributions' to Wednesday, the local community and the wider city of Sheffield.

The appointments are doing much to improve the atmosphere around the club following a tumultuous period in the club’s history under the guidance of former owner Dejphon Chansiri.

Owls fans hold Wilkinson in high regard for his past achievements with the club.

Sports.title: National League manager quits in post-match interview after nine matches in charge
Sports.content:
National League manager quits in post-match interview after nine matches in charge

Lee Clark stepped down from his role as Hartlepool boss moments after their 3-1 defeat to Worthing.

The National League side confirmed the 53-year-old's exit to bring an end his four-month stay at Victoria Park.

2 Hartlepool are already on the hunt for a new boss despite appointing Clark in the summer Credit: Getty

Clark only took charge of the fifth-tier outfit in May, but he endured a nightmare time in the North East.

Hartlepool have won just three of their opening nine league matches, while they have lost on six occasions.

Five of those losses have come from their last six fixtures in the division.

They have also been defeated in their opening two games in the National League Cup.

And Saturday's home loss to Worthing has proven to be the final straw for Clark.

What did Lee Clark say in his post-match press confernece?

Clark, who featured for Newcastle and Fulham in the Premier League, made the announcement in his post-match presser after fans serenaded him with a brutal chant of, 'You're getting sacked in the morning'.

He said: "There was no reaction to the result [2-1 defeat to Altrincham midweek] or the performance, all I want to say is I resign from my position with immediate effect.

"I wanted to give this club and the fans something to be proud of, what they deserve, I haven’t been able to do that unfortunately.

"I know what this club means, I said it at the start when I got the job, I was excited to take it and I wanted to be the man that got them back where they need to be and deserve to be.

"It hasn’t worked out, you’ve heard the reaction of the supporters, I took a long time out of the game and I wasn’t going to be coming back and getting an atmosphere like that.

2 Hartlepool are competing in their fourth consecutive season in the National League Credit: Getty

"It’s not going to change and it’s not nice for the family and friends to listen to that."

Clark added: "I wish whoever takes the job on success, I wish the fans all of the best, they’re a magnificent group of people.

"The people in behind the scenes, my staff, the people in the offices, they’re absolutely brilliant and the support I’ve had from the chairman, the owner, Chris Maxwell, it’s been fantastic.

"But you have to understand in this game, I’m nearly 54, you have to understand when things aren’t going your way.”

What did Hartlepool say in their statement?

Issuing a brief statement, Hartlepool said: "Hartlepool United Football Club can confirm that Lee Clark has resigned from his position as Head Coach with immediate effect.

"We would like to thank Lee for his service during his time at the club and wish him every success for the future. A further update will be provided in due course."

Hartlepool have a week to bring in an interim before they battle Scunthorpe on the road, with a clash against Harrogate Town coming three days after.

Sports.title: Lee Grant in contention for new EFL job as 50-man list whittled down
Sports.content:
Lee Grant in contention for new EFL job as 50-man list whittled down

Walsall manager Lee Grant is a contender to replace Paul Heckingbottom as Preston manager, talkSPORT understands.

Grant is part of a whittled-down shortlist that initially included 50 different potential successors at Deepdale.



2 Walsall manager Grant is on the shortlist to become Preston's new boss Credit: Richard Hammersley

Heckingbottom was dismissed last week just six games into the Championship season, with his side winning just one.

Premier League cult hero Jason Euell has taken interim charge, but Preston have been on the lookout for a new boss.

And it appears Grant is a strong candidate to take over.

Ex-Manchester United goalkeeper Grant only took his second managerial job in May when he was named Walsall manager.



He has taken charge of eight games so far with the Saddlers, going unbeaten in League Two so far this season.

Before joining Walsall, the 43-year-old spent eight months in charge of Huddersfield Town, being sacked in January of this year.



Of his 36 games in the dugout for the Terriers, he won 17.

Who else is a contender to take over?

Grant is on the shortlist for Preston and is in contention, but who else is a candidate to take over at Preston?

talkSPORT understands that Robbie Keane, who left Hungarian side Ferencvaros in May, is appreciated by the club.



Meanwhile, Bradford City manager Graham Alexander is understood to be open to the role.

2 Euell was placed in interim charge after Heckingbottom was dismissed last week Credit: Getty

Other free agents in the manager market include Scott Parker, Sean Dyche and Steven Gerrard.

However, the three former Premier League bosses are not in contention to replace Heckingbottom.



Could Euell get the job full-time?

On top of those options, Euell may end up fancying the job...

In his first game in charge of Preston away at Queens Park Rangers, the Lilywhites took the lead after just 20 seconds.

Johnny Kenny netted in the opening minutes before going on to score a second after 26 minutes.

It meant that Euell's side headed into half time 2-0 up, with QPR also going down to 10 men.

However, Preston eventually ended up losing their advantage and drawing 2-2 to continue their poor form.

Sports.title: Fans left baffled by new 20,000-seater Red Bull stadium which ‘looks like a call centre’
Sports.content:
Fans left baffled by new 20,000-seater Red Bull stadium which ‘looks like a call centre’

Brazilian club Red Bull Bragantino have released images of their new 20,000-capacity stadium.

The ground is currently under construction on the site of their old home.



3 Red Bull Bragantino's new stadium has been compared to a 'call centre' by fans Credit: Photo: Illustration / Red Bull Bragantino

However, fans have been left confused by the design of the venue, which will host top-flight football.

Bragantino currently compete in the Brazilian Serie A, where they sit ninth in the table after 26 matches.

They ended up finishing in tenth spot last term - despite spending half of the season away from their home ground.



What does Red Bull Bragantino's new stadium look like?

The club played their final match at the Estadio Nabi Abi Chedid in April before it was demolished to make way for the new arena.

First opened in 1949, their old home had a capacity of 17,000 supporters.



That figure will be raised by 3,000 at the new stadium, which is set to feature lounges, restaurants and bars.

It will also be a multi-purpose venue capable of hosting other sports and events once completed.



The rectangular design of the arena has baffled fans, though, with the box-like exterior also featuring a raised silver roof across all four stands.

Reacting to the design on social media, one supporter wrote: "I can't decide if I love it or if it looks like a call centre."

Another added: "Looks like a cardboard IKEA box."

3 The Brazilian club are currently building a new 20,000-capacity stadium Credit: Photo: Illustration / Red Bull Bragantino

Meanwhile, a third fan simply commented: "Looks soulless."

During the stadium's construction, Bragantino are playing at the Estadio Cicero de Souza Marques.



The 12,000-capacity ground was purpose built to host their matches whilst their usual home is being rebuilt.

Who are Red Bull Bragantino?

Originally founded in 1928, Bragantino have been owned by Red Bull for the last five years.

Following their takeover, the group changed the club's name from Clube Atletico Bragantino as well as altering their colours.

The club is now one of seven clubs to form Red Bull's football network.



3 Bragantino's new ground will be built on the same site as their old home ground Credit: Photo: Illustration / Red Bull Bragantino

Red Bull Salzburg, New York Red Bulls, RB Leipzig and Japanese side RB Omiya Ardija are all fully controlled by the group.

Meanwhile, they own 10 per cent and 15 per cent stakes in Leeds United and Paris FC, respectively.

Sports.title: Stuart Pearce visibly shocked by performance from big-money Tottenham player
Sports.content:
Stuart Pearce questioned Jan Paul van Hecke's price tag in a damning assessment during Tottenham's defeat to Aston Villa.

The £52million summer signing got on the scoresheet but endured a tough afternoon otherwise, as Spurs' woes continued with a 3-2 defeat at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.



4 Jan Paul van Hecke cut a lonely figure as Spurs were beaten again at home Credit: Getty

Goals from Johan Manzambi, Jackson and Emi Buendia put Villa 3-0 up and in cruise control, before Conor Gallagher and a last-gasp header from Van Hecke gave the hosts some credibility.

This sealed Villa's first win of the season, while Roberto De Zerbi's side remain winless after their first five Premier League games.

Despite a lively start which saw Spurs force saves from Zion Suzuki, Manzambi gave the visitors the lead on the stroke of half time as four goals followed in the second half.



'What is Van Hecke doing?'

Villa became increasingly dominant in the second period, as club-record signing Jackson began to run riot against the Spurs' backline, and Van Hecke in particular.

In the 55th minute, the Senegalese picked the ball up out wide by the halfway line and breezed past the Dutchman, before driving towards goal and seeing his 20-yard effort fly just over the bar.



This left talkSPORT commentator Sam Matterface unimpressed, who reacted: “What is Van Hecke doing? He sold himself completely.”

Co-commentator Pearce was in agreement, immediately questioning Van Hecke's big-money summer move from Brighton.



He replied: “He certainly did. Was that £52million worth of central defending?"

With Pearce clearly shocked by Van Hecke's struggles against Jackson, Matterface replied: "Honestly, I wish everybody could see the look on your face."

The England great came back: “Honestly, when he moved for the summer money that he did it raised an eyebrow or two in my head.

4 Nicolas Jackson was a constant threat up against Tottenham's back line Credit: Getty



4 Van Hecke and Micky van de Ven were undone by Jackson for Villa's second goal Credit: Getty

"And his performance today has done exactly that again.”

Pearce's damning verdict was proven right minutes later, as Jackson once again got the better of Van Hecke to score Villa's second.

The striker outmuscled the defender to lay Suzuki's long ball off to Manzambi, before getting the ball back and flicking it past Micky van de Ven and volleying a stunning effort past Antonin Kinsky in goal.

This put Villa in firm control as Spurs despaired, and Van Hecke soon found himself on the end of criticism from talkSPORT's Jamie O'Hara.



Taking to X, the ex-Tottenham man and Sports Bar host tweeted: “Van Hecke looks like he’s playing in cement.”

Things then went from bad to worse Spurs as Buendia fired in a 25-yard stunner to make it 3-0, only for the home side to finally score their first league goal of the season when Gallagher prodded home in the 86th minute.

4 Despite a tough afternoon, Van Hecke opened his Spurs account with a late goal Credit: Getty

Despite a challenging afternoon, Van Hecke managed to leave with some credibility when he headed home Andy Roberton's free-kick to open his Spurs account.



But the scoreline flattered Spurs, and questions will continue to be asked over manager De Zerbi, whose side continue to struggle despite a summer overhaul over more than £300m which includes Van Hecke.

Sports.title: West Ham player accused of spitting at Millwall goalkeeper in first clash for 14 years
Sports.content:
West Ham player accused of spitting at Millwall goalkeeper in first clash for 14 years

Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall accused West Ham player Taty Castellanos of spitting during the 2-2 draw on Saturday.

There was confusion in the second-half of the Dockers Derby as the Lions shot-stopper appeared to hold onto the ball for too long.

4 Castellanos found himself at the centre of a row during the lunchtime clash Credit: Getty

Thinking the Hammers had a corner, Castellanos took it quickly and created a goal, before it was ruled out and Millwall given an uncontested drop-ball by referee Paul Tierney.

Moments later, a replay showed Marschall wiping his head and suggesting he had been spat at by Castellanos.

Sky Sports later confirmed the accusation after conversations with the Millwall bench and the fourth official, moments before West Ham completed a comeback from two-goals down and drew level.

Fiery atmosphere

The high-profile London rivalry was reignited for the first-time in 14 years on Saturday.

A fierce atmosphere erupted from the moment it kicked off - with Millwall’s opening goal met with a deafening explosion of noise.

The Den rose to its feet when Caleb Taylor fired the Lions ahead in the 16th minute of the much-anticipated dockers derby.

It was all one-way traffic in the early exchanges and Millwall deservedly broke the deadlock thanks to Taylor’s close-range finish in front of the travelling away support.

The decibel levels were ramped up compared to usual as Taylor was mobbed by his teammates in the celebrations that followed.

And the noise was felt in the press area at The Den with talkSPORT reporter James Fielden left stunned by what he had experienced.

“The Dockers Derby has just absolutely exploded,” Fielden belted out on air. “The Hammers can’t say it hadn’t been coming.

4 Caleb Taylor's opener saw The Den explode into a cauldron of noise Credit: Getty

“Caleb Taylor with the goal as he scrambled it in from close range.

“I haven't seen celebrations like that inside a stadium for a long, long time.”

The Lions continued their dominance as the half drew on and rewarded themselves with a two-goal cushion.

Just moments after Mark Sykes’ thunderous effort from range came crashing off the crossbar, Camiel Neghli fired home from five yards out, leaving the Hammers with a mountain to climb in the second half.

However, the visitors scored twice in quick succession to draw level through Mohamadou Kante and Konstantinos Mavrpanos.

West Ham were reduced to ten men late on when goalscorer Kante was shown a straight red card for a professional foul, but still held on to salvage a point from their historic rivals.

4 Alex Neil has confirmed the spitting allegations from his goalkeeper Credit: Getty

In his post-match interview, Millwall boss Neil confirmed Marschall’s spitting allegation but admitted he was too far away from the incident to see it.

“Phil was telling the referee when it happened but I was so far away to see what had happened," Neil told Sky Sports.

“But I would presume that Phil wouldn’t say that without cause. I’m sure the referee and the authorities will look at it and if it warrants that it needs dealing with and looking at, then I’m sure they will.”

'The best I've ever played in'

Taylor, scorer of Millwall's opener, admits he was left stunned by the atmosphere created at at The Den.

“I can’t lie, it’s one of the best atmosphere’s I’ve ever played in. It was incredible. I got shivers walking out," he told ITV.

“We showed so much today but there’s disappointment because that’s two weeks in a row we’ve been 2-0 up at half time and now got the result we wanted."

4 Millwall fans were in full voice during the first half of their match against West Ham Credit: Getty

Asked if he was surprised at West Ham’s second-half resurgence, Taylor said: “ No, I’m not surprised. We battered them in the first half, we were so on the front foot and they couldn’t deal with it.

“I think that’s one of the best halves we’ve had and we deserved the 2-0 lead. But we knew at half time they were going to change and they are a good team.

“They came out, changed shape and made it difficult for us.”

Sports.title: Arsenal open to Max Dowman loan in January after EFL request
Sports.content:
Arsenal could allow Max Dowman to leave the club on loan, but only if it supports his development.

The 16-year-old impressed in the midweek Carabao Cup win at Ipswich, scoring twice in a 4-2 win for Mikel Arteta’s side.



3 Max Dowman put in a superb performance in the midweek win at Ipswich Credit: Getty

Dowman became the youngest player to score in Premier League history last season when he opened his account for the Gunners against Everton.

The teen prodigy was left out of the squad for last weekend’s win at Sunderland with competition for places as fierce as ever at the club.

Earlier this week, Luton Town scout Mick Harford told talkSPORT that the League One club had enquired about taking Dowman on loan ‘a couple of times’ but their advances were rebuffed by Arteta.



Luton are managed by ex-Arsenal star and former Gunners Under-18 head coach Jack Wilshere who has kept a close eye on the star’s development.

But it now appears that Arteta is open to the idea of a loan with the club set to regularly evaluate the player’s needs.



The Dowman plan

"We will evaluate every six months where we are and what is the best thing for him to do and then make the right decision," Arteta said.

"It depends on a lot of factors. What he needs, and what the team needs as well, the availability we have in the squad, the minutes that he is playing and the qualities of those minutes.



"We have to be open, but now the focus is to be here and to impact the team."

Dowman is unable to complete any loan move until he turns 17 on New Year’s Eve.

That falls just one day before the winter transfer window opens and that could see Wilshere try his luck once more.

3 Arteta will play a key role in where Dowman goes if he does leave on loan Credit: Getty



"We haven't really listened to any of the possibilities because we were crystal clear that we wanted to have Max in the squad, that we wanted him to be part of the pre-season and then start to see where we are from there," Arteta added.

Dowman made 13 appearances for Arsenal last season, picking up a Premier League title medal.

And with such promise shown at a young age, Arteta took a high-protective approach over the academy graduate.

A cautious approach

"There have been many cases of that age when they have gone out and been successful and others not," Arteta added.



"In my particular case, I was 17 when I went to Paris [Saint-Germain]. It depends on the atmosphere that you find there, and how much the coach believes in you as to whether you go there just to be part of a squad or play minutes.

"Which country, it depends. But now he is in a good place, let's keep him here."

3 Ex-Arsenal player and coach jack Wilshere may try again in January to bring Dowman to Luton Credit: Getty

Dowman’s heroics at Portman Road would have done his hopes of breaking into the starting XI no harm.



His superb two-goal haul has certainly provided Arteta with some food for thought over the coming months.

"The best way to knock on the door is to do it on the pitch, not in the office," Arteta said when asked whether Dowman could feature against Brighton this weekend.

"Then you just leave out the arguments. When a player delivers constantly on the pitch, every single day in training, that's the best way, that's the best signal for the manager. That's the best signal for his team-mates, too.

"And what Max did the other day, alongside all the other players as well that haven't played many minutes this season, was really impressive."

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi TEARS into Spurs flops after defeat by Aston Villa and sends warning to struggling stars after £320m summer splurge
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi TEARS into Spurs flops after defeat by Aston Villa and sends warning to struggling stars after £320m summer splurge

Roberto De Zerbi let rip at his Tottenham flops after crashing to another home defeat which will leave them marooned in the drop zone for the next three weeks.

Spurs were 3-0 down in the 86th minute and Aston Villa had threatened to stretch further ahead before salvaging a little respectability with two late goals.

They are winless in the first five games of the Premier League season and De Zerbi did not try to hide his emotions.

He hit out at his team’s defensive ‘fragility’ and the feeble manner of Villa’s goals, especially the ‘unacceptable’ second, scored on the break by Nicolas Jackson at the start of the second half.

He demanded more strength in adversity and more from certain individuals including Dominic Solanke and Mateus Fernandes, who was replaced at half time.

He also grumbled about the problems in the transfer window.

Roberto De Zerbi hit out at his team’s defensive ‘fragility’ and the feeble manner of Villa’s goals

'I was very disappointed, very sad, very frustrated for the performance,' fumed De Zerbi. 'We can’t lose this game in this way, absolutely. We can’t concede the second goal. We can’t lose balance. In the beginning of the second half I spoke with the four attackers, to use their heads, be calm.

'It was minute 51. All the second half, be calm, play, enjoy, don’t take risks. But the goal we conceded, the second goal was incredible.'

De Zerbi was no happier about the opener, scored by Johan Manzambi when Spurs were down to 10 men because Micky van de Ven was off having treatment on a facial cut after a clash of heads with Tyrone Mings.

'I don’t want to speak about the first half when we dominated and created more chances to score,' said De Zerbi. 'My focus is on why we concede the first goal with 10 players, just for one minute in that situation.

'We can stay stronger, we can communicate more, we can defend in a compact way. I put [Rodrigo] Bentancur to centre back and Mateus Fernandes into midfield. If we have a red card we could play for 60 minutes with 10 players, so what is the problem?'

Spurs thought sub Kudus had levelled at 1-1 but the goal was ruled out by a VAR offside call and soon afterwards were 2-0 down.

'I don’t know if some players lost energy, but we conceded an unacceptable goal from a long goal kick, with a long ball,' said De Zerbi. 'We knew Aston Villa are playing 86 per cent more long balls than last season. We spoke about it in many meetings.

Spurs were 3-0 down in the 86th minute and Aston Villa had threatened to stretch further ahead before salvaging a little respectability with two late goals

'Then we have to explain another game like Newcastle, where we play well in the first half and then lose. For sure it’s an aspect.

'It’s my responsibility, I don’t want to leave without taking my responsibility, but in that moment of the game, when the game is different to ball possession, to playing in the last third, because we can’t play for 90 minutes in the last third like the first half, because there is an opponent.

'Aston Villa is not such a bad team. It is a good team, good players and the moment we have to defend, we have to defend compact. The leaders have to be leaders and lead the team.'

'Football is like life, either you are stronger or you lose.'

De Zerbi vowed also to work harder and improve but accused his players of losing their way when things conspired against them.

'In the second half, we lost balance because we were losing,' said the Spurs boss. 'We forced the pass, forced the situation, lost the ball.'

De Zerbi dropped Mathys Tel for what he called ‘technical reasons’, and demanded more from individuals including £85million summer signing Fernandes and Solanke.

On Fernandes, he said: 'I have a big confidence in Mateus, but I didn’t like his performance. Otherwise, I wouldn't change. He knows, but it’s normal, it’s not an attack on Mateus, I love Mateus, but we need more from Mateus.'

On Solanke, he said: 'We need more from him, for sure. I like Dom as a player, and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough.

'Maybe he doesn’t have enough confidence in himself in this moment, because he’s much better than this. But maybe many things can be better. We can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.'

On summer transfers and the failure to land a reliable goalscorer, De Zerbi said: 'The transfer market was long, and the situation changed many times. There was also the Financial Fair Play to respect at the end of the transfer market.

'We didn’t sell the players we thought, in the beginning, there was the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. The club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.'

Spurs will return after the international break with a trip to Manchester United.

Sports.title: Timid Arsenal were BULLIED by Brighton in 3-0 defeat: This performance from Mikel Arteta's men beggared belief and proves it is far too early to write off title challengers yet, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
Timid and shell-shocked. Bullied, even. Rarely have such negative words been attributed to Arsenal in recent times. Even those with a particular liking to Mikel Arteta’s team would struggle to utter more positive terms. By full-time, the Seagulls had pecked holes through each Arsenal player, and Arteta’s tactical sheets. The score ended 3-0. Though, on another afternoon, four or five nil would have been more fitting. Even the typically composed Declan Rice decided to boot Malick Yalcouye in frustration seconds before the full-time whistle, somehow escaping a red card. This was a Gunners display synonymous with their side from four or five years ago, when the Spaniard had started paving the building blocks towards a Premier League title competing side. What transpired here on the south coast defied belief. All teams can have an off day. No side is truly unbeatable in this league, even if the hype around Arsenal had reached silly levels because of the sheer frailties of the other Big Six members. Yet, the manner in which Fabian Hurzeler’s relentless Brighton team had run straight through the visitors sent a warning to the league. This season’s champions is not a foregone conclusion. Far from it. Mikel Arteta's Arsenal side were bullied by Brighton as they lost 3-0 on Saturday afternoon Right from the start, Arsenal were completely at sea. David Raya’s passes were laced with panic, many reaching his team-mates with too much power; a few even breached the touchline. That is a rare sight indeed. The backline looked nervy. The midfield were being cut through at will. The frontline were hidden. Pascal Gross, one of Brighton’s many in-form players, had struck on 31 minutes to set the rout off. He received the ball outside the area, Arsenal’s backline dropping off, as if to say, ‘Go on, try, your luck’. He did just that, lashing the ball with pace towards goal, rebounding off the bottom-right post and into the net. Riccardo Calafiori was the main culprit. He should’ve stepped forward to challenge. Still, it was an excellent strike befitting a man in red-hot form. Gross now has seven goal contributions across all competitions this season. Diego Gomez’s strike before half-time followed a similar pattern, the backline dropping off. He passed to Charalampos Kostoulas, who swivelled outside the area and struck past Raya from 25 yards out. Another goal was to follow, courtesy of Chema Andres from a Gross corner kick. Yet by the end, the Brighton players were queuing for their turn to strike at goal like kids at a half-time football challenge. Substitute Matt O’Riley had his one-on-one shot saved by Raya on 89 minutes which Yalcouye latched on to hit the crossbar, for example. Brighton deserve enormous credit, a side which outfought, outthought and outran Arsenal. Not many sides in recent times can claim as such. It could have been more than three, too, with the champions suffering their first loss of the season Having warded off a clawing by the Black Cats, Arsenal had a pecking by the seagulls to overcome. The animosity around Hurzeler’s comments last season, where he criticised Arsenal’s style of play, may have been forgiven by Arteta though the German was in no mood for a friendly-natured fixture. The Premier League’s best attack v best defence, thus far, was the billing. Brighton started fiercely on the front foot. Diego Gomez stayed on Calafiori like a hare, refusing to give him an inch. Each time the ball arrived on the flank within the first ten minutes, Gomez was on the Italian’s foot. The home side had registered three attempts – one on target – within the first ten minutes, illustrating how front-footed they had set up. In truth, Raya’s pass out of play on two minutes had set the tone for an afternoon only going in one direction. It took until 18 minutes for Arsenal’s first attempt at goal, Bruno Guimaraes’ cross-shot whacking the side netting. When Gross struck, an inevitability had been felt. There was a general sloppiness across the pitch, the Arsenal midfield struggling to string passes together. Pascal Gross, one of Brighton's many in-form players, struck early on to set the tone The Gunners had nearly grabbed a goal back on the cusp of half-time, Martin Odegaard marching forward on a counter-attack. His shot, saved by Bart Verbruggen, rebounded into the path of Bukayo Saka who could only scuff his attempt. The winger hit the turf face down, in dismay at his profligacy. By the time he had looked up, Brighton were in the opposite half. Gomez latched on to a pass and drove forward, supplying Kostoulas. He swivelled outside the area and struck past Raya from 25 yards out. Whatever transpired in the Arsenal dressing room, it clearly didn’t work. It will have been some scene, nevertheless, Arteta expectedly incensed at what he had watched from a team stamping their authority on the league – not just chasing three points. A win here would have been an eighth consecutive win across all competitions, equalling the club’s 123-year record for their best start to a campaign. That quickly became clearly unattainable. Raya’s first action of the second period was to hoof the ball out of play, an early sign that Arsenal were not going to improve anytime soon. Ferdi Kadioglu fell to the deck under pressure from Calafiori, referee Darren England waving away the penalty call. Nothing went Arsenal's way - they now have an international break to mull over their struggles Later, Gross’s corner found the head of Andres to put Brighton three goals ahead, the midfielder rising above Gabriel and Calafiori to head home. Kai Havertz found himself one-on-one with Verbruggen on 78 minutes, Viktor Gyokeres’ clever chipped pass finding the striker. He should have scored – but the ball rebounded off Verbruggen’s leg. Nothing went Arsenal’s way on a day which sent a warning across England’s footballing fraternities.
