Sports.title: West Ham star Taty Castellanos is accused of SPITTING at Millwall goalkeeper during feisty Dockers Derby
Sports.content:
Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall appeared to allege that West Ham forward Taty Castellanos spat at him during a heated Dockers Derby at The Den.

The flashpoint came in the second half with the hosts 2-0 up and cruising in a dominant display against the Hammers, who started the day top of the Championship table.

The shot stopper could be seen dabbing his shirt to his face in astonishment, before appearing to tell referee Paul Tierney: 'He spat at me.'

No sanction was handed to the striker after the accusation. West Ham have denied their player spat at Marschall.

Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall appeared to allege that West Ham forward Taty Castellanos spat at him

Marschall made the accusation during a feisty Dockers Derby between Millwall and West Ham

West Ham deny their striker Taty Castellanos spat at the goalkeeper on Saturday

Lions boss Alex Neil confirmed the allegation afterwards, saying: 'I believe so. Fil was saying to the referee throughout the game when that happened, at that point.

'Obviously I'm so far away so it's hard for me to see what happened, but I wouldn't presume Fil would say that without cause, if you like, so I don't know. I'm sure the referees and the authorities, whoever, will look at it and if it warrants that it needs dealt with, I'm sure they will.'

Hammers boss Nuno Espirito Santo said: 'I didn't see, so I'm not going to comment on any allegations. I didn't see it. And that's not what we should be speaking about [in] this game, this game has much to speak about, it was a very intense game for both fans.'

The Hammers went on to score two goals to leave The Den with a share of the points, with the game ending 2-2.

In December last year, Burnley's Hannibal Mejbri was given a four-match ban and a £15,000 fine after he spat at Leeds fans.

In December 2024, Norwich's Borja Sainz was hit with a six-game suspension and a £12,000 fine for spitting during a Championship defeat by Sunderland.

Sports.title: Unai Emery offered a glimpse of Aston Villa 2.0 during his side's 3-2 win over Tottenham, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - but there is one star they have struggled to replace, while stalwart remains vital to manager's success
Sports.content:
Unai Emery offered a glimpse of Aston Villa 2.0 during his side's 3-2 win over Tottenham, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - but there is one star they have struggled to replace, while stalwart remains vital to manager's success

After six key players left and 11 new ones arrived in a tumultuous summer, Aston Villa 2.0 is slowly starting to take shape.

Unai Emery will know his rebuilt team are some way from the level they reached to lift the Europa League and finish fourth in the Premier League last season but he can see the signs of an intriguing new project.

Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson have the makings of a promising understanding. Joao Gomes and Boubacar Kamara are dovetailing nicely in central midfield. Zion Suzuki looks an excellent replacement for Emi Martinez in goal.

Emery called the three-week international break ‘crazy’ and he will be hugely frustrated that just as his team are finding their stride, he must wave goodbye to a significant number of them.

Villa take on Brentford when the Premier League resumes next month and Saturday’s 3-2 win at Tottenham means they should have a spring in their step.

Unai Emery offered a glimpse of Aston Villa 2.0 during his side's win over Tottenham

Glimpse of a post-Emery world

During Emery’s first four seasons at Villa, he established such control at the club that it became tempting to wonder if they could live without him.

He hired multiple backroom staff, improved virtually every player and had a significant control over transfers. It has been a throwback to the days of Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United, or Arsene Wenger at Arsenal.

Emery remains the key man at Villa Park and when he does depart, it will still leave a huge gap. Yet few coaches would turn down the chance to work with players like Jackson, Manzambi, Gomes, Suzuki and Ibrahim Mbaye. With their recruitment this summer, it feels like Villa were trying to deliver for today while also laying down the foundations for the future.

Of the six players Villa paid fees for last summer, Gomes is the eldest and he does not turn 26 until February. Jackson turned 25 only in June, and the average age of the other six players is 21.5.

Manzambi and Mbaye, in particular, have huge scope for improvement while Suzuki could be the club’s goalkeeper for at least the next decade. Too often in the Emery era, the recruitment has looked hurried. This summer, under difficult circumstances, at least they followed a plan.

Villa's recruitment means that a post-Emery world is not as scary as first thought

Defensive wobbles

Of all the players who left Villa last summer, Ezri Konsa is the one they miss the most.

Jackson looks like a viable replacement for Ollie Watkins, who was starting to decline. If Manzambi fulfils his potential, he can ensure Morgan Rogers is not missed too much. Suzuki’s performances are already making the memory of Emi Martinez fade.

But they don’t have a new Konsa yet. Taylor Harwood-Bellis was nominally the replacement for the England man but is not yet trusted to start the important games. Victor Lindelof has done well but he is no Konsa.

That is why Villa have kept only one clean sheet this season and have already let in 15 in eight matches in all competitions. If Harwood-Bellis is not the answer, do not be surprised to see Villa move again for Club Brugge centre-back Joel Ordonez in January, if he can prove his fitness. Until they fix that, every team will feel they have a chance against Emery’s men.

Victor Lindelof has done well but Villa are struggling to replace Ezri Konsa

McGinn is the man

Whether he is on the left, the right, deep in midfield or as a No10, John McGinn never lets Emery down. Somehow the Scotland man continues to be overlooked when awards season rolls around – he is never even a contender, let alone a potential winner.

Name a player more important to their team than McGinn. Not only does he deliver on the pitch, he sets the tempo off it, too. With so many new faces at Villa this term, McGinn’s role has become even more important and he is clearly relishing it.

Working for Emery is tough. The hours are long. Training sessions are intense and – at times – a little dull. There are long meetings in front of the video at least twice a week. These players belong to a generation famed for its short attention span and life with Emery can be challenging.

When they see the captain step up every day and take it in his stride, it becomes easier to follow suit. McGinn joined Villa for just £2.75m in 2018. The statue they commission for him after retirement will probably cost at least that.

Sports.title: It's time to question Roberto De Zerbi's future after a £320m summer makeover which has left Tottenham looking cheap and tacky, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI
Sports.content:
It's time to question Roberto De Zerbi's future after a £320m summer makeover which has left Tottenham looking cheap and tacky, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

One clock stopped, another ticks on and the question of time is beginning to weigh heavily over the head of Roberto De Zerbi. More precisely, how much embarrassment must Tottenham sustain before his position comes under serious review?

After five games of the campaign, they have no wins, two points and a side that fluctuates in its desire to be either a punchbag or a punchline. Here, against an Aston Villa team with many of the same needs and problems, they submitted themselves to being both.

It was a humiliation that throws sharp focus, once again, on the £320million of summer spending that has somehow left Spurs looking cheap and tacky.

For that, De Zerbi will need to offer better answers than a discussion about incremental progress, which in this case meant scoring not only one goal but two. Times of plenty indeed.

But there’s an obvious issue with getting two when the other guys have three. And there’s a bigger one when each of those goals, finished by Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke, arrived at 3-0 down. In other words, Spurs clocked on when Villa had their first win of the season in the bag.

Credit to Villa for that. They rode an early storm in London, as did Everton at the same ground last week, and in that period Tottenham looked good. Savio, especially. But he faded against Everton and Villa inspired the same withdrawal, because that is what happens with Tottenham – when the going gets tough, or a little frustrating, they shrink. De Zerbi’s clever patterns become charges into blind alleys.

Emi Buendia's stunning strike from distance put Aston Villa 3-0 ahead

Pressure continues to mount on Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi, despite his side scoring two late goals

Johan Manzambi's first-half goal on debut set Villa on their way to their first win of the season

That was shown up against Unai Emery, who read this match so well and turned it by little and large degrees. For one, see how he introduced Matty Cash for Aaron Wan-Bissaka at half-time and in a masterstroke killed the strong momentum Tottenham had built on the left.

This win was a vindication for the Spaniard, who has faced questions of his own about a slow start and a redesigned squad. His international break will spent in a state of far greater comfort.

For De Zerbi, much thinking lies ahead, especially as this was close to his strongest side, evidenced by making only one change to the XI held by Everton, with Pedro Porro brought in for Archie Gray.

If the lack of De Zerbi’s usual tinkering signified some level of clarity in his mind, then it was soon replaced by the usual anxieties – Porro lasted only 17 minutes before succumbing to injurt. On went Gray.

With his first contribution, he dragged a shot a fraction wide, but this was a purple patch for Spurs. In that first half, they were quick, clean and threatening. Omar Marmoush was dangerous on the left, Savio offered greater signs of an end-product on the right, and Dominic Solanke was demonstrating a level of understanding with both.

Naturally it came to nothing. Savio forced a couple of good saves from Zion Suzuki, but no breakthrough was forthcoming and this fell at a point when De Zerbi’s defence were becoming a concern. As individual components, that back four is solid, but Sandro Tonali and Rodrigo Bentancur offer a thin shield.

Villa’s threat was initially limited but they had spaces to exploit and areas to target. Nicolas Jackson helped stretch those lines by keeping to an advanced position and into the voids fell chances for Emiliano Buendia and Johan Manzambi, who each drew decent saves from Antonin Kinsky.

Those were the warnings before the goal arrived with two elements of good fortune in the same attack.

Manzambi swept home after a mistake by Andy Robertson

Savio thought he had equalised for Tottenham...

Before the goal was ruled out for off-side by VAR

Spurs now sit 18th in the table and remain without a win in the league going into the first international break of the season

The first came when Andy Robertson made a well-intentioned lunge to prevent a corner but succeeded only in redirecting play to John McGinn. The latter’s subsequent pass then introduced the second stroke of luck when Boubacar Kamara’s scuffed his shot directly to Manzambi for the finish. Given it was his first start after a £50m move, the Swiss has already made more of an impact than most Tottenham imports beyond Van Hecke.

PLAYER RATINGS Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 6 (Gray 18, 6), Van Hecke 7, Van De Ven 6, Robertson 5; Tonali 6 (Gallagher 84), Bentancur 6 (Bergvall 84); Savio 7, Fernandes 5 (Kudus 46, 6), Marmoush 6; Solanke 5 (Maddison 66, 6). Subs not used: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Udogie. Booked: Van Hecke Manager: Roberto De Zerbi 5 Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 7; Wan-Bissaka 4 (Cash 46), Mings 7, Lindelof 6, Ruggeri 6; Kamara 7 (Mbaye 84), Gomes 6; McGinn 7, Manzambi 7 (Hemmings 72, 6), Buendia 8; Jackson 7 (Abraham 88). Subs not used: Wright, Harwood-Bellis, Barkley, Garnacho, Bogarde. Booked: Jackson Manager: Unai Emery 7 Referee: Sam Barrott 7

Clearly, the goal was a gut punch for De Zerbi and his response was to hook off Mateus Fernandes for Mohammed Kudus at the break. For his part, Emery sent on Cash for Wan-Bissaka, who appears no closer to grasping the complex requirements of his manager.

Emery has those quirks, which extended here to a running battle with the fourth official about the boundaries of his technical area, but there is no doubting the wisdom in his madness. Cash’s handling of Marmoush was far sharper and so too his control of Savio when Marmoush took a more central role.

For De Zerbi, the pursuit was exasperating and made worse when the VAR correctly disallowed Kudus’s strike after spotting that Robertson was a nose offside behind McGinn. In rolling the dice on one that might count, the Spurs coach then sent on James Maddison but within a minute it was 2-0.

The goal was an embarrassment in stages, with Van Hecke losing out to Jackson under a punt from Suzuki, before Micky van de Ven was easily turned by the same man. Fair play to Jackson, his movement was excellent and strike well placed, but Kinsky ought to have saved. When Buendia added a third with a beauty from outside the area, Kinsky could at least be spared any blame.

Tottenham did get their goal, and indeed a second in stoppage time, but by then the game was gone. Time was up. Assuming De Zerbi is given more to play with, he has a lot to think about.

Sports.title: Man Utd Muslim supporters group call for Sir Jim Ratcliffe to QUIT: Fans hit out at billionaire co-owner, 73, after he claimed Britain is 'on the slide' in anti-immigrant BBC rant
Sports.content:
Man Utd Muslim supporters group call for Sir Jim Ratcliffe to QUIT: Fans hit out at billionaire co-owner, 73, after he claimed Britain is 'on the slide' in anti-immigrant BBC rant

Manchester United's Muslim Supporters' Club has issued a statement of no confidence in Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the club's ownership in light of his latest remarks on immigration, coupled with the team's poor start to the season.

Ratcliffe, who is a resident of Monaco and is worth around £15billion, pulled no punches in the BBC's 'Big Boss' interview, where he labelled the UK as a country 'on the slide' from the days when it had 'the greatest empire in the world', pointing to immigration as a significant reason why.

'We had the greatest empire in the world. We were a great people,' Ratcliffe, 73, said.

'We won two world wars. We're good, honest folk. But unfortunately, at the moment, I think the UK is on the slide. It's quite difficult to see how we arrest it.'

He added, which has caused great upset to United fans across the globe: 'Nobody's tough enough to deal with the immigration problem.

'Nobody's tough enough to deal with the benefits problem. But somebody needs to do it.'

Furious Manchester United fans have issued a statement of no confidence against ownership

Sir Jim Ratcliffe angered the club's Muslim Supporters' Club with comments on immigration

🚨 After careful consideration of the current direction of Manchester United, the way the club is being run, and recent statements made by Sir Jim Ratcliffe, we wish to issue a statement of no confidence.



Read our full statement below. pic.twitter.com/Qhx2H4PMTP — Man United Muslims (@mum_sc) September 19, 2026

The response from United's fans, who protested against Ratcliffe, Ineos and the Glazers ahead of last week's Manchester derby defeat, has been fierce and the Muslim Supporters' Club is calling for Ratcliffe to leave the club.

'Our players, staff, stewards, security teams and supporters come from different countries, cultures, ethnicities, religions and backgrounds,' part of the 750-word statement reads.

'Manchester United would not be Manchester United without them. That diversity isn't a weakness of Manchester United. It is part of Manchester United

'Different backgrounds. Different beliefs. Different politics. One Manchester United.

'Manchester United does not belong emotionally to investment funds, shareholders or billionaires. It belongs to the generations of supporters who inherited this club from their parents and grandparents and who will one day pass it to their children.

'We love Manchester United. This club is all we know and, when it comes to football, it will be all we ever know. That is precisely why we cannot stay silent.

'This is bigger than one defeat. Bigger than one manager. Bigger than one season. It is about the direction, leadership and identity of Manchester United Football Club.

'After years of decline, broken promises and repeated failure, Manchester United Muslim Supporters' Club has lost confidence in the current ownership structure of Manchester United Football Club.

There is a growing animosity from matchgoing supporters against those in positions of power

Ratcliffe has come into sharp focus, just months on from angering fans with similar remarks

'Enough is enough. It is time for change. The Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe must go.'

Manchester United put out a statement of their own earlier this year when Ratcliffe again addressed his frustration at the UK government's view on immigration. Ratcliffe went on to apologise if he 'offended some people'.

This time it is the fans that have turned on Ratcliffe and an ownership that are under huge pressure after a difficult transfer window which looks to have left head coach Michael Carrick short.

'Earlier this year, MUMSC publicly challenged Sir Jim Ratcliffe after his comments that the UK had been 'colonised by immigrants'. We condemned those comments then. He subsequently apologised for his choice of language,' the latest Muslim Supporters' Club statement read.

'We hoped a lesson had been learned. Clearly, it has not.

'This week, Sir Jim has again placed immigration and people receiving benefits at the centre of his explanation for Britain's problems, arguing that nobody is 'tough enough' to deal with either.

'We find these latest comments deeply disappointing and completely unacceptable.'

It is the latest flashpoint in a dismal start to the campaign which has seen United crash out of the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle, booed off after throwing away a 2-0 lead at home to Brighton to lose 3-2.

They are also in the bottom half of the Premier League with just one win in the league so far, losing at Hull City, drawing at Everton and losing to Manchester United.

Daily Mail Sport criticised Ineos' negligence in their time in charge this week and more fans are becoming increasingly irate at an ownership that promised to be best in class and is falling some way short of that.

Sports.title: Jordan Henderson embroiled in tense on-field spat with Emiliano Martinez: Chelsea star exchanges words with new team-mate after first Brentford goal in shock 3-0 defeat
Sports.content:
Chelsea new boys Jordan Henderson and Emiliano Martinez were involved in a war of words after Brentford's first goal on Friday night.

The Blues were schooled in a 3-0 rout away at Brentford as second-half goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago, and Fabio Carvalho left them for dead.

Club legend Gary Cahill blasted them as 'soft' in the aftermath, with Chelsea having conceded 12 goals in their five Premier League games so far.

Martinez was signed from Aston Villa for £7.5million late in the window to seemingly fix their goalkeeper issue. Former number one Robert Sanchez conceded three on the opening weekend against Fulham and is now on loan at Como.

But the 33-year-old Argentinian has struggled to have the desired impact so far and Henderson voiced his frustration after Anthony's opening goal.

Brentford scored far too easily from a corner, with Mikkel Damsgaard's cross being whipped towards the back post before it was headed back across to an unmarked Anthony.

Jordan Henderson and Emiliano Martinez got into a heated exchange after conceding

Chelsea lost 3-0 against Brentford - and Jaidon Anthony's opening goal was far too easy

Anthony was only loosely marked and Martinez was nowhere near as the forward headed in

Martinez was fairly static throughout the set-piece and Henderson appeared annoyed that the goalkeeper had not come for the ball.

But the fact that Anthony had found space to head home with three defenders in his vicinity raised alarm bells.

Henderson, meanwhile, had been marking nobody.

The midfielder, who was signed from the Bees for his experience and leadership qualities, also remonstrated with defender Maxence Lacroix at another point.

This was Henderson's debut for Chelsea, having signed while he was recovering from a broken arm sustained on England duty.

Brentford now sit third in the Premier League and are still unbeaten, while Xabi Alonso's side are seventh - and you can expect them to slip with nine matches still to come this weekend.

Former Chelsea captain Cahill told Sky Sports at full time: 'There is a certain element of fragility.

'Once they’ve conceded that set piece, you don’t want it to be a mindset but it is a "here we go again" type scenario.

Henderson and Martinez did appear to comfort each other in their full-time disappointment

'I’m sure the manager will address it in videos and on the training ground. Obviously, as a goalkeeper and a back four, you feel a big responsibility when goals are going in.

'The only way you can get out of that is by working hard together and making sure you’re harder to play against, and be more ruthless.

'There just seems to be a kind of softness at the minute in terms of the way they concede goals. You have a few weeks now during the international break, although some of them won’t be there, but they will have time.'

Alonso is attempting to implement a back three with wing-backs, a system which has often been a risk in the English top flight.

Ruben Amorim, for example, could never get his back-three structure to work at Manchester United.

It does have precedent as being successful for Chelsea - fans will remember Antonio Conte's 2016-17 title-winning season fondly.

The Blues were 3-0 down at half-time against Arsenal in their sixth game of that season, prompting Conte to switch to a back three, which he had never drilled.

They then went on a remarkable 13-game winning streak in the league, and won the title by seven points, proving that flexibility can be a key trait for a manager.

Sports.title: Tabby Stoecker's incredible life in a circus before starting new career due to Instagram ad
Sports.content:
Tabby Stoecker's incredible life in a circus before starting new career due to Instagram ad

Winter Olympics hero Tabby Stoecker is one of the stars taking part in the new series of Strictly Come Dancing

View 3 Images Tabby Stoecker will be on this year's Strictly Come Dancing (Image: BBC/Ray Burmiston)

Skeleton star Tabby Stoecker will hit the dance floor on Saturday night as she begins her stint on Strictly Come Dancing. Stoecker, 25, made history with teammate Matt Weston after winning mixed team gold at the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics earlier this year.

‌



The highly decorated Team GB athlete only made her international debut in the sport five years ago and was turned on to the discipline by an Instagram advert.

‌



Speaking to BBC Breakfast in February, she elaborated: "I saw an advert on Instagram for Discover Your Gold Talent ID process and got selected for skeleton." Prior to that, Stoecker had a life in the circus, training in such activities as juggling and clowning.

‌



Stoecker told Olympics.com in November 2025: "When I was about 11, one of my friends was doing an open day at the National Centre for Circus Arts in London, and I just went along with her.

"And having a background in gymnastics as a very young kid, I was really up for this whole circus skills thing. One of the coaches asked me to audition for a scheme they have, which was to help kids get really, really good circus training basically, and it was a very holistic approach."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Stoecker trained from ages 11 to 17, with around 20-25 hours of training in addition to school. She added: "Someone does your schedule for you and helps you with managing school and all the training.

"To be honest, it was one of the most incredible things. It was an incredible opportunity for me and just the people that you were surrounded by. It was this massive community and they really cared about your well-being as well as your training. I think that just gave me a very well-rounded level of athletic ability."

View 3 Images Great Britain's Matt Weston and Tabby Stoecker with their gold medals (Image: Andrew Milligan/PA Wire.)

‌



Her favourite circus act was the flying trapeze, which she believes helped her adjust to the dangerous and high-speed world of Skeleton.

"I had an incredible coach with that," she said. "You have to let go of a bar and fly around in the air and the adrenaline rush was incredible.

"I didn't know what skeleton was at that point, but I just wasn't sure I saw a career for myself in circus, and you're at that age where you're not sure about things, and I wanted to test some other stuff out.

‌



View 3 Images Olympic champion Tabby Stoecker opened up on his career (Image: Getty Images)

"I got accepted for skeleton and they taught me how to run, how to lift, and when I went out on the ice for the first time, that feeling of adrenaline was quite familiar, I guess. I had good spatial awareness and body awareness, and I just picked it up, and I guess the rest is history."

Ahead of joining Strictly, she said: "I am over the moon to be joining the cast of Strictly 2026. I’ve had the wildest year of my life so far, so to be rounding it off with a childhood dream of dancing in the Strictly ballroom is surreal and I can’t wait to get stuck in."

Article continues below

Stoecker joins Lacey Turner, Dani Dyer, Delta Goodrem, Chris Appleton, Cach Mercer, Will Best, Dame Sarah Storey, Jaime Winstone, Bethany Antonia, Shaun Wright-Phillips, Graeme Hall and Lawrence Robb in the new season of Strictly.

Sports.title: Jarrod Bowen's alternative marriage offer and saucy chant about Dani Dyer
Sports.content:
Jarrod Bowen's alternative marriage offer and saucy chant about Dani Dyer

West Ham legend Jarrod Bowen had an unusual marriage request shortly before tying the knot with Strictly Come Dancing star Dani Dyer

View 4 Images Jarrod Bowen and Dani Dyer have been an item since 2021 (Image: Jed Cullen/Dave Benett/Getty Images)

West Ham hero Jarrod Bowen actually had a wildly different proposal before marrying Dani Dyer in 2025. Reality TV star Dyer, 30, is back on screens on Saturday for Strictly Come Dancing.

‌



The daughter of acting icon Danny Dyer shot to fame after winning Love Island in 2018. Fast forward three years, and she met Hammers striker Bowen, 29, in 2021.

‌



Danny was clearly ecstatic at his daughter's choice of partner, being a West Ham fanatic. When the duo announced their engagement in 2024, after having twin daughters Star and Summer a year earlier, The Football Factory star jokingly claimed that Bowen should be marrying him instead.

‌



Ahead of the pair's nuptials, he told Closer: "I think I'm in love with him. He plays for West Ham and he's unbelievable, this guy. He comes in my house, I take his shoes off for him and I give him the remote control, and I say, ‘Mate, this is your house now.’ He's an incredible person.

"I can't wait to give Dani away, but I still think that he's marrying the wrong Danny Dyer. Honestly, I feel sorry for my other daughter, who's nearly 18, because she could never bring home a man to match what Jarrod’s done for me.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Jarrod Bowen could land Premier League return in £50m transfer despite contract vow READ MORE :

"She could bring home a heart surgeon or somebody who cures cancer and I’ll go, ‘Well, really? Jarrod's got the winning goal in a European final.’ I couldn't have written a better script. He's just such a beautiful man."

Danny's love for Bowen is shared by the Irons' faithful. Sections of the crowd often serenade the forward to the explicit chant: "Bowen's on fire, and he's s******g Dani Dyer" - to the tune of dance hit Freed from Desire.

View 4 Images Bowen has grown close to his West Ham-supporting father-in-law (Image: danidyerxx)

‌



Danny himself slightly restructured the song to make it more family-friendly during his father-of-the-bride speech at his daughter's wedding. On videos shared on social media, he could be heard urging guests to sing "Bowen's On Fire – and he's married Dani Dyer.'

After Bowen scored the late winner in West Ham's heroic 2-1 Europa Conference League final victory against Fiorentina in 2023, supporters once again sang the song. This time, Bowen was filmed jumping up and down to the chant.

Despite West Ham's relegation from the Premier League last season, Bowen signed a new deal with the East London club. He's started the Championship season in fine form, too.

‌



4 View 4 Images Danny Dyer led the chant at his daughter's wedding (Image: Instagram/) 4 View 4 Images Dani Dyer and Jarrod Bowen tied the knot in a stunning ceremony (Image: Danu Dyer Instagram / evieradfordsocials)

Yet Saturday night will see Dani take the stage after her stint on the BBC ballroom show was cut short last year due to injury. Such was its severity that she was ruled out of the show before the live shows even began.

Article continues below

Dani is now being given a second shot at being part of the BBC One dance show. She said: "If I'm really honest, my biggest fear is getting injured again. I'm going to do everything I can to look after myself, stay positive and just enjoy every moment of the experience."

Sports.title: Man Utd Muslim supporters group demand Jim Ratcliffe exit after statement on UK decline
Sports.content:
Man Utd Muslim supporters group demand Jim Ratcliffe exit after statement on UK decline

Manchester United minority co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe has landed himself in hot water once again with comments on immigration and welfare

View 3 Images Manchester United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe has come under fire from the Manchester United Muslim Supporters Club. (Image: PA Wire)

Manchester United's Muslim Supporters Club have released a damning statement of no confidence in co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe following a recent interview regarding the 'decline of the United Kingdom.' During the interview, the United minority owner expressed his view that the United Kingdom is on the slide and calls for a tougher stance on immigration and what he describes as 'the benefits problem.'

‌



Speaking in Denmark at the launch of the EU's first carbon capture and storage system (CCS), Ratcliffe said: "We had the greatest empire in the world. We were a great people. We won two world wars.

‌



"Nobody's tough enough to deal with the immigration problem. Nobody's tough enough to deal with the benefits problem. But somebody needs to do it."

‌



It's not the first time Ratcliffe has found himself coming under fire for comments related to immigration. Earlier this year he sparked controversy by saying the UK had been "colonised by immigrants" before apologising for his choice of language.

However, the Manchester United Muslim Supporters' Club has now called for Ratcliffe and the Glazers to leave the club, saying it is time for change.

The statement read: "After careful consideration of the current direction of Manchester United, the way the club is being run and recent statements made but Sir Jim Ratcliffe, we wish to issue a statement of no confidence.

‌



"This week, Manchester United were knocked out of the Carabao Cup following another defeat at Old Trafford, Days earlier, we lost at home to a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men. We sit 13th in the Premier League with four points from four games.

"As always, the immediate reaction will be to point at the manager. Then the players. Then the coaching staff. But Manchester United supporters have been doing this for more than a decade. Managers have changed. Players have changed. Coaching teams have changed. Executives have changed. The cycle hasn't.

"At some point, we have to stop looking at the latest person standing in the dugout and start looking at those responsible for the direction of the football club. For years, the Glazer ownership has presided over Manchester United's decline. When Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS arrived, many supporters hoped it would finally signal meaningful change.

‌



"We were among those who hoped. Instead, our confidence in the ownership structure has continued to erode. Supporters have continued to turn up, travel and spend their money through years of underachievement. And what have they received in return?

View 3 Images (Image: Bo Amstrup/EPA/Shutterstock)

"Higher ticket prices. A stadium allowed to deteriorate. Years of poor decision-making. Vast sums spent without sustained success. And a football team that continues to fall further behind where Manchester United should be. The manager didn't create this cycle. The players didn't create this cycle. The people making the decisions did.

‌



"And now our concerns extend beyond the pitch. Earlier this year, MUMSC publicly challenged Sir Jim Ratcliffe after his comments that the UK had been 'colonised by immigrants.' We condemned those comments then. He subsequently apologised for his choice of language. We hoped a lesson had been learned. Clearly, it has not.

"This week, Sir Jim has again placed immigration and people receiving benefits at the centre of his explanation for Britain's problems, arguing that nobody is 'tough enough' to deal with either. We find these latest comments deeply disappointing and completely unacceptable.

"Once again, immigrants and some of the most vulnerable people in society are being presented as part of the problem by one of Britain's wealthiest individuals. And the hypocrisy is difficult to ignore. Once again, instead of focusing on years of allowing corporate greed to prosper at the expense of political investment in key institutions and infrastructure, which would have benefited Britain, he is scapegoating and deflecting political mishandling and mismanagement onto racialised communities, playing into populist tropes that are bereft of accurate academic rigour.

‌



"Sir Jim talks of Britain's 'benefits problem,' yet the UK Government recently committed more than £120m of public money towards supporting an INEOS operation. Sir Jim also chose to move his own tax residence from Britain to Monaco. There may be sound economic reasons for governments to protect strategically important businesses and jobs. But if state support is acceptable when it benefits your own business interests, it is difficult to then lecture ordinary people about their reliance upon the state.

View 3 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe became co-owner at Manchester United in 2024. (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista, Getty Images)

"You cannot demand toughness for ordinary people while welcoming state support when it benefits you and expect nobody to question this contradiction. And there is something particularly troubling about this rhetoric coming from one of the people responsible for Manchester United. Look around Old Trafford on any matchday.

‌



"Our players, staff, stewards, security teams and supporters come from different countries, cultures, ethnicities, religions and backgrounds. Manchester United would not be Manchester United without them. That diversity isn't a weakness of Manchester United.

"It is part of Manchester United. Different backgrounds. Different beliefs. Different politics. One Manchester United. Manchester United does not belong emotionally to investment funds, shareholders or billionaires. It belongs to the generations of supporters who inherited this football club from their parents and grandparents, and who will one day pass on to their children.

"We love Manchester United. This club is all we know and, when it comes to football, it will be all we ever know. That is precisely why we cannot stay silent. This is bigger than one defeat. Bigger than one manager. Bigger than one season. It is about the direction, the leadership and identity of Manchester United Football Club.

Article continues below

"After years of decline, broken promises and repeated failure, Manchester United Muslim Supporters' Club has lost confidence in the current ownership structure of Manchester United Football Club. Enough is enough. It is time for change. The Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe must go."

Sports.title: West Ham star accused of SPITTING by Millwall goalkeeper during derby clash
Sports.content:
West Ham star accused of SPITTING by Millwall goalkeeper during derby clash

Referee Paul Tierney stopped play during the clash between Millwall and West Ham following an allegation of spitting made by Filip Marschall against Taty Castellanos

View 3 Images Filip Marschall and Taty Castellanos got into an altercation (Image: Sky Sports)

Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall accused West Ham striker Taty Castellanos of SPITTING at him during Saturday's Dockers Derby. The incident happened midway through the second half with Millwall leading 2-0 at The Den, where there was a charged atmosphere.

‌



As Castellanos attempted to close Marschall down before he picked up the ball, the players got into an altercation. It was at that point when Marschall claimed that he'd been spat at and wiped his head with his shirt.

‌



Referee Paul Tierney, who normally officiates at Premier League level, halted play to speak to Marschall. The allegation was reported to fourth official Lewis Smith by Millwall's coaching staff.

‌



Post-match, Millwall manager Alex Neil was asked about the incident by Sky Sports and replied: "Obviously, I'm so far away so it's hard for me to see what happened, but I wouldn't presume Fil would say that without cause, if you like, so I don't know.

‌



"I'm sure the referees and the authorities, whoever, will look at it and if it warrants that it needs dealt with, I'm sure they will."

Meanwhile, West Ham boss Nuno Espirito Santo said that he 'didn't see' the incident. When play restarted, the away side mounted a comeback and quickly made it 2-2 through goals from Mohamadou Kante and Kostas Mavropanos.

Kante was then sent off in the 89th minute as he desperately prevented a Millwall attack. The hosts pushed for a winner in front of a baying crowd, but the two London clubs had to settle for a thrilling draw in their first meeting since 2012.

‌



View 3 Images The allegation was made against Taty Castellanos (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

Millwall took the lead inside 16 minutes, as Caleb Taylor pounced at the far post after West Ham goalkeeper Mads Hermansen made two brilliant saves. Neil's side doubled their lead in the third minute of first-half stoppage time, with Camiel Neghli bundling home after a long throw-in.

Nuno made two changes at half-time, bringing on Kante and Pablo. The pair combined to score in the 74th minute and West Ham were level soon after.

‌



View 3 Images Paul Tierney was seen in discussion with Filip Marschall (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

Mavropanos scored his fourth goal of the season courtesy of Manor Solomon's cross. Millwall were given a lifeline when Kante - as the last man back - was shown a red card for taking down Kyrell Lisbie, yet they were unable to find a third goal.

The result leaves West Ham at risk of being knocked off top spot by several chasing teams later this weekend. For Millwall, they'll go into the international break outside of the play-off positions.

Sports.title: Golf latest: Rory McIlroy reacts as former Masters winner withdraws from BMW PGA
Sports.content:
Golf latest: Rory McIlroy reacts as former Masters winner withdraws from BMW PGA

The 2026 BMW PGA Championship is underway at Wentworth - here are the latest headlines from the world of golf including a major update on Rory McIlroy

View 3 Images Rory McIlroy is in the hunt for the BMW PGA Championship title (Image: Getty)

The BMW PGA Championship is into its crucial weekend stages, with Wentworth once again providing the backdrop for one of the biggest events on the DP World Tour calendar. With a host of the world's leading players battling it out, there is plenty at stake as the season edges towards its conclusion.

‌



As ever, the action has not been short of talking points, with events on and off the course adding an extra layer of intrigue to proceedings in Surrey. One of the tournament's biggest names has seen his hopes take an unexpected turn, while another has been given fresh reason to believe he can make an impact on the Race to Dubai standings.

‌



There has also been plenty of respect between two familiar rivals, despite their history of fierce competition over the years. With the third round now underway, here is the latest from Wentworth as the BMW PGA Championship takes centre stage.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rory McIlroy statement released after star gets big boost by BMW Championship officials READ MORE :

PGA Tour caddie quits job midway through round as he drops club, throws bib and storms off READ MORE :

Patrick Reed withdraws

Patrick Reed was forced to pull out midway through the second round of the BMW PGA Championship. The former Masters champion had made an encouraging start and was sitting inside the top 10 before his afternoon took a dramatic turn.

Reed ran into trouble on the ninth hole before attempting a difficult shot close to a tree root. After playing the awkward shot, he appeared to be struggling with his wrist and was eventually taken away from the course by cart.

‌



View 3 Images Patrick Reed has withdrawn after appearing to injure his wrist (Image: Getty)

The withdrawal represents a major setback for Reed's ambitions on the DP World Tour. He arrived at Wentworth leading the Race to Dubai standings, narrowly ahead of Rory McIlroy, and had been hoping to strengthen his position with another strong showing.

Instead, his early exit gives McIlroy a valuable opening in the battle for the season-ending prize.

‌



Rory McIlroy speaks out

McIlroy was asked about Reed's withdrawal and his own position in the Race to Dubai battle, making it clear that his motivation to win remains unchanged regardless of who stands in his way.

The Northern Irishman also acknowledged the competitive history between the pair and paid tribute to Reed's performances since leaving LIV Golf. With Reed unable to add to his points tally at Wentworth, McIlroy now has a chance to make significant ground this weekend.

View 3 Images McIlroy has had his say (Image: Getty)

‌



McIlroy began the third round on eight under, four shots behind leader Ryan Gerard, and knows a strong finish could considerably reduce the gap between himself and Reed with only a few weeks of the season remaining.

Speaking about his long-running rivalry with Reed, McIlroy said: "Obviously Patrick and I have had quite the battles over years, whether it be Ryder Cup, final round in a major," he said.

"Dubai Desert Classic a few years ago. He's a great competitor and he's played great all year. I respect him for how he's went about it, and coming through here, he's put his head down and done the work, and it's actually been really good to see.

Article continues below

"Unfortunately he's pulled out this week, which gives me an opportunity to try to claw back some ground that I lost last week in Ireland. This weekend is a big weekend for me to pick up a few points and make the race even tighter going into these last few weeks."

Sports.title: Ayr Gold Cup under threat after 40-minute deluge of rain leaves standing water on track
Sports.content:
Ayr Gold Cup under threat after 40-minute deluge of rain leaves standing water on track

The ground at Ayr Racecourse was changed to heavy after 8.5mm of rain fell and caused water to build up on the course ahead of Scotland's biggest meeting on the Flat

View Image Jockey Paul Mulrennan (left) inspecting the ground conditions at Ayr Racecourse (Image: Steve Welsh/PA Wire)

Horse racing's big Saturday meeting at Ayr is under threat after a deluge of rain at the track this morning.

‌



A total of 8.5mm fell in 40 minutes and turned the ground heavy, causing standing water around half-a-furlong from the winning post. The area is unavoidable and will need to be crossed the the horses and jockeys on the final day of three at the Ladbrokes-sponsored festival.

‌



Jockeys including St Leger heroine Saffie Osborne and top northern rider Paul Mulrennan went out to check conditions at 12.20pm and a decision was made to push the first race to 2.30pm. However the seven-race card, which had the feature £180,000 Ladbrokes Ayr Gold Cup scheduled for 3.40pm, has to pass a second inspection at 1.45pm.

‌



Prior to the call being made, Racing TV presenter Gordon Brown suggested there is a "40 per cent chance of racing." "There's slight odds against racing taking place," he said.

"The problem area is about half-a-furlong down from the winning post. The rain that fell was of biblical proportions, really heavily and quickly. Lots of the car parks were flooded, the way I have come in all the roads were flooded and there is a showery forecast this afternoon.

‌



"The jockeys have had a look at this area. It's all the way across so it's unavoidable. You can't come past it on the round or straight course and we have two big fields today for the Gold and Silver Cups."

Trainer Jim Goldie said on ITV he thinks officials could "probably" give the event the green light if it stays dry. "It's up to the jockeys if they decide it's not safe," he said.

Sports.title: Florian Wirtz admits Liverpool issue as playmaker takes personal responsibility
Sports.content:
Florian Wirtz admits Liverpool issue as playmaker takes personal responsibility

Liverpool are yet to click into gear this season and, having drawn three of their four Premier League games, Florian Wirtz admits he and his fellow attackers need to have more of a ruthless edge

View 2 Images More is expected of Florian Wirtz in his second Liverpool season

Florian Wirtz admits Liverpool's frontmen finishing off games is something they must "work on" having seen the Reds already drop six points this season.

‌



Three draws in their opening four games has left Liverpool someway off the pace set by Arsenal and Manchester City with Nottingham Forest and Fulham both leaving Anfield with a point.

‌



Last weekend Liverpool failed to find a way through the Fulham defence, despite the Cottagers sitting in the bottom three of the Premier League, Forest twice led on Merseyside and Newcastle held Andoni Iraola's side on the opening weekend.

‌



During those games Wirtz, who has been deployed centrally as the team's No.10, and record signing Alexander Isak have both underwhelmed and copped criticism. Summer signing Bradley Barcola is yet to score his first goal, missing several big chances against Atletico Madrid recently, and the German admits the Liverpool attack need to do more.

He told the club's website : "I think we had a few games where we could have scored more goals to win the game. I have also the expectations for myself to decide games. We need me and the attackers to finish the games off, so we definitely try to work on that."

Iraola is yet to taste defeat as Liverpool boss but Wirtz admits, with just one win from four league games, they want to have amassed more points.

"It's good that we are still unbeaten," he said. "For sure we want to have more points at this stage. But I think it's still a good base to build on – let's try to keep going like that and get even more points."

‌



View 2 Images Liverpool's expensively assembled side is yet to click

Liverpool are spoilt for attacking personnel but Iraola is tasked with finding a system that can get the best from those individuals as a unit. Despite having three £100million plus players in their ranks it is Cody Gakpo who has been their best performer. Youngster Rio Ngumoha and summer arrival Victor Munoz are also seeking minutes.

Much of the spotlight has fallen on the expensive stars and Iraola has claimed that the reaction to Wirtz and his performances is overblown.

Article continues below

The Spaniard said: "He should be judged like everybody else, whether he plays well or doesn't play well. Mostly I always say how does the team play when you are on the pitch. I am very happy with Florian, I rate him very highly, he understands what we need from him. He is trying to help in every aspect of the game."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
