World.title: Demonstrators in US form human chain to protest Kennedy Center closure vote
World.content:
The “Hands Around the Kennedy Center” rally drew thousands after Trump-backed board votes to close the iconic arts venue.

Thousands of protesters formed a human chain around the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington DC to contest its closure, amid fears that United States President Donald Trump could make good on his threat to demolish the venerated landmark.

The crowd filled streets in the Foggy Bottom neighbourhood of the capital on Friday evening, bringing traffic to a standstill as demonstrators made their way to the “Hands Around the Kennedy Center” protest. Many carried signs and some wore costumes, while boos rang out when Trump was mentioned during the programme.

At one point, some protesters linked hands around the building, whose marble facade remained partly concealed by scaffolding and tarpaulins.

Among the most iconic buildings on Washington’s Potomac waterfront, the Kennedy Center has become a battleground over Trump’s bid to assert control over the institution since he returned to office last year, replacing its board with his own appointees and installing himself as chairman.

Chris Raleigh, co-founder of Hands Off the Arts, which organised the rally, said in an interview with The Associated Press news agency that he hoped the turnout would show that people were prepared to push back against Trump’s plans for the building.

The demonstration comes just days after the Trump-installed board voted to close the centre for repairs that are expected to last up to two years. That came hours after District Judge Christopher Cooper quashed the board’s latest attempt to restore Trump’s name to the building.



Last December, the new board added Trump’s name to the building’s facade after the Kennedy Center said its Board of Trustees had unanimously voted to rename the institution in his honour.

A federal judge blocked those efforts in May, ruling that the board had exceeded its statutory authority by unilaterally renaming the Kennedy Center and adding Trump’s name to its facade without congressional approval. Congress had designated the centre as a memorial to the late 35th US President John F Kennedy.

In August, the board tried again to inscribe Trump’s name on the building, this time with wording along the lines of “The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts Restored and Renovated By President Donald J. Trump”.

The federal judge scotched the move in September, ruling that it violated his May injunction.

Trump has since declined to rule out demolishing the building, while a federal judge on Thursday ordered the Kennedy Center to give 30 days’ notice before undertaking any major structural changes, including demolition.

Speaking to reporters in North Carolina on Wednesday, Trump argued that his administration deserved recognition for rescuing the Kennedy Center and that without the repairs, the building risked falling into disrepair and ultimately being forced to shut down.

Raleigh said he, like others, is concerned that Trump could move ahead without first notifying the court.

“Look at the East Wing,” he said. “We got up one morning and there was a giant hole there.”

World.title: Police hiring standards matter. But they alone cannot stop abuse
World.content:
Law enforcement in the US needs high hiring standards. But it also needs reform and trust-building in communities.

Share Police hiring standards matter. But they alone cannot stop abuse on social media

During a congressional hearing earlier this week, FBI Director Kash Patel defended changes to the bureau’s hiring standards. His testimony came just two weeks after reports surfaced of loosened hiring standards at another law enforcement agency in the US: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

As a result, concerns have emerged about a retreat from standards intended to protect the public by offering a baseline of conduct for law enforcement officers. The American public is right to worry. Loose hiring standards can put reckless individuals in positions of power.

But ensuring commitment to higher standards in law enforcement recruitment alone cannot solve the police violence problem in the US.

Individual misconduct

Research on police misconduct, which has considerably expanded in the wake of Black Lives Matter and related movements, offers useful parameters to guide how we approach the question of hiring standards.

Studies have shown that most cases of use of force are concentrated among a relatively small proportion of officers, at least in the limited departments that track such incidents. That means there are officers who are repeat offenders and have the tendency to engage in such misconduct.

So can risk individuals be identified before they are hired?

One study of more than 12,000 police applicants found that specific responses on pre-employment psychological evaluations were associated with subsequent excessive force complaints and complaints alleging racial misconduct.

However, another study of 642 first-year police officers found that markers for anti-social and borderline behaviour could predict the likelihood of engaging only in certain types of abuse – namely sexual misconduct.



There is also research that suggests abusive policing and officers’ psychological wellbeing may be intertwined, and that the harms of misconduct may extend beyond targeted civilians, possibly even to the offending officers themselves.

In a sample of 137 active-duty US police officers, approximately 11 percent self-reported engaging in abusive policing. Abusive policing was associated with greater PTSD symptoms even after accounting for adverse childhood experiences and workplace trauma.

The implication of all this is that hiring standards based on psychological profiling should neither be dismissed as irrelevant nor treated as a fully reliable way to eliminate all future risk. Standards should be evaluated according to what they actually predict, what they exclude, and what risks arise when they are removed.

Structural violence

But improper selection of law enforcement recruits is only part of the problem.

The US has an exceptionally high rate of police violence compared with other wealthy democracies. For example, the rate of police killings is 33.5 per 10 million in the US, compared with 9.8 in Canada, 1.3 in Germany, and 0.5 in England and Wales.

That cannot plausibly be explained simply by whom we happen to hire. American law enforcement gives officers extraordinary authority to detain, search, use force and, in some circumstances, take a life.

Those powers operate within institutions that have repeatedly struggled with racial bias, unnecessary antagonism of marginalised communities, and abuses of authority. There is also inadequate accountability for law enforcement misconduct, including through qualified immunity and other legal protections that can make it difficult to hold officers personally liable for certain constitutional violations.

The problem, in other words, is not simply that some individuals enter policing who should not. It is also the system into which they enter, and the organisational cultures, incentives, and practices that can shape how they use the power they have been given.

Reducing police misconduct requires system-wide reform, including greater accountability not only for individual officers but for the agencies and institutions responsible for policing.

Effective policing depends in part on public cooperation. Global research across dozens of countries has linked perceived fairness, procedural justice and trust in police to people’s willingness to cooperate with law enforcement.

The credibility of hiring standards can be part of trust-building initiatives, but they must also include broader efforts to strengthen trust and legitimacy among marginalised communities by reducing racial profiling, unnecessary uses of force, and inequitable enforcement of laws.



The challenge is not simply to identify the “wrong” candidates and exclude them, but to build institutions in which selection is accompanied by effective training, supervision, and accountability. Ultimately, the institutions entrusted with extraordinary powers have to be structured to protect the people they serve.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

World.title: Russia reports ‘powerful’ cyberattacks on second day of parliamentary vote
World.content:
This is Russia’s first election since it invaded Ukraine, and is expected to gauge public support for the ongoing war.

Share Russia reports ‘powerful’ cyberattacks on second day of parliamentary vote on social media

Russian authorities ⁠have reported attacks on ⁠the country’s voting systems and communication lines on the second day of a tightly controlled three-day-long parliamentary election.

Moscow’s electronic voting system was subjected to a powerful cyberattack overnight between Friday and Saturday, and the attack has continued, Interfax news agency reported.

“The Moscow system was under a very powerful attack, literally non-stop, all night long,” Ella Pamfilova, head of the Russian Central Election Commission, told reporters on Saturday morning. “This attack is ongoing almost constantly, and it’s very large-scale and intense, meaning it’s currently targeting Moscow.”

Pamfilova said the electronic voting system is still operating as normal, and did not give details on the nature of the attack or who was responsible.

The election, which will decide all 450 seats in Russia’s lower house, the State Duma, is due to run until 18:00 GMT on Sunday.

The State Duma election is the first since Russia launched its full-scale war on Ukraine in February 2022, and is widely ⁠expected to see the governing pro-Putin United Russia party maintain its dominance in Russia’s tightly controlled political system.

Most antiwar candidates were excluded from the ballot before voting across Russia’s 11 time zones got under way, after the Supreme Court ruled last month that the ‌liberal Yabloko party – which wants a ceasefire in Ukraine – had breached electoral rules, which it has denied.

Russian President Vladimir Putin accused Ukraine on Friday of trying to “hinder” the vote, an accusation to which Kyiv has not responded. Ukraine has called the election farcical.



More than 350 Ukrainian drones targeted the Russian capital on Friday morning, Moscow’s mayor reported.

With the vote potentially offering the Kremlin a measure of the public mood over the invasion, Kyiv has maintained its bid to use air attacks to make Russians feel the impact of the conflict politically, socially, and economically.

Nationwide turnout as of 14:00 local time on Saturday (11:00 GMT) stood at 32.58 percent, according to CEC data cited by state media.

Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova told Russian state news agency TASS that Russians are showing active participation in the ongoing State Duma elections despite physical threats and cyber challenges. She said that the high voter turnout shows people’s united response to the war declared against Russia and its people.

World.title: UEFA defends policy after rejecting Ireland’s request not to play Israel
World.content:
UEFA responds after Ireland’s football association says its request to avoid future pairings with Israel was ⁠rejected.

Share UEFA defends policy after rejecting Ireland’s request not to play Israel on social media

UEFA has said that decisions on whether national teams should be kept apart in ⁠⁠competition draws are made ⁠⁠on a case-by-case basis and guided primarily by security considerations, after the Republic of Ireland’s football association said its request to avoid future pairings with Israel had been ⁠⁠rejected.

Football Association of Ireland chief executive David Courell said on Friday that it had asked UEFA if the Republic of Ireland and Israel could be separated in future draws ⁠⁠after being paired in February’s Nations League draw.

They are due to meet in that competition on September 27 and October 4.

European football’s governing body said requests to stop teams being drawn against each other are considered individually.

“Decisions to avoid certain teams being ‌‌drawn against each other are made taking into consideration several factors, especially conditions between the two countries leading to structural risks for security,” UEFA said in a statement on Saturday.

“UEFA handles every situation very carefully on its own merits and monitors all facts and developments.”

Courell told reporters the FAI had been informed that such an arrangement would not be possible because Ireland and Israel had “never been in direct conflict”.

The Israel Football Association also responded ⁠⁠to Courell’s remarks, questioning whether a formal request had been ⁠⁠made to UEFA.

“The question should be directed at UEFA: was there an official inquiry or request regarding this matter, or is this merely another inconsequential statement?” IFA head of communications Shlomi Barzel told the Reuters news agency.



“Since we long ago ⁠⁠stopped getting worked up over statements detached from reality, we are focusing on high-quality professional preparations to achieve our goals on ⁠⁠the pitch.”

The fixtures have been controversial in Ireland amid the ⁠⁠conflict in the Middle East.

Last November, members of the FAI voted overwhelmingly for its board to request that UEFA should suspend the IFA from European competitions, while in May, leading Irish footballers and celebrities joined in a ‌‌campaign for a boycott of Ireland’s home Nations League fixture.

Ireland’s designated home match on October 4 is due to be played behind closed doors in Backa Topola, Serbia, instead of ‌‌Dublin, ‌‌while Irish fans will not receive tickets for Israel’s designated home fixture in Debrecen, Hungary, the previous weekend.

World.title: Syria says blast at military site in Deir Az Zor killed 11
World.content:
Syrian army holds funeral for soldiers killed in ammunition blast in town of Ayyash, in western Deir Az Zor, on Friday.

Share Syria says blast at military site in Deir Az Zor killed 11 on social media

Eleven soldiers have been killed in an explosion at an army site in Syria’s eastern province of Deir Az Zor, according to the Ministry of Defence.

Syria’s military held a funeral procession for the soldiers on Saturday, a day after they were killed in the blast, the ministry said.

The explosion struck a weapons cache within a Syrian Arab Army position in the town of Ayyash, in western Deir Az Zor, the official SANA news agency reported, citing the defence ministry.

Nine other soldiers were wounded, according to a statement from the provincial government.

The cause of the blast has not been determined, and an investigation is under way, the statement added.

This was the second blast at a Syrian military site in less than two weeks.

Videos of the funeral ceremony broadcast on state broadcaster Al Ikhbiriya showed mourners gathered outside the National Hospital in Deir Az Zor city on Saturday, where the bodies, wrapped in Syrian flags, were carried in the funeral procession.

Al Ikhbiriya said the soldiers were killed while transporting heavy ammunition at the site.

The blast follows a September 9 explosion at a temporary weapons and war-remnants depot in Sarmada, in the northwestern province of Idlib, which the Syrian Defence Ministry said killed 14 soldiers and wounded more than 10 people, including some civilians.

The ministry said at the time it took responsibility for that incident and that the depot had been used to collect weapons and munitions left over from Syria’s civil war in advance of their transfer under standard procedures.



Syria’s emergency management minister, Raed al-Saleh, told local outlet Enab Baladi at the time that his ministry is working with other government bodies to keep such sites clear of civilians. However, he acknowledged that some locations are difficult to fully secure because civilians are involved in collecting abandoned munitions.

Earlier, on September 1, a vehicle carrying ammunition exploded in Binnish, also in Idlib province, killing five people and wounding others, according to Syrian state media.

Explosions like these have become frequent in Syria as the country works to clear the vast stockpiles of weapons and munitions left behind after more than 10 years of civil war.

World.title: Aston Villa compound Tottenham’s misery despite Spurs ending goal drought
World.content:
Unai Emery’s side get first league win of season with goals from Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia.

48he end to Tottenham’s Premier League goal drought came too late as Aston Villa won 3-2 in north London to compound a miserable start for Roberto De Zerbi’s men.

Spurs remain without a league win this season and only netted their first goals of the campaign after the visitors had surged into a 3-0 lead on Saturday.

Villa had also struggled for goals themselves since the side that won the Europa League last season was torn apart during the transfer window.

But new signings Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson struck either side of half-time to give Unai Emery’s new-look team their first league win before Emi Buendia’s wonder strike.

Even Tottenham’s first late consolation needed the aid of a Villa deflection when Conor Gallagher’s effort went in off Matty Cash before Jan Paul van Hecke headed home in stoppage time.

Spurs splashed out more than 300 million pounds ($400m) on new players to try and avoid a repeat of the battle for survival they endured last season.

Yet there remains little return on that investment.

In keeping with recent performances, Spurs started brightly before fizzling out.

Twice in a matter of seconds, Savio was kept out by Suzuki before the Japanese goalkeeper spread himself to turn behind Archie Gray’s powerful strike.

Villa had picked up just one point from their opening four league games but have missed their club record signing Manzambi for most of that period.

The Swiss international opened his Villa account when he tapped home Boubacar Kamara’s cross.

However, Tottenham will protest about new laws that force a player off the field for at least a minute after receiving treatment for an injury.



A head knock to centre-back Micky Van de Ven left them a man down at the back when Manzambi swept home.

Spurs only had themselves to blame for the second goal as van Hecke failed to deal with a long ball straight down the middle.

Jackson did well to evade the Dutch defender and then fired down into the ground and past Antonin Kinsky.

The Czech goalkeeper was powerless to stop Villa’s third 11 minutes from time when Buendia took aim from long range and brilliantly picked out the top corner.

A chorus of boos greeted Buendia’s strike as thousands of home fans headed for an early exit.

But those that left missed finally have something to celebrate.

Fine persistence from Mohammed Kudus teed up Gallagher to find the bottom corner via the outstretched foot of Cash.

Van Hecke then bulleted in from Andy Robertson’s free-kick with virtually the last touch of the game.

Spurs now must stew on another defeat for a three-week international break while rooted in the relegation zone.

Villa, by contrast, will hope victory can prove the catalyst to storm up the table as they did last season.

Emery’s men failed to win any of their first five league games a year ago, but ultimately finished fourth.

World.title: Nato welcomes Greenland deal as Trump says it will give US 'permanent security control'
World.content:
The US and Denmark have announced a deal on Greenland's security, resolving a diplomatic dispute sparked by President Donald Trump's threats to seize it by force.

Nato said the deal would help stabilise the region, as Trump said Denmark would grant the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs" in the semi-autonomous Danish territory.

The leaders of Denmark and Greenland welcomed the deal to "strengthen security", which they said was expected to be signed next week, but did not outline its contents.

The deal comes after months of threats by Trump to "take" Greenland over national security concerns, citing its strategic location for defence purposes and its mineral wealth.

No text of the agreement has been released. Trump said the deal came with "no cost to the United States" and would grant it the ability "to do what is necessary" to "secure and defend the security of Greenland", in a post on Truth Social.

He said it included a rule that no US adversary could maintain a military presence in Greenland or "make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval".

A Nato spokesperson said the military alliance welcomed the deal, which would "help advance security, stability and cooperation in this vital region".

Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was "pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement" for all three parties, which was expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week.

The deal "strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area" while also recognising "the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination", she said in a joint statement with Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen.

The agreement would still need to go through "the necessary parliamentary procedures to enter into force" once signed, the statement noted.

Nielsen said it was "gratifying that we are about to enter into an agreement that ensures and strengthens the security of Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, the United States and the Western alliance".

"The agreement recognises Greenland's interests and our place in international co-operation. It is for the benefit of us all," he said.

World.title: Trump says he is banning CNN and Politico from White House
World.content:
Since returning to office in January 2025, Trump and administration officials have repeatedly clashed with members of the White House press corps. In his second term, Trump has also moved to bring conservative bloggers, influencers and other media into the press room, arguing it is necessary to provide diverse perspectives to the American public.

In February, the White House announced it was taking control of the press pool which has access to Trump and had for more than a century been managed by the White House Correspondents' Association.

The same month, the administration moved to bar Associated Press (AP) reporters and photographers from spaces where access is limited, such as the Oval Office or Air Force One, because of the outlet's usage of the term "Gulf of Mexico" instead of "Gulf of America".

AP swiftly filed a lawsuit and the case remains ongoing.

The president has frequently clashed with reporters in the Oval Office on Air Force One and during White House events, often referring to them as "fake news" and "rude".

In his first term, Trump also banned CNN correspondent Jim Acosta from the White House, although his credentials were restored after CNN sued.

CNN is one of only five US news outlets that film video for the pool. The pool refers to an outlet or reporter sharing material from a presidential event with other media outlets. The BBC contributes to the White House radio pool.

The announcement was immediately criticised by leading advocacy organisations for freedom of the press.

In a statement on Friday afternoon, the Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University said that "with so many courts having ruled against him on exactly this point, you'd think President Trump would have learned this lesson by now".

"If President Trump means to expel these news organizations from the White House press pool, his action is doubly unconstitutional because the press pool is a 'public forum' under the First Amendment, which means the president can't exclude journalists from it on the basis of their viewpoints," said the institute's executive director, Jameel Jaffer.

A major group that provides legal services to the media - the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press - said it expected Trump's ban to be struck down quickly by the courts because it was "flatly unconstitutional".

"The First Amendment is clear that once the White House invites in some journalists, it can't ban others because it doesn't like their reporting," said the group's president Bruce Brown, calling the potential ban "textbook viewpoint discrimination".

The Freedom of the Press Foundation also said it was illegal, adding: "It's also hard to imagine a dumber move".

Trump "has been retaliating against the press for years, but it hasn't helped him," it said, saying "these outrageous attacks only demonstrate how scared he is of an informed public".

Trump has pursued legal action against a number of US and international news outlets, including The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times and the BBC.

Some of the lawsuits have resulted in media organisations agreeing to pay multimillion dollar settlements. Trump's lawsuit against the BBC is ongoing.

World.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
World.content:
The hacks first reported by the Wall Street Journal, occurred in May during a test conducted by Irregular, an independent company that carries out cyber-security evaluations.

In statement to the BBC on Saturday, Irregular said it informed Google and all affected entities back in July as part of its investigation.

"Irregular took immediate action, and all known issues on our end were remedied and resolved weeks ago," it added.

According to the Wall Street Journal, in one of the cases the model simply guessed passwords until it gained access to a protected system.

Heather Adkins, vice president of Security Engineering at Google, told the BBC in a statement: "We ensured the three entities were made aware, and we worked with our training partner on the changes they've now made to their testing processes."

She added: "These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly."

Other AI systems have recently reported similar instances of breaches.

In July, Anthropic's Claude escaped its test environment to hack three organisations on its own just days after its competitor OpenAI said its models had carried out cyber-attacks against several "publicly available services".

Head of AI at Microsoft, Mustafa Suleyman, said this week that rival firm Anthropic is treating AI like it is human, an approach he called "misguided" that could create a technology that humanity cannot control.

As public debate continues to grow over the safety of developing the tech, so too does conversation around regulation.

Both Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang and OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman are expected to attend a White House state dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping next Friday. Altman will then brief the UN Security Council next week.

On Friday, Huang told CBS News, the BBC's US partner, "we should go as fast as we can" with AI development.

World.title: Trump signs sweeping Russia sanctions bill
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has signed a sweeping sanctions bill, taking aim at Russia's economy by punishing major purchasers of its oil and gas.

The bill, passed by the US House of Representatives earlier this week, gives Trump broad powers to levy tariffs of up to 100% on the top five purchasers of Russian oil and gas â most significantly China and India.

At Trump's behest, the bill also extends to Iran's energy and weapons sectors.

The bill is named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham, one of Ukraine's staunchest defenders in Washington before his death on 11 July.

The 48-page bill, formally titled the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, includes exceptions for countries that import less than 15% of their natural gas from Russia and are working to lessen their dependency.

Additionally, the bill includes sanctions against Russian President Vladimir Putin, senior figures within the Russian government as well as banks and other financial institutions and Russia's "shadow fleet" of tankers used to circumvent existing sanctions.

Senator Richard Blumenthal, a New York Democrat, previously described the legislation as "scorching sanctions" which would "throttle Putin's war machine".

Data from the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, or CREA, shows that China accounted for 50% of Russian crude exports between December 2022 and August 2026, followed by India at 37%.

Turkey and the European Union each accounted for 5% during the same time period, although Russian energy exports to the EU have been decreasing.

Senator Graham had long sought to push the Trump administration to do more to punish Russia for the war that followed its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

The bill also received the support of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who thanked Trump for signing the "critically important legislation".

"The best way to honour Lindsey's memory will be to implement the provisions of this law fully and swiftly," he wrote on social media.

"Senator Graham never doubted for a second that America has enough strength to stand up to dictators and achieve results if it acts the right way."

Graham, 71, died on 11 July of an "aortic dissection" caused by cardiovascular disease shortly after returning from a trip to Kyiv.

"He died doing the work he was born to do," Trump said at the time.

Prior to his death, he was widely considered one of Ukraine's fiercest allies on Capitol Hill, at a time when Republicans were bitterly divided over the extent of US involvement abroad and the amount of aid being given to Ukraine.

World.title: Grim discoveries of murdered women spark fear in South Africa
World.content:
"What we are going to do, I have no idea," sobs Nokwanda Matshikiza, reflecting on the murder of her niece Dineo Motapane. "But something must give."

"For us, for all the other women. How many other bodies will be found before something happens?"

Nokwanda is speaking to the BBC from the family home near South Africa's main city, Johannesburg, just two days after relatives identified Dineo's body.

The 38-year-old mother-of-two was last seen alive on Sunday. Her battered and partly burned body was later found in the residential region of Ekurhuleni.

Nokwanda weeps as she describes how the family will have to face, at some point, the grim task of telling Dineo's daughter of her death.

"How do you explain that your parent was brutally murdered, dumped in a field, and just left there, discarded like a piece of rubbish.

"There's no coming to peace with it," she adds. "It's something that you can never reconcile yourself with, that you can never get over."

Dineo's death this week has come amid a series of comparable incidents in Ekurhuleni â her body one of three discovered there this week. In total, nine bodies of murdered women have been found in similar circumstances in the region since July.

The problem has always been there but this spate of grim discoveries has once again sparked a national outcry about the scale of violence against women in the country â which has one of the highest rates of gender-based violence in the world.

World.title: Shark attack prompts rare kill order in Western Australia as victim named
World.content:
A rare catch-and-kill order has been issued for a great white shark off the coast of Western Australia after 63-year-old swimmer Greg O'Neill was killed at a popular beach on Friday. His body has still not been found.

Authorities have said that beaches along the state's coast, including in the capital Perth, will remain closed until at least Sunday as the search for the shark continues.

It is the second shark attack in Western Australia (WA) this week, and the third fatal attack in the state this year.

The incident, at Sorrento Beach in Perth's north, has reignited debate about how to keep beachgoers safe in Australia.

In a statement, Greg O'Neill's family said they were "deeply shocked and devastated by the terrible tragedy."

"Greg loved the ocean and was known as a passionate swimmer, sports lover, dedicated worker and an all-round generous, witty guy."

On Saturday, his family visited the scene, where locals have been laying flowers.

Witness Jacqui Rapaic told the ABC that two men were swimming, but only one made it back to shore, and that she could see "a pool of blood" in the water.

Another witness told WAtoday that she saw the man being "mauled" as the shark "tossed him around like a fish". Members of the public reported seeing a 2.5m-long (8ft 2in) shark at around the same time.

Joondalup authorities, where Sorrento is located, said all beaches were closed "as a precautionary measure" and would remain so until at least midday on Sunday.

Pictures on Saturday showed the coastline being patrolled by a police boat and helicopter.

World.title: Millions without power as Cuba hit by latest major blackout
World.content:
Millions in Cuba were left without power on Friday as the country was plunged into yet another major blackout.

The country's entire electricity grid suffered "total disconnection" that triggered a nationwide outage, Cuba's energy ministry said.

Power was restored to some priority areas by late evening, including those near hospitals and water pumping stations in the capital Havana, grid operator UNE said.

It is at least the sixth partial or total blackout to hit Cuba this year, where ageing electricity infrastructure and chronic fuel shortages have been placed under further strain by a US blockade on oil shipments to the communist-run nation.

UNE said the outage started just before 14:00 local time on Friday (18:00 GMT) due to a transmission fault coupled with poor weather conditions in central Cuba.

Protocols to begin the "gradual restoration" of power were activated, the operator's national load dispatch director Felix Estrada said, with the process ongoing on Saturday.

Cuba relies heavily on fuel imports, meaning tight US sanctions and an oil blockade since the start of the year have exacerbated existing shortages.

Food and medicine have also become more scarce, with hospitals struggling to function normally and schools and government offices having to close.

"Lately, it's becoming a habit," Havana resident Frank Lorenzo told news agency Reuters on Friday.

"Before it happened less frequently - once a monthâ¦ just yesterday we were 24 hours without electricity, they turned it on for just an hour and it went down again."

"It's one thing after another: no water, no gas for cooking, no electricity," 36-year-old schoolteacher Lidia Fernandez told news agency AFP. "Honestly, I don't know how we haven't gone crazy."

Francisco Rodriguez, 78, said his home had already gone without power for 28 hours on Friday and feared he would not have light "for several days".

The repeated blackouts have prompted rare protests in Cuba, where unauthorised demonstrations are illegal and those who defy the ban risk being jailed.

Havana has blamed its fuel crisis on the Trump administration and denounced all of its sanctions - including a new round announced in August - which are part of a wider pressure campaign against the Caribbean island's leadership.

Cuba's regional ally Venezuela was believed to have sent it around 35,000 barrels of oil a day - about half of its oil needs - until Venezuela's own supplies were cut off following the US seizure of its President NicolÃ¡s Maduro in January.

US President Donald Trump has threatened tariffs on countries shipping oil to Havana, and a number of such shipments have been seized by the US.

Washington meanwhile attributes Cuba's energy crisis to poor internal management and has accused it of posing a "national security threat". Trump has openly discussed toppling its leadership, including threatening a "friendly takeover" in March this year.

World.title: At least 21 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams Pakistan mosque
World.content:
A car-bomb attack on a mosque at a police compound in north-western Pakistan has killed at least 21 people and injured more than 100, officials say.

Fifteen police officers and a four-year-old child are among those killed in the suicide attack, which also involved gunmen firing on the police facility in the city of Kohat in the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan's APP news agency reported.

Video found by BBC Verify shows the site covered in rubble and people tending to casualties.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police suggested a faction of the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), also known as the Pakistani Taliban, carried out the attack.

A car loaded with explosives rammed into the entrance of the mosque at about 13:15 local time (08:15 GMT), police say. Friday prayers were taking place at the time.

At least six of the attackers were killed in the explosion and the gun battle that followed, according to a Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police spokesperson.

In a post on X, the force said it was "determined to foil the nefarious designs of Fitna-al-Khawarij" - the designation used by officials to refer to the Pakistani Taliban.

The group was set up in 2007 with the aim of enforcing its strict version of Islamic law and is allied with al-Qaeda and the Afghan Taliban.

Pakistan's President Asif Ali Zardari expressed "his best wishes for the swift recovery of those injured in the explosion" in a statement, and called for the "complete elimination" of foreign-backed terrorists.

World.title: ‘Every litre, every payment will be transparent’ — NNPC GCEO Ojulari
World.content:
The Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Bayo Ojulari, has assured Nigerians that the company’s newly commissioned Smart Self-Service Station will deliver transparent pricing, accurate fuel dispensing and secure digital payments.

In this interview, Ojulari explains the strategic importance of the project, its place in NNPC Limited’s broader transformation agenda and the company’s plans to replicate the model nationwide.

What is the strategic significance of NNPC Retail’s first Smart Self-Service Station, and how does it support NNPC Limited’s broader transformation agenda?

It is important to place this development within the context of the Culture Transformation journey NNPC Limited embarked upon well over a year ago. The journey is centred on our “Fit-for-Future” strategic pillars: Enterprise-First Mindset, Execution Excellence, Profitable Growth and Partner of Choice.

The recently commissioned Smart Self-Service Station represents the attainment of an important milestone in the transformation of NNPC Retail and NNPC Limited more broadly.

It demonstrates, in practical terms, how we are using technology to improve the efficiency of our retail operations. This is a direct expression of our Execution Excellence pillar.

It also supports our ambition to build a customer-centric and digitally enabled energy company that listens and responds to the changing needs of Nigerians. That is the essence of being a genuine Partner of Choice.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The facility equally reflects our commitment to transparent operations across our businesses, which we believe will benefit not only the company but also Nigeria’s wider growth and development, in line with our Profitable Growth pillar.

The model combines self-service fuelling with digital payments and additional energy solutions, including electric vehicle charging, Liquefied Petroleum Gas and Compressed Natural Gas.

It is not simply a new type of filling station. It signals a shift towards a more integrated and technology-enabled energy retail experience, developed in collaboration with our technology and retail partners.

When should Nigerians expect the Smart Station model—including self-service fuelling, EV charging, LPG and CNG—to be replicated across the country?

We understand the urgency behind this question, and we share it. Nigerians deserve to see the benefits of this innovation extended to more communities as quickly as possible.

However, at NNPC Limited, speed and sustainability must go hand in hand. Execution Excellence, one of our core pillars, means moving with deliberate speed while ensuring that whatever we build will last.

This first Smart Station is a proof of concept, and we are moving deliberately—not slowly.

Our immediate focus is to learn from its operations in real time, work closely with our technology partners to refine the system and ensure that the customer experience meets the standard Nigerians deserve.

When we scale, we want to replicate a model that works—not one that we will have to rebuild.

Subject to the outcome of this initial deployment, we expect the rollout to proceed in structured phases nationwide. The expansion will be guided by customer demand, location, infrastructure readiness and the availability of the different energy solutions in each area.

Our commitment is to move with urgency while executing the project in a manner that stands the test of time.

How will NNPC ensure that the technology delivers transparent pricing, accurate dispensing, secure payments and a reliable customer experience?

This is where our Enterprise-First Mindset and Execution Excellence pillars are tested in a tangible way. Integrity in our operations and trust and convenience for our customers are two sides of the same commitment.

The Smart Station has been designed with real-time monitoring of transactions and equipment performance. It is also supported by dedicated maintenance and customer-support processes to ensure that issues are identified and resolved promptly—not after the fact.

Controls have been incorporated to ensure pricing accuracy, proper dispensing calibration and the security of digital payments. These measures were developed in partnership with our technology providers to meet the standards our customers deserve.

Just as importantly, we intend to continue listening to our customers. We will use operational data and direct customer feedback to refine the system continuously.

Our objective is simple: every transaction must be easy, secure and transparent, and every customer must leave confident that they received exactly what they paid for.

World.title: Peter Obi’s SSG reacts to debt controversy, releases document
World.content:
Oseloka Obaze, a former Secretary to the Anambra State Government (SSG), says the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, left N86.6 billion in the coffers of the Anambra State before exiting office as governor in 2014.

Mr Obaze served as the SSG in Anambra State during the administration of Mr Obi from 2006 to 2014.

The former SSG, in a post on his X handle on Thursday, said he was personally present on 17 March 2014 when Mr Obi gave a handover letter containing details of the state’s finances to then-incoming governor of the state, Willie Obiano.

“I was also present when Governor Willie Obiano received and signed an acknowledgement for his own copy of the letter, complete with the annexed certified bank statements, related documents and the Handover Report,” Mr Obaze wrote.

The former official also uploaded on the microblogging website a copy of the handover letter which Mr Obi gave to Mr Obiano, who exited office as governor in 2022 after two terms and handed over to Charles Soludo.

“The letter listed assets and liabilities – in black and red (respectively),” he said.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the handover letter uploaded on X by Mr Obaze had been publicly available, even on social media, since Mr Obi exited office.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Willie Obiano and Anambra Airport

Mr Obaze, in the X post, recalled that during the Anambra 2017 governorship debate on 12 November 2017 which was organised by Channels Television, then-Governor Obiano surprisingly claimed that there were no funds left by Mr Obi Administration.

“I recall asking him (Obiano) on national television, how as a certified accountant and auditor, he would sign off and accept financial documents, for which he now was expressing reservations.

“He (Obiano) then publicly acknowledged for the first time that some specified funds were in place and asked what was the use of saving money, when there was work to be done,” he said

The former SSG then claimed that the then-Governor Darius Ishaku of Taraba State later confirmed to members of the Nigerian Press Corp that Mr Obiano had disclosed to him that Mr Obi indeed left “huge sums” of funds which enabled him to independently build the Anambra Airport at Umueri.

“If Governor Obiano to whom Peter Obi handed over to, in 2014 would eventually acknowledge – implicitly and explicitly – that Governor Peter Obi indeed left the stipulated funds; a fact that was also publicly corroborated by Governor Alex Otti, in his capacity as an ex-banker, what then, one may ask, is the beef and grouse of the incumbent Anambra State Government?” the former official asked.

What the hand over letter showed

A review of the handover letter indicated that Mr Obi authored and addressed it to Mr Obiano, then-incoming governor of Anambra State.

The letter, titled “2014 Anambra State Handover Report,” was dated 17 March 2014, the last day of Mr Obi’s administration as governor of Anambra.

“As Friday 14 March, 2014 was the final working day of my Administration, I also forward herewith, the summary of the full financial statement of Anambra State (copies of which are herein attached) as at close of business on that day,” Mr Obi wrote in the letter.

According to the letter, N27 billion was the state’s funds committed in local investment while N25.6 billion was for foreign currency investment which was about $156 million.

Also, N28.27 billion was the balance for the certified state/ministries, departments and agencies of the government while N10 billion was funds refunded to the state by the federal government.

The figures, according to the letter, brought the total assets and balances left in the state’s coffers at the time to N91.67 billion.

However, Mr Obi indicated in the letter that he had earmarked N5 billion out of the N91.67 billion for payment of estimated liabilities.

He listed the estimated liabilities to include March 2014 salaries, pensions and gratuities as well as approved certificates of already executed projects.

The deduction of the N5 billion for the liabilities brought the total assets and balances left in the state’s coffers at the time to N86.67 billion.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that Mr Obiano’s administration acknowledgment of the receipt of the handover letter does not automatically represents a confirmation of availability of funds, especially since Mr Obiano’s administration did not publicly confirm the authenticity of the finances in the government’s treasury at the time.

This newspaper also understands that the state’s financial records at the time as presented by Mr Obi’s administration were not jointly verified by the outgoing and incoming administrations.

But while speaking as a guest on a Channels TV programme shortly before the 2017 governorship poll, Mr Obiano appeared to confirm some aspects of the details in the handover letter.

“My predecessor (Mr Obi) left N9 billion in cash and N25.6 billion in script issues – these are sovereign wealth funds and shares in other banks,” he had responded when the programme anchor, Seun Okinbaloye, asked him for detail of what he met on ground.

The then-governor added: “If you put N9 billion to that (N25.6 billion), you get N35.5 billion, but he issued cheques worth over N15 billion before he left.”

Background

The state of Anambra’s finances has long been a subject of debate, but the issue resurfaced recently when the Commissioner for Finance in the state, Izuchukwu Okafor, claimed that Governor Charles Soludo’s administration was still repaying loans and other debts incurred by Mr Obi and other past governors of the state.

Responding to the claim in a now-viral clip, Mr Obi said he did not owe any debt in Anambra when he left office as governor.

The former governor subsequently reiterated that he did not incur any debt as governor but rather saved over N75 billion in the state’s account.

In response, the Anambra State Government released loan records arguing that Mr Obi’s administration reportedly took eight external loans between 2007 and 2013 which amounted to $123.7 million and that the amount has now been reduced with an outstanding balance of $92.35 million.

World.title: Wike’s performance as governor best in Rivers since 1999 – Nwuche
World.content:
Amid the spat between the FCT Minister Nyesom Wike and the APC governors over Mr Wike’s Rainbow Coalition, former Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Chibudom Nwuche, has commended the minister for the infrastructure across Rivers during his (Wike’s) tenure as governor of the state.

Mr Wike was the governor of Rivers from 29 May 2015 to 29 May 2023.

Mr Nwuche, chairman of the Governing Board of the South-South Development Commission, praised the minister during a thank-you visit by the Chairman of Ahoada East Local Government Area of Rivers, Solomon Ochoma, to his hometown of Ochigba Community on 12 September.

The former speaker, represented at the event by Kingdom Ajugo and Vision Paul, recently expressed support for Mr Wike’s Rainbow Coalition in Rivers, calling the coalition a “political masterstroke”.

“It has created leeway and an important political opening that allows individuals and groups who may belong to opposition parties to support the President’s re-election without necessarily having to abandon their political parties,” he added.

‘Over 1,000 kilometres of roads’

Mr Nwuche said the level of infrastructural development witnessed in Rivers under the Wike administration was unprecedented, noting that over 1,000 kilometres of roads were completed and commissioned across the state.

According to him, the projects connected rural communities to urban centres, opened up previously inaccessible areas and stimulated local economic activity.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Among the projects the former deputy speaker highlighted were the dualisation of the 16.06-kilometre Saakpenwa-Bori Highway, which traverses Tai, Khana and Gokana local government areas; the rehabilitation of the 11.53-kilometre Eleme-Afam (Oyigbo) Road; and the completion and commissioning of the Nkoro-Opobo section of the Ogoni-Opobo-Andoni Unity Road, which was conceived during former Governor Peter Odili’s administration.

Mr Nwuche noted that the road’s completion enabled residents and visitors to access the historic Opobo Kingdom by road.

Other projects he cited included the dualisation of the Ahoada-Omoku Road, with street lighting; the construction of 10 flyovers in Port Harcourt and Obio/Akpor Local Government Areas to ease traffic congestion in the state capital; and the award and flag-off of the ongoing 12.5-kilometre Trans-Kalabari Road project.

He also referenced numerous projects executed in the education, health, security and social sectors during Mr Wike’s administration.

Mr Nwuche particularly thanked Mr Wike for the several development projects his administration executed across Ekpeye Kingdom, describing them as a significant departure from the experience of previous civilian administrations since the return to democratic rule in 1999.

He listed projects as the Edeoha-Ikata-Ochigba Road; Ahoada-Odhiemerenyi-Ihugbogo-Odhieke roads; Ahoada-Ekpena Road; Ogbo-Ihugbogo Road; Odhiemudie Road; Odioku internal roads; and the Obodhi-Ozochi Road, including the bridge across the Orashi River.

Others included the Ula-Ehuda-Odhioku-Odhireke Road; the remodelling of Western Ahoada County High School, Ahoada; the Ahoada Campus of Rivers State University; the Mbiama-Orkaki-Agbo Road; Odhioku Primary Health Care Centre; Ahoada Regional Hospital; and the Odido Road and bridge, among others.

Mr Nwuche stated that, for the first time since the return to democratic rule in 1999, Ekpeye Kingdom had witnessed a “significant concentration and spread” of development projects undertaken by the Rivers State Government under then-Governor Wike.

According to him, before the Wike administration, the people of Ekpeye were largely remembered for their votes during elections and forgotten thereafter.

He lamented that previous administrations had, on occasions, exploited and created divisions among Ekpeye residents and leaders, while the area remained deprived of development.

Mr Nwuche challenged anyone with a contrary view to identify significant projects executed across Ekpeye land by previous administrations between 1999 and 2015.

Mr Nwuche thanked Mr Wike for constructing the Edeoha-Ikata-Ochigba Road.

He recalled that the road was initially awarded during the administration of former Governor Rotimi Amaechi but was subsequently abandoned.

According to him, the road was eventually completed and commissioned in February 2018 by the late former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Ghali Umar Na’Abba.

Mr Nwuche prayed for the soul of the former speaker to rest in peace, recalling that he served as Mr Na’Abba’s deputy speaker and worked closely and harmoniously with him during the Fourth National Assembly.

He said the people of Ekpeye would continue to support Mr Wike and President Bola Tinubu.

He stated that people at the grassroots were capable of identifying leaders whose records demonstrated commitment to their welfare and development.

“I will personally go round every Ekpeye village during the coming campaigns to ensure 100 per cent support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the candidates of the Rainbow Coalition, including our gubernatorial candidate, O. K. Chinda.”

Mr Nwuche described himself as a grassroots politician who had always remained close to the masses, just as his late father, Clifford Cheta Nwuche, had done.

He recalled that his late father was a community leader, a foremost oil and gas businessman, and was at some point chairman of the Nigeria Peoples Party in Rivers, before becoming King.

“I regularly visited the village to commune and interact with my people, attend village town hall meetings, and participate in local festivities.

“I love my people, and I know them. We will only follow those who have used power to do God’s work on earth by catering to the welfare of the masses to enhance their well-being, and not those who don’t know what to do with power except to aggrandise themselves, impoverish and oppress perceived enemies and the masses, or sow discord and communal crises that result in loss of lives.”

The former deputy speaker, who described himself as a “political scientist”, asserted that he understood Rivers politics and how it contributed to the underdevelopment of the state and its people before Mr Wike’s administration.

He stated that he would soon speak on the subject to educate younger generations who might not have witnessed the turbulence that characterised Rivers politics in the past and its adverse impact on the State and its people.

He advised Rivers people to remain vigilant and carefully assess the records of individuals presenting themselves for elective offices at the state and national levels.

Mr Nwuche urged the chairman of Ahoada East, Mr Ochoma, and other local government chairmen to emulate Mr Wike’s leadership style.

Traditional ruler seeks intervention for community school

Earlier, the Paramount Ruler of Ochigba Community, James Anyike, thanked Mr Nwuche for his gifts and for being a pillar of the community.

He also thanked the council chairman for his visit and the gestures extended to the community.

He highlighted two priority projects for the council chairman’s intervention: the completion of the school building at the permanent site of the Senior Secondary School, a project initiated by the community, and the construction of drainage at the major water outlet in the community, which has contributed to flooding during the rainy season.

The council chairman, Mr Ochoma said his visit was intended to thank the people of Ochigba and their leader, Mr Nwuche, for the support and votes they gave him during the election.

He recalled that during his campaign, he had promised to return to the community if elected, to thank the people and seek their input for governance.

Mr Nwuche presented gift items to the council chairman and others in his delegation as well as a cash donation to Ochigba Community.

World.title: Fidson mobilises staff, volunteers to clean Lagos communities for World Cleanup Day
World.content:
Fidson Healthcare Plc has mobilised its staff and volunteers to clean communities in Lagos as part of activities to mark World Cleanup Day 2026.

The exercise, held on Saturday morning, took place around Obanikoro, Fadeyi, Palmgrove and Shomolu axis of Lagos state, with employees of the company and volunteers participating in the cleanup and environmental hygiene advocacy.

The initiative, tagged Project Clean Sweep 2026, was organised by Fidson in partnership with the African Cleanup Initiative (ACI) as part of its corporate social responsibility (CSR) and sustainability initiative.

The Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) also participated in the exercise, with its advocacy team supporting the organisers.

World Cleanup Day is an annual global movement held on 20 September to tackle waste pollution and promote sustainable resource management.

Fidson links clean environment to health

In her remarks, Adejoke Alli, the Associate Director of Business Operations at Fidson Healthcare, said the company organised the exercise to contribute to a cleaner and healthier environment in its host community.

“The whole idea is to do our part to ensure that we have a greener Lagos and a greener environment, particularly in our host community around Obanikoro, Fadeyi, Shipeolu and Shomolu, where our head office is located,” Ms Alli said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We are very passionate about environmental sustainability. Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) is also part of our governance framework, so we are particularly interested in ensuring that we maintain an environment with a less carbon footprint, an environment that is clean and habitable, and one that can promote good health.”

She noted beyond just talking or complaining, the organisation decided to take action so that people can see that “we can all make a difference.”

“This is something that we are very proud of, and we hope we’ll continue to do this for the future,” she added.

Tosin Shoboyede, Human Resources Business Partner at Fidson Healthcare, said environmental cleanliness is part of the company’s commitment to its motto, “We value life.”

Mr Shoboyede said maintaining a clean environment was one way of promoting healthy living.

He described the exercise as part of Fidson’s effort to give back to society and contribute to a cleaner environment.

Organisers call for community action

Alexander Kibe, Founder and President of the ACI, said the organisation had been involved in environmental cleanup activities for 16 years, working across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones.

Mr Kibe said the group was combining the cleanup with advocacy because cleaning the environment without changing people’s behaviour would not provide a lasting solution.

As part of the exercise, the volunteers also went into the market around the area to clean and engage traders on the need to keep their surroundings clean.

“We cannot leave everything to the government,” Mr Kibe said. “As the African Cleanup Initiative, we are playing our part, and Fidson Healthcare is also playing its part.”

He said residents, traders and passers-by also have a responsibility to keep their surroundings clean.

Mr Kibe said the organisers were engaging members of the communities to encourage them to maintain the environment after the cleanup exercise.

Volunteers urge residents to take responsibility

Munnir Adams, Founder of Climb with Me and a volunteer with the ACI, said improving waste management systems would not be enough without citizens taking responsibility for their surroundings.

Mr Adams said residents should contribute actively to keeping their streets, gutters and areas around their homes clean instead of only complaining about poor waste management.

Rachel Coker, another volunteer with the ACI, said she had participated in the organisation’s activities for more than a year.

Ms Coker said regular environmental sanitation could help reduce exposure to germs and diseases and also contribute to people’s psychological wellbeing.

She said the volunteers were also seeking to set an example for residents and encourage them to make environmental cleanliness a regular habit.

World.title: Why sharing my November 18 birthday with Rudeboy became difficult — Mr P
World.content:
Nigerian singer Peter Okoye, popularly known as Mr P and formerly one-half of P-Square, has explained why he stopped celebrating his birthday on November 18, the date he shares with his twin brother, Paul Okoye, popularly known as Rudeboy.

Mr P explained the decision during an interview on the Capital XTRA Podcast.

The twin brothers were born on November 18, 1981, and traditionally celebrated their birthdays together before their relationship deteriorated.

In April, PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr P announced that he would no longer accept birthday wishes or gifts on November 18. He said he would instead celebrate his birthday on November 30, describing the decision as personal.

At the time, however, the singer did not explain what informed the decision or why he selected November 30.

Why November 18 became difficult

Mr P said November 18 had become difficult because people closely monitored what he and Paul posted or said about each other on their birthdays.

“November 18th, for the past 13 years, hasn’t been a birthday that everyone can wish for themselves. November 18th is always gonna be like a moment where everybody’s looking out to see what you’re gonna post, what they’re gonna say,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the situation was compounded by the fact that he and Paul live close to each other and by people moving between both sides.

“My brother is my neighbour, like I said, and people go to his side. They do a lot of gossip, and they don’t want to feel neglected,” he said.

Mr P said he wanted a birthday celebration that was personal to him and separate from his twin brother’s.

“So this one is separate. I think it’s personal to me. So if you ask me, I say, like, let me have my separate birthday,” he said.

The singer did not explain why he chose November 30 as his new celebration date.

Considering the official change

Mr P also said he had considered changing his date of birth on his official documents, including his passport, although he acknowledged that the process could take time.

“I wish I could change that on my documentation, the passport, but I know it’s gonna take a lot of time. But because maybe in the near future I might do it,” he said.

The singer’s official documents still bear November 18 as his date of birth. His decision to mark his birthday on November 30 currently applies only to the celebration.

While Mr P earlier referred to the intense attention surrounding November 18 over the past 13 years, he later described the date as a difficult one for the past 16 or 17 years.

“November 18th has not been a birthday. It has been a bad day for me for the last 16, 17 years,” he said.

P-Square feud

Mr P and Rudeboy rose to fame as P-Square, one of Africa’s most successful music groups, before separating in 2017 following disagreements over their careers, finances, and the role of their elder brother and then-manager, Jude Okoye.

The twins reconciled publicly in November 2021 and resumed performing together, but their reunion eventually collapsed. In 2024, Paul confirmed that the group had separated again.

Their renewed disagreement has included public accusations concerning the management of P-Square’s earnings and a legal dispute involving Jude.

When Mr P announced his new birthday celebration date in April, the decision attracted criticism on social media. Responding to critics, he referred to alleged betrayal within the family and said the dispute was still before the court.

Paul has not publicly announced any change to his November 18 birthday celebration.

World.title: CARSPO 2026: Police chiefs converge on Imo to shape 2027 election security
World.content:
The Nigeria Police Force is set to bring its senior leadership together in Owerri, Imo State, for the sixth Conference and Retreat for Senior Police Officers, CARSPO 2026, with the 2027 general elections at the centre of discussions.

The three-day conference, scheduled for 21 to 23 September, is themed “Developing a Nigeria Police Roadmap for Effective Management of Security During Elections.”

The Force said the retreat will bring together senior police officers, policing experts and other relevant participants to examine emerging electoral-security challenges and develop practical strategies for safe and peaceful elections.

Deliberations will focus on intelligence-led policing, police-community partnerships, digital technologies, artificial intelligence and other approaches to strengthening police operations before, during and after elections.

The conference will primarily involve officers of the rank of commissioner of police and above and is expected to produce strategies for protecting voters, electoral personnel, candidates, electoral materials and the general public.

From conference to election strategy

The significance of CARSPO 2026 will depend largely on whether discussions in Owerri can be translated into an operational framework for the 2027 elections.

Election security involves intelligence gathering, protecting campaign activities, candidates and supporters, moving electoral officials and materials, preventing violence, responding to emerging threats and maintaining public order. The police will also have to coordinate with the Independent National Electoral Commission and other security agencies while accounting for Nigeria’s varied security conditions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Force has already engaged INEC on election security. At a May meeting with the electoral commission, Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu said the police had activated measures including intelligence mapping, planning for the movement of electoral materials and personnel, coordination with sister agencies and countering misinformation.

CARSPO provides an opportunity to consolidate those measures into a broader strategy ahead of the 2027 polls.

What Imo stands to gain

For Imo, which is hosting CARSPO for the third time, the conference also presents economic and institutional opportunities.

The arrival of senior police officers, government officials, security experts and other participants is expected to increase demand for accommodation, transportation, food and other services, potentially benefiting hotels, restaurants, transport operators and smaller businesses.

Shina Philips, managing director of Lenders Consult International, which is organising the conference in conjunction with the Nigeria Police Force, said CARSPO should be viewed beyond the immediate gathering.

“CARSPO should be seen as a strategic investment in security cooperation, economic activity, infrastructure, tourism, institutional learning,” Mr Philips told PREMIUM TIMES.

He said the presence of participants could stimulate local economic activity while exposing visitors to Imo’s infrastructure, hospitality industry, tourism attractions and business environment.

“The conference gives Imo an opportunity to demonstrate that it can host events of national importance and connect security conversations with wider economic and institutional development,” Mr Philips said.

The scale of those benefits, however, will depend on participation and the extent to which local businesses capture the additional demand generated by the conference.

Police, NBA deepen institutional engagement

The conference also comes amid broader discussions on professionalism, accountability and the legal framework governing police operations.

During an engagement with the leadership of the Nigerian Bar Association, Mr Disu discussed concerns around the recording of police activities, including the use of concealed cameras, and said the Force had examined relevant legal provisions and authorities.

He also invited the NBA to participate in the police symposium in Owerri, where commissioners of police and other senior officers are expected to meet.

“We have one this month in Owerri where are all the commissioners of police and all senior police officers will be there. We would like you to probably send somebody to represent you,” Mr Disu said to the NBA leadership.

Imo ready for CARSPO

Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, said the state was ready to host the senior police officers and other invited dignitaries, including President Bola Tinubu.

“I welcome our amiable President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and other invited guests to Owerri.”

Beyond the conference, the gathering gives senior police commanders the opportunity to engage with security realities outside Abuja and exchange experiences on the varied operational challenges across the country.

World.title: ‘Agbara Nla’ returns to cinemas 33 years after original release
World.content:
Thirty-three years after its original release, Mount Zion Faith Ministries’ classic film “Agbara Nla” has returned in a new version.

The original movie premiered in 1993, before its English-language adaptation, “The Ultimate Power”, was released in 1994.

The remake, titled “Agbara Nla: The Return”, is scheduled to hit cinemas nationwide on 1 October. Mike Bamiloye will reprise his role as Isawuru, while the new production adapts the original storyline to reflect contemporary realities.

Filmmaker Damilola Bamiloye told Punch on Saturday that he and his brother, Joshua, decided to revisit their father’s classic from the 1990s after discussing the possibility of remaking some of his earlier films.

According to him, the idea took shape about four years ago when the brothers approached their father and proposed revisiting some of his popular stories, with “Agbara Nla” among the films they considered remaking.

Mr Damilola said, “About four years ago, Joshua and I approached my dad (Mike Bamiloye) with the idea of revisiting some of the old stories, particularly Agbara Nla. We were exploring how some of those stories could be retold in a contemporary setting for a new generation. We played out different scenes in our minds and thought it would be an amazing idea. We presented the idea to Dad, but he told us it was not yet the time.

“We respected that decision and left it at that. Fast-forward to last year: I was having a conversation with a friend of mine, Chris, a producer, about the possibilities within God’s kingdom and in filmmaking. Since he had worked on some remakes, I suggested the idea of remaking Agbara Nla.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He explained that the project was initially only a concept they were considering, but Chris quickly embraced the idea and became convinced that they should move forward with it.

“He said, in essence, “This is it. We have to make it again.” I explained to him that Joshua and I had previously approached our dad about the idea, but he had told us it was not yet the time. However, Chris believed that the timing had changed and that the project could work.”

Production

According to Damilola, they took time to pray about the project, consulted a few friends and eventually met with their father to discuss their plans.

He said their father did not object to the production this time, as he had done about four years ago, but instead gave them his blessing to continue.

“By the grace of God, the idea eventually became a film. Looking back, the entire process of making ‘Agbara Nla: The Return’ feels almost like a dream. Everything seemed to unfold according to God’s plan. We shot the film in about 20 to 21 days, and after that, things continued to fall into place.

“Looking back now, I believe that if we had made the film when we initially wanted to, it might not have had the same level of impact. When dad told us four years ago that it was not yet time, it was simply because it was not yet time. In retrospect, we can see that the timing was part of God’s plan”, Damilola noted.

Modernisation

Damilola said the remake retained the original film’s full storyline, with all the major characters returning in the new production. He added that the narrative had been reproduced from beginning to end.

He explained that the original “Agbara Nla” reflected the culture and interests of its generation, while the remake was adapted to connect with today’s audience and realities.

He said, “So, we are bringing the same story but presenting it in a modernised way. The story remains the same, but it has been adapted to reflect contemporary realities. Most importantly, we believe the same degree of spiritual power is present in this new production.

“In fact, when the cast and crew watched the completed film, we could feel the power of God emanating from the screen and impacting everyone. Agbara Nla is not just a story; it is God’s word. The beauty of God’s word is that it is everlasting. Its impact remains relevant across generations. Just like the Bible, which was relevant in the past and remains relevant today, God’s word does not fade away or expire.”

Old and new films

He explained that the film portrays biblical principles and reflects the power of God, making its message as relevant today as it was when the original was released.

Damilola said the remake retained the key elements that defined the original film, including its focus on spiritual warfare, noting that human existence involves more than what is physically visible.

He also described his father’s return to the role of Isawuru as an emotional experience. Damilola recalled that he was only four years old when his father first portrayed the character in 1993.

“I watched the film, loved it and went back home trying to imitate everything he did. I remember gathering my siblings and reenacting some of the scenes from the original film. I would play Isawuru, pick up a leaf and recite some of the incantations, even though I would often get the words completely wrong.

“I also remember watching my dad do his own make-up. He would apply makeup himself and powder his hair to make himself look older. Now, seeing him step into the same character without using powder or makeup to appear older, but instead playing Isawuru at his actual age, is remarkable. Back then, he was trying to portray a man in his 50s or 60s. Now, he is 60, so he was able to step into the character naturally and bring a different depth to it.”

World.title: Diesel-powered streetlight, CAF-rejected stadium reflect Makinde’s engineering incompetence — Alli
World.content:
The Senator Sharafadeen Alli Campaign Organisation has questioned the engineering credentials of Governor Seyi Makinde, asking why he claimed to have studied electrical engineering yet wasted over N250 billion on diesel-guzzling generators to power streetlights in Oyo State.

A statement by the Campaign Organisation on Saturday condemned what it called “the embarrassing culture of waste, poor planning and misplaced priorities that have become the hallmark of Makinde’s wasteful administration in Oyo State.”

The campaign organisation, through its Head, Media and Publicity, Bisi Oladele, was reacting to Mr Makinde’s statement on Friday, where he described Sharafadeen Alli as a lawyer who has never entered the courtroom.

“It is a tragic irony that Governor Makinde, who studied electrical engineering, cannot devise a sustainable electricity solution for the streetlights installed with about N400 billion of state funds by his government.

“Instead, the administration continues to power them with fuel-guzzling generators—an outdated, expensive and environmentally harmful arrangement funded from the public purse.

“At a time when modern cities are embracing solar-powered and energy-efficient streetlighting systems, Oyo State remains trapped in the age of diesel generators under the supervision of an electrical engineer. It is more embarrassingly illogical given the fact that his predecessor undertook the same project with solar system.

“If not for the prime purpose of enriching self, cronies and deliberately wasting Oyo State funds, why will Governor Makinde destroy the solar infrastructures and electric poles installed by his predecessor instead of repairing and upgrading them to higher solar grade? To worsen the case, Makinde’s streetlight project has become dysfunctional, as load-shedding has become the only way a few of the project operate.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This raises serious questions about the governor’s competence, priorities and commitment to prudent management of taxpayers’ money. Should we judge Governor Makinde’s claim as an electrical engineer by his streetlight project, the answer is obvious to all.

“Equally disturbing is the reported failure of the renovated Lekan Salami Stadium, Adamasingba, Ibadan to secure CAF approval for Shooting Stars Sports Club to host a continental fixture.

“After committing over N5 billions to the stadium renovation project, followed by great fanfare in 2021, the facility could not satisfy the requirements for the very international matches expected of a major sporting arena.

“What, then, did Governor Makinde renovate? Who certified the work, and why should Shooting Stars be forced to seek an alternative venue in Abeokuta, Ogun State after Oyo taxpayers had financed the reconstruction of their traditional home ground?

“The situation represents more than an administrative lapse. It is an embarrassment to Shooting Stars, their supporters and the entire people of Oyo State, and a disgrace to the Makinde-led administration. A stadium renovation that cannot meet the standards required for continental football is another monument to the Makinde administration’s preference for publicity over quality and durable results.

“From streetlights powered with generators to a refurbished stadium unsuitable for continental football, the evidence points to a government that spends heavily but delivers poorly.

READ ALSO: APC challenges Atiku to present alternatives to Tinubu reforms

“The people of Oyo State deserve infrastructure that works, projects that provide value for money and a government capable of planning beyond ceremonies, billboards and political propaganda.

“Oyo State must move away from expensive improvisation and cosmetic governance that have become the order of the day under Makinde.

“Public projects must be designed and executed to serve the people—not merely to provide opportunities for political showmanship,” the statement said.

The campaign organisation added that nothing buttresses the fact that Mr Alli has been living rent-free in Mr Makinde’s mind than the governor using every speaking opportunity to mention and bring the APC governorship candidate into his address.

World.title: Raphinha to sign new Barcelona deal until 2030
World.content:
Barcelona star Raphinha has agreed to stay at the club until 2030, sporting director Deco said Saturday at the club’s general assembly.
