World.title: Planning to study in 2027? NSFAS applications are officially open
World.content:
Students planning to study at university or a public Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) college in 2027 can now apply for financial assistance through the National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS).

Higher Education and Training Minister Buti Manamela officially opened the 2027 NSFAS application cycle during a media briefing in Parktown, Johannesburg, on Friday.

Prospective students have until 18 November 2026 to submit their applications.



Students urged not to wait

Manamela encouraged prospective students to apply as early as possible rather than waiting until the final day.

Applying early gives students more time to check their information, provide any outstanding documents and get assistance if they encounter problems during the application process.

NSFAS will also deploy outreach teams across provinces, districts, rural areas and marginalised communities to provide information and application assistance.

The teams will work with schools, provincial education departments, community stakeholders and institutions to reach students who may otherwise struggle to access funding information.

Changes coming to NSFAS applications

NSFAS has introduced several changes for the 2027 cycle to improve the application process and student experience.

These include:



Direct extraction of student information from institutional systems to strengthen data integrity.

Automated document verification.

Electronic document signing.

A modernised student-support environment.

Stronger verification of student registration and banking details through collaboration with the Department of Home Affairs.

Work on a new Loan Management System for student loans.

The scheme has also been working to improve the handling of appeals, with the aim of strengthening communication with students and ensuring appeals are dealt with according to clear rules and timelines.

Manamela said the changes are intended to make the application process simpler, faster, more secure and more responsive.

Successful applicants are expected to receive their funding outcomes in December, ahead of registration for the 2027 academic year.

The Minister said the changes come as demand for student financial aid continues to increase, with NSFAS receiving a record number of applications during the 2026 cycle.

What about the ‘missing middle’?

Government is also working on another funding option for students who fall outside the NSFAS bursary threshold but still cannot comfortably afford higher education.

These students are often referred to as the “missing middle” because their household income may be too high for a bursary but not high enough to comfortably cover tuition, accommodation, study materials and other tertiary education costs.

Manamela said government is strengthening the missing-middle loan scheme as an additional funding pathway.

Unlike a bursary, the loans are repayable according to the applicable terms and conditions.

The Minister said the scheme is intended to expand the funding system beyond the traditional bursary model while providing another option for students who could otherwise face financial exclusion.

Manamela also urged young people to consider studying at public TVET colleges.

Applications for the 2027 academic year at public TVET colleges are open until 30 September 2026.

The Minister encouraged Grade 9 learners and older students, school leavers and people looking to gain new skills to research the programmes available and consider qualifications that align with their interests and career plans.

Importantly, applying for admission and applying for NSFAS funding are separate processes.

Students must apply to the institution where they want to study and then separately apply for NSFAS funding if they require financial assistance.

World.title: City of Cape Town opens swimming pools for the upcoming school holidays
World.content:
Cape Town’s public swimming pools will be open every day from 23 September to 5 October 2026, giving residents and visitors a chance to cool off during the upcoming September school holidays.

The City said the pools will operate from 10:00 to 17:00 daily throughout the school holiday period.

However, five pools will remain closed while maintenance and redevelopment work takes place.



Five Cape Town swimming pools will remain closed

The following public pools will not open during the September school holidays:

Westridge Swimming Pool

Bellville Central Swimming Pool

Mnandi Swimming Pool

Athlone Swimming Pool

Vulindela Swimming Pool

The City said major maintenance and improvement work is under way at Westridge, Bellville Central, Mnandi and Athlone. Once this work is complete, the facilities will undergo quality assessments and safety checks before reopening.

The City said the four pools will reopen on a phased basis, with reopening dates to be announced once they have been confirmed.



Vulindela Swimming Pool will unfortunately remain closed for the summer season while the City works on plans to redesign and redevelop it.

Pool hours change after the holidays

The extended daily schedule will only apply during the September school holidays.

After the holidays, public swimming pools will move to a reduced operating schedule until 1 December 2026.



From 6 October, pools will be open:

Wednesday to Friday: 13:00 to 17:00

13:00 to 17:00 Saturday and Sunday: 10:00 to 17:00

The City has encouraged residents to check the operating hours of their local pool before visiting.

Most pools will be open during the holidays

With spring now underway, the City said the holiday schedule will give families and young people more opportunities to swim, exercise and spend time outdoors.



The City is also continuing with upgrades, repairs and maintenance at its pool facilities, with major work completed during the previous financial year and further projects under way.

World.title: WATCH: Man threatens to ‘murder’ women at 5-star Sandton restaurant
World.content:
Sandton's Vlamo restaurant has distanced itself from a male patron who threatened to 'murder' a group of women. Images via X

A five-star Sandton restaurant has distanced itself from a viral video filmed on its premises, in which a man threatened to “murder” several women who had allegedly rejected his advances.

The incident took place at the Vlamo Mediterranean establishment in Sandton.

MAN THREATENS TO ‘MURDER’ WOMEN AT SANDTON RESTAURANT

In a video that has gone viral on social media, a man, who claimed to be a wealthy businessman, threatened to physically harm a group of women.



During the incident, which took place in the “powder room”, the man angrily reacted to a woman who had allegedly rejected his romantic advances.

He said: “I will put a bullet in you now, I will murder you now and walk. I can buy this restaurant and own it. You can say no in a nice way.

“I’m a wealthy man. You guys are poor ladies”.



The man – who claimed to live in Steyn City – was later asked to leave the restaurant, which angered him further.

He allegedly threatened to physically harm the Sandton restaurant owner, who is believed to have called the police.

INTIMIDATION | The victims in these video clips are encouraged to come forward and open criminal cases against the ruffian seen threatening women with being shot and killed.



The matter may enable the Designated Firearms Officer (DFO) to institute a Section 102 procedure under… pic.twitter.com/IFp9wMkSaT  September 19, 2026

VLAMO RESTAURANT RESPONDS IN STATEMENT

In a statement posted on its social media platforms, Vlamo restaurant confirmed that the incident took place at its Sandton establishment and that the man, who was not affiliated with the establishment, was escorted off the premises.

“We take the safety, dignity and well-being of women as well as other guests and our team extremely seriously. We have zero tolerance for behaviour that compromises the safety or experience of anyone within the establishment.

Vlamo restaurant stated that it was in contact with the women and would support the steps they took. It also affirmed that it was “committed to providing a safe, respectful and welcoming environment for everyone who walks through our doors”.



REACTION FROM PUBLIC

The viral video trended on social media, with many public profiles speaking out against it.

Here’s what a few had to say…

Siv Ngesi: “He was rejected by a woman, so he followed her into the women’s toilet to threaten her! Let’s make this wealthy man FAMOUS. Maybe he can lose some of that wealth and gain a police charge instead!”



Tumisho Masha: “Men like these can no longer be allowed to live freely amongst us. Please make him trend, and let’s find him”

Cassper Nyovest: “Unbelievable. Despicable! Disgusting! Sies!

Tshepi Vundla: “This is so scary 🥹. Fact, he had the audacity to even walk into the Powder Room 😞”



Mona Monyane: “Weak, insecure and probably doesn’t sleep well at night because of what he does to get his money. These ones are spiritually already in hell, and they won’t hesitate to make others join them.

World.title: Who really won the 2007 World Cup? Jake White or Eddie Jones?
World.content:
Former Springbok head coach Jake White has come under fire after criticising Rassie Erasmus over the way the current coach has managed the national team.

White, who guided the Springboks to the 2007 Rugby World Cup title, questioned the frequency with which Erasmus has rotated his squad and handed out Test caps.

The former Bulls coach argued that the prestige attached to the Springbok jersey and the iconic green blazer had been “cheapened” by players earning caps too quickly.



His comments sparked a strong reaction among South African rugby supporters, with Erasmus also appearing to disagree with White’s assessment.

Following the publication of a video in which White discussed the issue, some supporters accused the former Springbok coach of being bitter, while others questioned how much credit he deserved for South Africa’s 2007 World Cup triumph.

Eddie Jones debate resurfaces, Jake White bashed

The backlash has also reignited the long-running debate over the role Eddie Jones played in the Springboks’ 2007 World Cup success.

Jones, the Australian coach who is currently in charge of Japan, was part of White’s coaching staff during the tournament and has previously been credited with making a significant contribution to the campaign.

Former Springbok coach Nick Mallett famously described Jones’ appointment as a “masterstroke”, while several players from the 2007 squad have also spoken highly of his influence.

Fourie du Preez has previously suggested that the Springboks would not have won the World Cup without Jones’ contribution.



Many fans feel Eddie Jones should take the credit, not Jake White

Jones’ reputation in South Africa was further enhanced when he masterminded Japan’s famous upset victory over the Springboks at the 2015 Rugby World Cup. His win over the All Blacks as England coach in 2019 semi-final is also another highlight.

As a result, some supporters have argued that Jones deserves greater recognition for South Africa’s 2007 triumph.

Jones himself, however, has consistently played down his own contribution and credited White for leading the Springboks to World Cup glory.

Fans question White’s 2007 legacy

White’s latest comments have now prompted some supporters to revisit his legacy as Springbok coach, with several arguing that Jones’ contribution to the 2007 campaign has been overlooked.

One supporter on X, @PeterRugbyEater, wrote:

“I never rated Jake White. Even when he won the 2007 Rugby World Cup.. We all know Eddie Jones had a huge role in that campaign. White was almost fired a few months before that World Cup after losing to Australia with a record score.”

Another user, @TheTruth3212, wrote:

“That’s true. Jake White makes me want to credit Eddie Jones for the 2007 RWC.”

Meanwhile, @The_Claymore69 posted:

“Eddie Jones carried this clown in 2007. Go watch the games in the 2007 era before Eddie Jones joined.”

While White’s comments have sparked a heated debate among supporters, the respective contributions of White and Jones to the 2007 Springbok World Cup triumph remain a subject of discussion among South African rugby fans.

Who was the brains behind Boks success in 2007?

World.title: Cyril Ramaphosa grants Madlanga Commission final deadline extension
World.content:
President Cyril Ramaphosa addresses Parliament during a sitting of the National Assembly. Parliament's Section 89 impeachment committee has agreed to request his appearance before its inquiry. Image: Flickr

President Cyril Ramaphosa has extended the deadline for the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry to submit its final report to 25 January 2027.

The Commission had previously been given until 16 November 2026 to complete its work and submit the report.

The Presidency announced the latest extension on Saturday, 19 September.



The additional time will allow the Commission to process further evidence, including testimony from experts who have made recommendations relevant to its terms of reference.

The Presidency described the latest extension as the final extension.

Madlanga Commission welcomes extension

The Madlanga Commission has welcomed the additional time, saying it will allow it to hear outstanding testimony and complete its final report.



Commission spokesperson Jeremy Michaels said the inquiry welcomed the extension to 25 January 2027.

“This extension to 25 January 2027 will allow the commission to hear outstanding testimony and write the final report,” Michaels said.

The Commission has been holding public hearings since 17 September 2025 and has heard evidence from more than 100 witnesses during its work.



Inquiry into criminality and political interference

The Commission was established following serious allegations made by KwaZulu-Natal police commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi in July 2025 concerning alleged criminal infiltration, political interference and corruption within the criminal justice system.

President Ramaphosa established the judicial commission in July 2025, with retired Constitutional Court Justice Mbuyiseli Madlanga as chairperson.

The inquiry’s work has included testimony relating to alleged criminal infiltration of law enforcement agencies, the Political Killings Task Team and other matters falling within its terms of reference.



The Commission recently resumed public hearings after a two-week break, with evidence focusing on the Johannesburg Metro Police Department and allegations of criminal networks and collusion involving officers.

The Commission will now have until 25 January 2027 to complete its outstanding work and submit its final report.

World.title: Orlando Pirates have EIGHT players on international duty
World.content:
Orlando Pirates will be represented across three nations during the upcoming FIFA international break by eight players. Image: Orlando Pirates media

Orlando Pirates will be represented across three nations during the upcoming FIFA international break, with eight Buccaneers players set to join their respective national teams.

South Africa, Namibia and Zambia have all named squads in recent days, with the Orlando Pirates contingent expected to report for international duty following Sunday’s Betway Premiership clash against Marumo Gallants at the Royal Bafokeng Stadium.

Gamphani Lungu earns Zambia recall

One of the standout inclusions is new Orlando Pirates signing Gamphani Lungu, whose impressive start to life at the club has earned him a first Zambia call-up in more than two years.



The 27-year-old has made 15 appearances for Chipolopolo and could add to his international tally as Zambia begin their AFCON qualifying campaign.

Zambia face a difficult opening assignment away to Algeria before returning home to host Togo.

Six Orlando Pirates players in Bafana Bafana squad

The largest contingent on international duty is for South Africa, with newly appointed Bafana Bafana coach Pitso Mosimane selecting six Orlando Pirates players.

Among them are two potential international debutants: defender Lebone Seema and striker Yanela Mbuthuma.

Seema has carried his impressive form from last season into the new campaign after being named the Premiership Defender of the Season.

The centre-back has been part of a Orlando Pirates defence that has recorded eight clean sheets in 10 matches across all competitions.



Mbuthuma has also been rewarded for his recent form, having scored three goals and provided two assists in his last three appearances.

They will be joined in the Bafana squad by Orlando Pirates captain Nkosinathi Sibisi, goalkeeper Sipho Chaine, Kamogelo Sebelebele and Oswin Appollis.

South Africa’s upcoming fixtures include an AFCON qualifier against Guinea, followed by an away clash with Eritrea in Group D.

Deon Hotto earns Namibia call-up

Veteran winger Deon Hotto could also add to his international tally after being included in Namibia coach Collin Benjamin’s 29-man provisional squad.

The Brave Warriors are scheduled to face Congo-Brazzaville and Comoros in their AFCON qualifiers before travelling for a friendly against Russia.

With eight players heading into international camps, Orlando Pirates will have a significant presence across the continent during the FIFA break.

For the Buccaneers, the international selections also provide an opportunity for several players to gain valuable experience on the international stage while representing their respective countries.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs provide FIVE players to Amajita COSAFA U20 squad
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs will have five representatives in the South Africa Under-20 squad competing at the upcoming COSAFA U20 Championship. Image: SAFA website

Kaizer Chiefs will have five representatives in the South Africa Under-20 squad competing at the upcoming COSAFA U20 Championship in Mozambique.

Goalkeepers Takalani Mazhamba and Keabetswe Morake, defender Egan Freese, midfielder Teboho Mlangeni and attacker Steven Mendez have all been selected for Amajita’s 23-man squad.

Leadership role

Head coach Raymond Mdaka confirmed his final squad on Wednesday after assessing 31 players during a training camp in Johannesburg that began on 8 September.



The team departed for Mozambique on Thursday ahead of the regional tournament, where South Africa have been drawn in Group B alongside Lesotho, Angola and Eswatini.

Mazhamba has been given an additional leadership role after being named vice-captain, with Lazola Maku appointed captain.

Amajita aiming for third straight title

South Africa head into the tournament as back-to-back defending champions and will be targeting another successful campaign.



Amajita’s ambitions extend beyond retaining the COSAFA crown, with the tournament offering an important pathway towards continental and global competition.

South Africa will be aiming to secure one of the two available qualification places for the 2027 CAF U-20 Africa Cup of Nations in Ghana.

A strong showing at the continental tournament could then open the door to the FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup, which is scheduled to be hosted by Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan next year.



Kaizer Chiefs youngsters face busy group stage

Amajita will begin their title defence against Lesotho on Saturday, 19 September at 12:00.

They will then face Angola on Monday, 21 September at 15:00, before completing the group stage against Eswatini on Wednesday, 23 September at 12:00.

The winners of each group, together with the best runner-up, will progress to the semi-finals.



For Kaizer Chiefs, the tournament provides an opportunity for five of their academy players to gain valuable international experience and test themselves against some of the region’s leading young talent.

The Soweto giants congratulated their five representatives and wished the entire Amajita squad well as they look to defend their COSAFA U20 title in Mozambique.

Meanwhile, Kaizer Chiefs only have one player in the 30-man Bafana Bafana squad to play AFCON 2027 qualifiers later this month.

World.title: Aero Defence 2026 puts SA capabilities in global spotlight
World.content:
PRETORIA - The 13th biennial Africa Aerospace and Defence Exhibition is under way at Air Force Base Waterkloof in Pretoria.

Hundreds of military delegates and members of the public are getting a closer look at the latest aerospace and defence technology on display.

The exhibition continues Sunday, with South Africans encouraged to attend on the final day.

Milkor’s Daniel du Plessis described the show as “phenomenal”.

"Our role here is, as diamond sponsor of the event and also a large supporter and contributor, to showcasing some of the defense industry and South Africa's defense industry's capabilities on a global stage.

"We form quite a close contingency as the South African defense industry being a fully private company, also in supporting their efforts in marketing their activities as well.

“I think there's a lot of good things that came from this as well. For us as a company, we had the opportunity to work with a lot of international companies and it's definitely something that we need to retain in the next edition as well.

“The air show is also phenomenal, it attracts a lot of the public as well and I want to encourage the people that missed out on this year's event, there's still some tickets for tomorrow and there will be again for 2028. Make an effort and make it, put it in your diaries that in September 2028 there will be a massive air show as well."

World.title: Phakel’uMthakathi challenges men to step up
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The fight against gender-based violence and femicide cannot be left to government and law enforcement alone.

Activist Nkosikhona Ndabandaba, also known as Phakela Umthakathi, has challenged men to step up.

He wants to see cooperation with police and greater responsibility for the safety of communities.

"We are coming here to say our women must feel safe, our young boys and young girls must feel safe, even the weak and sick must feel safe. We need to build a community where we don't judge the situation by the death of women only, but we judge the situation by the violence that is going on in the country, because on both sides, on females and males, there is violence.

“But on this case where women are being brutally killed like this, we are saying as men, we can't stand aside and look and watch and say it's a fight for the government. We are actually coming to this police station, to this court, to affirm the police that they have our support. You know that the police can't work without the community, and we are offering ourselves as men, for free, to help wherever we can help. If we have to stay awake day and night to make sure that our women are walking safely on the streets, we will do that. We are coming to offer ourselves for the community."

World.title: Politics vs Maskandi in KwaZulu-Natal
World.content:
INANDA - The battle for political space in KwaZulu-Natal is heating up and this time, Maskandi is in the mix.

The EFF’s manifesto launch in Inanda has collided with a Maskandi event planned for the same area.

But EFF Secretary-General Marshall Dlamini is brushing off talk of no-go areas.

He said the party will campaign wherever it chooses as it works to rebuild support lost in 2024.

"There's no law that restricts me to be anywhere, so all is well. The rally is happening there, and while here I can be anywhere. The president is in Mthatha now, so there's no restriction of us being anywhere.

“I've decided to come here just to check because there's no one who's going to tell us that there's a no-go area of EFF in KZN. So when we were told that no fighters are not allowed to come here, I thought let me come and check this no-go area and test it, so we're fine. We've got candidates all over on all the wards of KZN.

“They were campaigning freely and nicely in KZN. We are rebuilding what we suffered in the 2024 election, so all is well, and the rally is part of that rebuilding program. That is why we are here in KZN, just to make sure that there's no issues, everyone else can campaign freely, and that's what we're doing."

Meanwhile, Ngizwe Mchunu is hosting a free entry maskanda concert about 4km away.

Mchunu has wasted no time calling out the EFF leader. He accused Malema of never saying anything worthwhile about KZN, saying he's merely using this as an opportunity to sway the masses.

“The events are not similar. We’ve not gone to their event, we’ve respected it. I will not allow Malema to disrespect the people of KwaZulu-Natal.

“He’s similar to someone sending a 'view once' message. He comes here once in a blue moon then disappears. He’s never said anything worthy about KZN.

“His statements are something else, he’s asking for unity when people are in the country illegally. Women have died in Ekurhuleni and there’s been no leads.

Malema is in favour of illegal immigrants so that they can commit crime freely.”

World.title: FW de Klerk Foundation reflects on SA and US relations
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The FW de Klerk Foundation has expressed concern about the escalating tension between South Africa and US.

Washington has now imposed visa restrictions on certain South Africans.

Christo van der Rheede, the executive director of the foundation, warned these measures could divide the country further, instead of addressing the challenges facing all South Africans.

"I think it's very important to understand the ethno-nationalist approach by the Washington administration. This is seriously problematic because once you start using that as a reason for sanctioning or putting punitive measures in place the punish those who call for land expropriation without compensation or racial redress, then you actually embarking on a very, very seriously problematic approach.

“South Africa at this point in time faces many challenges, and we need to address those challenges, but we need to have a united approach.

“South Africans must be united in condemning corruption, in condemning crime and lack of service in many municipalities. And, that is why we have said that the United States is not really addressing the core issues faced by all South Africans, but instead they are now tearing the country, or tearing the country apart in terms of old racial divisions."

World.title: Activists want to clean up Kempton Park
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Kempton Park communities and civil society groups are working to strengthen local efforts to prevent gender-based violence and protect vulnerable residents.

These stakeholders said ongoing criminal activity in the area is making community-based interventions more urgent.

Lumka Maqubela from Girls2Women Foundation said there is a lot of illegal activities in Kempton Park.

“We are always on the ground 24/7, not only as an NGO, but also with the Kempton Park Residence Forum. We work closely together all the time. The only way we can tackle this is to have patrols.

“But given to the lack of resources, even on our side or trying to assist, it becomes very discouraging. We are willing to go on the ground, patrol 24-7, have the necessary people at every corner. We've got the GBV Brigade where cases are also reported. They go see the families."

World.title: SA is experiencing a GBV epidemic - Tumi Sole
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Runners have handed over a memorandum to the Kempton Park Police Station.

They are calling for a safer environment for runners.

It follows the killing of nine women in various parts of Ekurhuleni.

One of those is runner Elizabeth ‘Tsontso’ Moselakgomo.

Tumi Sole, founder of Running With Sole said want to take a stand.

“This country is experiencing an epidemic of GBV and we are here to take a stand. More importantly, we are here to send condolences to the families of Tsontso, Itemeleng Kekana, Gracious Nkomo and all the ladies that are yet to be named.

“We are saying we can't have Kempton Park Police Station having the highest number of reported cases and nothing is being done. We are saying we have so many laws in this country that ought to be enforced and that should be done. And more importantly any of the women here may be next and I think it's time that the state law and the city do everything that it can to protect them.

“The city needs to fix the streetlights. They need to fix the potholes where services, people around, people walk, go to work. But more importantly, it needs to do what it's supposed to do. And we think it shouldn't take someone's death for there to be action within the country and the likes."

World.title: Mpox cases on the rise in the Western Cape
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Western Cape has been identified as a hotspot area for the recent Mpox outbreak.

15 of the 18 cases reported countrywide are in that province and most of those are in Cape Town.

This has led to the provincial health department strengthening its response.

The health department’s Ednah Baloyi Mpox is infectious.

“We are working very hard to make sure that those two clusters are, or rather the contacts that were involved in that exposure event are followed up, tested, and treated timeously when they're found to be Mpox positive.

“There were two events that, exposure events that basically, you know, did lead to these Mpox cases. So you would understand that Mpox is quite infectious. When you have one person that is in close contact with a group of people, it can actually result in quite a lot of cases.

“So unfortunately, in these two clusters that we identified, there was a positive case, there were positive cases, and unfortunately, it led to the spread of the disease among those that attended those two events."

World.title: Cop killers killed in the Eastern Cape
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Three alleged cop killers have been killed and two others arrested in the Eastern Cape.

They are suspected of killing two police officers in Libode near Mthatha.

Police activated a 72-hour plan to trace the killers of officers Thando Magoxo and Ntlahla Tyhali.

The officers, aged 52 and 32, were from the Mthatha National Intervention Unit and the Public Order Policing Unit.

They were killed while responding to an armed robbery at a local spaza shop.

Police recovered an AK47 rifle and three handguns during the shootout.

World.title: Sifuna pledges to replace taxi torched in Homa Bay violence, after Standard story
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Steven Otieno, a taxi driver from Nyalenda, Kisumu, is facing a double burden after he was attacked during the August 16, 2026 Linda Mwananchi rally violence in Homa Bay. He suffered deep machete wounds and a fractured arm while his vehicle was torched. [Rodgers Otiso, Standard]

Steven Otieno, a taxi driver whose vehicle was torched during last month's violent Linda Mwananchi rally in Homa Bay, can now breathe a sigh of relief after Nairobi Senator and Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna pledged to replace the taxi vehicle, offering a fresh lifeline to the injured driver who has been struggling to rebuild his livelihood.

Sifuna pledged on Saturday after reading the story of the predicament of the man in the Saturday Standard’s story of the driver who has been nursing injuries sustained during the incident.

“I have read this story in today’s Standard. We will replace your vehicle, Steven. The Linda Mwananchi team will be in touch,” Sifuna said in a social media post.

Steven was driving the Subaru Legacy hired to transport Abbie Zuena, also known as Abigail Gikonyo, to the Linda Mwananchi rally in Homa Bay.

Zuena is a mobiliser associated with the Linda Mwananchi political movement and was among those travelling to Homa Bay for the August 16 rally. She had contacted Steven to pick her up from the airport and drive her to the event.

During the rally, they encountered groups of youths and sought refuge at a church. He was attacked and suffered deep cuts to his face, back, arm, hands and feet, including a fractured arm. The vehicle he was driving was later set on fire outside the church.

Steven was taken to hospital and later transferred to Nightingale Hospital in Kisumu, where he continued treatment. More than a month later, he remains unable to resume his work as he recovers from the injuries.

The loss of the vehicle compounded his situation because the Subaru was the means through which he earned his daily income and supported himself and his parents.

His mother, Irene Adhiambo, had appealed for help, saying the family could not afford to replace the vehicle after it was reduced to ashes.

Steven’s case is part of the wider destruction of vehicles witnessed during the Homa Bay violence. A post-rally assessment reported that at least six vehicles were torched after drivers were unable to escape groups of armed youths.

The violence also left dozens of people injured and four people dead.

For Steven, however, the aftermath has remained particularly difficult. While continuing to recover from his injuries, he has been unable to return to the road and earn an income. The destruction of the vehicle effectively took away his means of work at the same time he was recovering from the physical injuries.

Sifuna’s pledge now offers hope that he could regain the means to earn a living.

The senator said the Linda Mwananchi team would contact Steven to work out the next steps in replacing the vehicle.

For the Nyalenda driver and his family, the pledge could mark a significant turn in a difficult period that began with the Homa Bay attack and left him facing both a long recovery and the loss of his livelihood.

World.title: Inside Parliament's probe into secondary school fees and capitation
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Pangani Girls School Chief Principal Dr Millicent Odhiambo before the National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

Parliament’s scrutiny of the Auditor-General’s report on public secondary schools has exposed inconsistencies in capitation funding, student enrolment figures and the National Education Management Information System (NEMIS).

The National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education has raised concerns over the impact of funding shortfalls on school operations and called for discussions with Ministry of Education officials to address the challenges.

The committee is also exploring whether the secondary school fee structure should be reviewed amid concerns that current capitation is insufficient to meet rising operational costs.

Chaired by Luanda MP Dick Maungu, the committee raised the concerns after the Auditor-General’s report showed that several national schools (C1) had sought additional fees from parents above the approved Sh53,000 annual amount, citing rising costs and inflation.

MPs also questioned disparities between capitation disbursements and the actual number of students in schools, which principals said had contributed to underfunding.

For the first time, administrators of national schools appeared before a parliamentary committee to respond to audit queries, with several saying discrepancies between NEMIS figures and actual school records had affected the amount of capitation they received.

Chief principals from Alliance High School, Alliance Girls, Bishop Gatimu Ngandu Girls, Limuru Girls, Mang’u High, Kenya High School, Pangani Girls and Kabare Girls, among others, said they had experienced difficulties validating learner data on NEMIS.

They said capitation received by their schools did not cover all students, with principals reporting that they receive less than the Sh22,244 expected per learner annually. The amount, they said, averages about Sh15,000.

Schools defend additional fees

During the committee’s examination of Alliance High School’s audit report, the Auditor-General flagged the irregular increase in school fees, including Sh17.6 million collected from parents.

“The school charged fees of Sh68,554 whereas the fees as per the Ministry’s guideline is Sh53,554 and the school thus raised fees by Sh15,000 per student annually contrary to Regulation 44 of Basic Education Regulation 2015, which states that no public school or institution shall issue alternative fee structure other than that approved by the Cabinet Secretary,” the auditor read. ‎Alliance High School's Principal David Kamau before the National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

Alliance High School Chief Principal David Kamau admitted that the school had sought alternative funding but said the initiative came from parents.

He said the approved Sh53,000 fee was insufficient to sustain the school’s budget amid rising costs and expectations of maintaining the institution’s standards.

“We have a certain lifestyle we have to maintain and that is why parents came in – in fact it was their idea – and asked us to maintain that. They came in and suggested they can do a budget support so that we maintain the same standards. For us, to acquire the results, we have to do a lot of activities to make sure we give a holistic education associated with the school over the years,” he explained.

“Parents approve that at an Annual General Meeting and we write to the Ministry but that letter of authority has never been granted. We have followed the process to the letter in terms of seeking approval for extra levies from parents,” he added.

The audit also flagged fee arrears in almost all the schools, with Alliance High School reporting arrears amounting to Sh36 million.

Kenya High School Chief Principal Rev Edith Koech was also required to respond to an audit query over unapproved fees under the parents’ association support programme, through which parents were charged Sh25,000 above the set amount per student without approval from the county education board.

Koech said the school had written to the Ministry seeking approval and, although it did not expressly receive authorisation at the time, it had since obtained it.

She said additional funds were approved during annual general meetings, where two budgets were presented — one based on Ministry guidelines and another reflecting what parents felt should be covered.

“Kenya High has its standards, for instance we have tea three times a day and they eat githeri once, they will burn the school if we change,” Koech explained.

Kiminini MP Kakai Bisau said the issue of additional levies had emerged in many schools, with principals arguing that the funds were necessary for students’ wellbeing.

“Looks like this issue is conflicting the law yet public participation is conducted among parents of respective schools. This is something we need guidance on and embedded in policy,” he said.

Other MPs questioned what happens to students from poor backgrounds who cannot afford the additional charges.

Lungalunga MP Chiforomondo Munga said principals had been entrusted with following the law, which states that public schools should not issue alternative fee structures without approval.

“I was a parent of Alliance but all said and done, you have done contrary to the law because approvals must come from the CS and I can assure you there is nobody who will approve that because they know they will be breaking the law and will be held accountable,” he said.

He said the situation presented a dilemma because schools were expected to maintain certain standards while operating within existing regulations.

Embakasi West MP Mark Mwenje said the issue of additional fees had existed for years, noting that he had paid about Sh40,000 while he was an Alliance High School student about two decades ago.

“We just need to sit down with the Ministry because it is becoming obvious that this money is no longer sufficient but we need to inform the principal that whenever such things are happening, there should be concurrence of the Principal Secretary but when we meet with the CS that issue should come out because we can no longer bury our heads in the sand,” Mwenje said.

Igembe Central MP Daniel Karitho described the issue as a “tricky” one, given rising inflation and the need to comply with the law.

“We cannot allow parents from any institution to just sit down and agree because there are those who are voiceless. This is an issue that needs to be discussed even in the House on the fees structure and if there is something that needs to be done, even on the basic regulation so that we can have a level,” Karitho said.

Alliance principal, however, maintained that the school’s process was transparent, with parents being provided with budget documents during annual general meetings and informed why additional funds were required.

“We tell the parents that is their decision to make and if they want to stick to the Sh53,000 but what we can offer as a school will reduce. I can assure we are conscious of the needy and we do not send anyone away because of the fees, either for statutory or additional,” he explained.

Kenya High echoed similar sentiments, saying additional contributions were based on public participation among parents and that no child was sent home over fees. The school also has endowment funds, it said.

NEMIS discrepancies

In another case, MPs questioned how Limuru Girls High School received an additional Sh785,946 in capitation after discrepancies emerged between its student enrolment records and figures captured in NEMIS.

The committee noted variances in Limuru Girls’ records and those of other national schools for the financial years 2020/2021 to 2024/2025.

The Auditor-General’s report for the year ended June 2024 showed that NEMIS recorded 2,099 students at the school in September 2023, 2,300 in January 2024 and 2,354 in May 2024.

However, records presented by the school showed enrolment of 2,062 students in September 2023 and 2,253 students in both January and May 2024.

The difference resulted in Sh785,946 in excess funding, raising concerns over whether the variance affected service delivery in other schools that did not receive capitation and made it difficult to confirm value for money.

Limuru Girls Chief Principal Susan Kariuki acknowledged the discrepancies but attributed them to differences between physical enrolment records and learner information captured in NEMIS.

“The difference arose from variations between the school’s physical enrolment records and the learner information captured in NEMIS at the respective reporting periods. The school did not intentionally provide inflated enrolment figures,” Kariuki said.

“So, because you are given more money, where do you take it?” Maungu posed.

Kariuki, however, said the school had not received the full amount of capitation due per learner and therefore did not consider itself overfunded in the ordinary sense. She said the Government was expected to provide Sh22,244 per learner but the school had been receiving about Sh15,000.

Narok Woman Representative Rebecca Tonkei questioned how Limuru Girls received higher funding for learners who were not captured in NEMIS, noting that other schools appearing before the committee had complained of underfunding caused by incomplete NEMIS records.

Maungu questioned the reliability of NEMIS, saying a system used to determine public funding should be predictable, consistent and dependable.

“This is not a good system. A good system should be predictable, consistent and dependable. But this system gives some people less and others more, sometimes the data is missing,” Maungu noted.

Starehe Girls raises fresh questions

Starehe Girls presented a different case that the committee said contained several grey areas after it emerged that 70 per cent of the school’s 776 learners are fully sponsored while the remaining 30 per cent are self-sponsored.

The school explained that all learners receive about Sh16,000 in Government capitation. For the 70 per cent, their upkeep is sourced through the board of trustees, while self-sponsored learners cover their own costs.

“Being a C1 school, by law it should pay Sh53,000. Instead, some are paying Sh150,000 meaning Sh96,000 extra to take care of the vulnerable. On this other side, you are saying they have a sponsor who take care...are you seeing the kind of confusion because they are already sponsored?” posed Maungu.

Despite the school’s unique funding arrangement, the committee said Starehe Girls remained a public institution and should therefore be audited.

The committee noted that not all financial years had been covered in the audit, unlike other C1 schools, and directed the institution to present all relevant documents for review.

Meanwhile, Mang’u High School surprised the committee when its administration said the school also faced challenges posed by snakes and hyenas that sometimes invade the institution.

World.title: Ruto faults Uhuru for undermining his government
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto join traditional dancers in Homa Bay on September 17, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has renewed his public criticism of former President Uhuru Kenyatta, accusing his predecessor of undermining the government and urging him to withdraw from active political mobilisation.

Ruto said he had supported Uhuru throughout their political partnership and expected reciprocal support when he sought the presidency.

“I stood by you through four elections; I stood by you, helped you, took care of you, and worked for you.”

Ruto claimed the two had discussed an arrangement in which each would serve as president for ten years. He accused Uhuru of failing to honour that understanding, saying:

“When the time came for you to help me, after you said ‘ten years for you, ten years for me,’ not even for a single day did you support me.”

Ruto also appealed to Uhuru to respect the position of former President and withdraw from political activities that he said were aimed at destabilising his administration.

“A former president! Surely, my brother, you are lowering the dignity of the office of the former president. You are a retired president respect your office, go and relax. Let us plan for this country of ours, Kenya,” Ruto said.

Ruto made the remarks on Thursday, September 17, 2026, in Sindo, Homa Bay County, as he concluded a four-day development tour of Nyanza.

The tour covered Kisumu, Siaya, Migori and Homa Bay and focused largely on roads, markets, housing, water and other development projects. The Star+1

The latest confrontation adds another chapter to the complicated political relationship between the two leaders.

Ruto served as Uhuru's deputy from 2013 to 2022, after the two politicians formed a political alliance that won the 2013 and 2017 presidential elections.

Contemporary accounts describe their original arrangement as involving support for Kenyatta for two terms, followed by support for Ruto's presidential ambitions. The Washington Post

The President nevertheless acknowledged Uhuru's democratic right to oppose his government but urged the former president to respect the office he once held.

“You are running schemes to sabotage the government. You are a retired president respect your office, go and relax. Let us plan for this country of ours, Kenya,” he said.

His criticism centred instead on what he described as continued political mobilisation against his administration.

He said his administration had stabilised the economy and pointed to investments in education, housing, markets and infrastructure. During the Homa Bay leg alone, the government highlighted a Sh3.5 billion plan for 21 modern markets.

World.title: Five killed as bandits ambush police search team in Isiolo
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Five people, including two police officers killed by bandits at the troubled grazing field of Gotu in Isiolo County on Wednesday.

The victims are a senior police officer, a police constable who was the driver of the vehicle that was ambushed by bandits, a livestock farmer and two National Police Reservists (NPR). The police officers were attached to an Anti-Stock Theft Unit (ASTU) located near Gotu trading centre.

The victims were part of a search team that was looking for an elderly man who reportedly went missing within the Gotu area and was last seen around Madho Gurba Huka, a grazing area in Chari Ward in Merti sub-county.

Isiolo County Police Commander Isaac Sang said the mentally challenged man from Barambate sub-location, Kulamawe location was reported missing a day ago.

The Isiolo camel keeper, reported to be related to the man who went missing, had requested police to search for him.

The mission turned tragic when the group was ambushed by armed bandits, killing all five on the spot.

The incident took place near the junction of Lososia-Merti road and Gotu-Merti route.

Mr Sang said the bodies of the officers and other victims were removed to Isiolo County Teaching and Referral Hospital awaiting postmortem.

"A reinforcement (of security personnel) had been sent to the area which includes an armoured vehicle to pursue the attackers," said the police chief.

The police boss called for calm and cooperation from the residents while police pursue the suspects.

He said that investigation into the incident had commenced.

On Wednesday afternoon, a gunfight was reported between police reservists and the bandits on the western bank of the river.

"The reservists in the area pursued the attackers minutes after reports of the killings that led to an exchange of gunfire. We are told an unknown number of people have been injured," said a herdsman from Gotu who sought anonymity for security reasons.

A source from Isiolo County and Teaching and Referral Hospital revealed that two ambulances had been sent to Gotu to attend to the injured persons.

Gotu, along with Kom in Merti sub-county is a bandit hotspot in Isiolo that is attributed to competition over scarce pasture by rival herders from Isiolo, Samburu East and parts of Marsabit with local leaders calling for eviction of pastoralists from outside the County. Several people have been killed in the two locations since last year and hundreds of livestock stolen.

On August 1, two people were killed in the Garse Dabata area in Gotu and nearly 700 goats and sheep were stolen. Nearly all the stolen animals were recovered in operation undertaken by a multi-agency security team stationed in various locations along the Isiolo-Meru border.

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen on two occasions called for an operation in parts of Isiolo, Laikipia, Samburu and Meru Counties that had experienced frequent cases of banditry and rustling.

However, leaders fault the CS for failure to take decisive action on insecurity that keeps on recurring in parts of Isiolo and Meru Counties. The leaders including Governor Abdi Guyo want herders from outside Isiolo who are in Kom and Gotu areas to be evicted.

World.title: Muthaiga Golf Club restores access after KFS standoff
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Muthaiga Golf Club has restored access to a section of its course that was temporarily taken over by the Kenya Forest Service (KFS), hours after the agency moved into the area, claiming it forms part of Karura Forest.

The disruption affected the Front Nine, covering Holes Two to Nine, before the club’s board intervened to restore normal operations.

In a statement issued Tuesday, Muthaiga Golf Club Chairman Dennis Mwirigi said the board had taken the necessary steps to facilitate the resumption of activities after the temporary disruption.

“We are pleased to confirm that access to the affected part of the course has been restored and members may proceed with their scheduled activities as usual,” Mwirigi said.

He said the board remained committed to protecting the club’s interests, assets and members while addressing the matter through the appropriate channels.

The development follows an earlier communication to members informing them that KFS had taken over access to the affected section, claiming it was part of Karura Forest.

The club had initially said the Front Nine would not be accessible until further notice as it sought to resolve the matter. The driving range and parking areas were not affected.

The incident sparked criticism over the manner in which KFS handled the dispute, with Prof Karanja, Chairperson of Friends of Karura Forest, urging the agency to pursue dialogue and legal channels.

Prof Karanja said KFS should have first engaged the club’s management and clearly explained its claim over the disputed land instead of deploying dogs, guns and heavy security.

“If they don't agree that it was your land, go to court. The court will determine,” he said.

He questioned whether KFS had adequately demonstrated that the disputed section was forest land or explained how it was allegedly acquired by Muthaiga Golf Club.

“They should have come publicly and said, look, Muthaiga, that area and that area belong to the forest,” Prof Karanja said.

He said KFS should identify the specific portion of land it claims belongs to the forest and explain the basis of its claim before taking further action.

Prof Karanja argued that the dispute should be resolved through established legal procedures rather than force. “Trees are not protected by guns,” he said.

He described the deployment of armed personnel as the wrong way of resolving a land dispute and called for engagement between KFS and the golf club.

Prof Karanja also warned that actions by government agencies could have wider implications for the administration of President William Ruto, saying confrontational conduct could lead members of the public to associate such actions directly with the government.

“When government departments behave like this, everybody now starts thinking, oh, it's Ruto's whatever,” he said.

He further recalled a previous dispute involving Friends of Karura Forest, where he said armed personnel were deployed and the group removed from an area before senior government officials intervened.

According to Prof Karanja, officials from the Treasury and forestry departments eventually intervened and encouraged dialogue to resolve the matter.

He urged KFS to adopt a similar approach in the Muthaiga dispute, saying the agency and the club should present their respective claims and seek a court determination if they cannot agree.

For now, the restoration of access means members can resume their scheduled activities, while the underlying dispute over the contested section remains subject to further engagement between KFS and the club.

World.title: Juja couple's surprise blessing of five babies
World.content:
Mercy Kanini, 28, from Juja, Kiambu County, gave birth to five children at Thika Level Five Hospital. [Gitau Wanyoike, Standard]

A couple from Juja, Kiambu County, is celebrating the unexpected arrival of five babies after scans during pregnancy showed they were expecting quadruplets.

Mercy Kanini, 28, delivered four girls and a boy through normal delivery at Thika Level Five Hospital, in a rare case believed to be among only a handful of quintuplet births recorded in Kenya.

World.title: Two Egyptian cultural projects named finalists in prestigious 2026 ICOM COMMS Awards
World.content:
Egypt’s museum and heritage sector has scored a double victory on the global stage.

Two Egyptian cultural initiatives have reached the shortlist for the International Committee for Communication and Marketing’s (ICOM) ICOM COMMS Awards 2026, competing among the world’s most innovative museum communication strategies.

The exhibition “Secrets of the Sunken City” at the Alexandria National Museum secured a spot in the Best Press Office Media Campaign category.

Meanwhile, the “100 Days of Heritage Truth” campaign—launched by the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities’ General Department of Archaeological Awareness—made the final four in the Best Digital or Social Media Campaign category.

Recognizing international excellence in museum marketing, media relations, and public engagement, the nominations highlight Egypt’s growing capacity to transform raw archaeological science into compelling global narratives.

Redefining underwater heritage and debunking myths

“Secrets of the Sunken City” (Best Press Office Campaign)

Honored for its high-impact media campaign, the exhibition modernized public engagement around Egypt’s submerged heritage.

Highlighting 86 artifacts retrieved from the ancient cities of Canopus and Heracleion in Aboukir Bay and Alexandria’s Eastern Harbour—excavated by the European Institute for Underwater Archaeology (IEA) alongside Egypt’s Central Department of Sunken Antiquities—the campaign’s massive media reach directly prompted a six-month extension of the exhibition.

World.title: EgyptAir crowned World’s Most Improved Airline at 2026 Skytrax Awards
World.content:
EgyptAir has claimed top global honors at the 2026 Skytrax World Airline Awards in London, winning the prestigious title of “The World’s Most Improved Airline.”

Marking a major milestone for the national carrier, the award recognizes a comprehensive overhaul in service quality, fleet modernization, and digital transformation aimed at elevating the passenger experience.

Rankings surge

Global top 50 entry

EgyptAir jumped 22 places in Skytrax’s overall global rankings to secure 46th place worldwide for 2026, up from 68th in 2025.

World.title: Egypt drives $12B tech push with AI, data centers, and infrastructure overhaul
World.content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi met on Saturday with Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, Minister of Communications and Information Technology Raafat Hendi, and key military signals leadership to map out the nation’s digital transformation agenda.

Moving beyond administrative updates, Cairo is positioning itself as a regional tech hub by prioritizing massive cloud infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI), and strict child online safety mandates.

Strategic goals

Surging digital exports

Egypt is targeting eight billion dollars in digital exports by 2028, with outsourcing services projected to hit US $12 billion by 2029. Additionally, the state aims to grow its electronics design footprint to 120 companies by 2030. Infrastructure and AI acceleration Sisi ordered officials to ramp up investment in hyper-scale data centers, cloud computing, and nationwide 5G network deployment. The government is also advancing “Karnak,” its national AI program designed to ensure digital sovereignty and build generative AI models in Arabic.



Unified smart government services The state is expanding the Unified Government Services Card, coordinating with the Ministry of Supply to unify databases and streamline citizen access to public services.



Enforcing child digital protections Minister Hendi reviewed implementation steps for the joint NTRA-SCMR decree issued on September 17, which bans social media accounts for children under 13 and locks mandatory “Safe Mode” settings for users aged 13 to 15.



Transparent talent development Reviewing the “Digilians” presidential initiative—run jointly with the Egyptian Military Academy— Sisi ordered strict neutrality, transparency, and accuracy in candidate selection to ensure youth are effectively upskilled for high-demand tech jobs.

World.title: Sharqiya Governorate imposes total ban on tree cutting to save greenery
World.content:
Felling trees across Sharqiya is now strictly prohibited under a total ban issued by Governor Hazem al-Ashmouny, who warned that penalties will be taken against anyone found violating the decree.

This enforcement measure is part of a broader crackdown to protect existing greenery and support nationwide efforts to combat environmental degradation.

Under the new directive, provincial authorities are expanding green spaces, utilizing vacant land along major thoroughfares, and revitalizing town entrances across Sharqiya’s municipalities and villages.

Ground teams have been deployed to oversee regular irrigation, structured pruning, and the planting of new trees as part of the presidential initiative to expand green zones across Egyptian governorates.

Al-Ashmouny emphasized that safeguarding urban foliage and expanding the province’s ecological footprint are essential to raising living standards, curbing pollution, and modernizing the region’s urban landscape.
