I don't have anything further to add at this point,â he said.

The White House said Trump signed the legislation on September 18. The law extends the Iran Sanctions Act for five years and expands measures against Russiaâs energy and financial sectors.

World.title: BJP promise in its coastal bastion: Why DK Shivakumar put Tulu at centre in Mangaluru
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

chief minister

on Friday announced that Tulu, spoken in the state's Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts, would be recognised as an additional administrative language in the region, fulfilling a long-standing demand.

"Today, we have decided to make Tulu applicable to Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts and declare it the stateâs second additional administrative language," Shivakumar told reporters after a marathon cabinet meeting in Mangaluru.

According to a cabinet note shared by the chief ministerâs office, Tulu would be Karnatakaâs "second additional administrative language" in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi.

The 2011 national census recorded more than 18 lakh native Tulu speakers in Karnataka, whose population was recorded at over six crore at the time.

Kannada is the state's most-widely spoken and its primary official language.

This was also the first time a cabinet meeting was held in Mangaluru and not in Bengaluru.

Eye on BJP's coastal bastion

The political significance of Shivakumar taking his cabinet to Mangaluru becomes clearer against the BJP's electoral dominance in the region.

Coastal Karnataka, particularly Dakshina Kannada and Udupi, has long been one of the BJP's strongest pockets in the state.





In the 2023 Karnataka assembly election, BJP won 11 of the 13 seats across the two districts, taking all five seats in Udupi and six of the eight in Dakshina Kannada. The Congress won only two constituencies.

This was despite Congress sweeping to power across Karnataka with 135 seats, against 66 for the BJP.

The BJP's hold remained intact in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. It won both parliamentary seats covering the region, with Brijesh Chowta defeating Congress's Padmaraj R by over 64,000 votes in Dakshina Kannada.

Kota Srinivas Poojary won Udupi-Chikkamagaluru by more than 2.5 lakh votes.

The BJP responded to the Tulu announcement by alleging that Shivakumar was "peddling soft Hindutva to make a dent in the BJPâs vote bank."

"Shivakumar has never made any secret of his firm belief in Hinduism and frequently visits temples, performs rituals publicly and quotes scriptures. He is now peddling soft Hindutva. This was also evident from his rendition of 'Namaste Sada Vatsale' inside the Karnataka assembly," a BJP leader told PTI, referring to an August 2025 incident in which Shivakumar sang a few lines of the RSS anthem.

The RSS is the BJP's ideological mentor.

But there is a political twist to the Tulu issue itself. The BJP had previously taken up the demand while in power in Karnataka.

In January 2023, the then BJP government led by Basavaraj Bommai constituted a committee to examine granting Tulu the status of a second official language in the state, months before the assembly election.

More than just Tulu

Significantly, Shivakumarâs announcements went beyond granting Tulu the status of a second administrative language.

The Cabinet meeting in Mangaluru marked the Shivakumar governmentâs first meeting outside Bengaluru, the state capital. Shivakumar claimed the move was intended to recognise the regionâs contribution and address its development needs.

He also announced a host of policies for the coastal Karnataka region, introducing a dedicated tourism policy for the coastal areas to treats tourism projects as infrastructure initiatives while offering investors special incentives and extended loan repayment windows.

Additionally, the government approved the Karnataka Marine Biotechnology Policy, 2026-31, which paves the way for upgrading the existing fisheries college into the Fisheries, Marine and Blue Economy University and expanding its student intake from 60 to 200 seats.

World.title: DUSU election results: BJP hails ABVP's 'splendid victory'; Congress claims vote tampering
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) on Saturday won three of the four central panel posts in the Delhi University Students' Union election, with its candidate Yash Dabas elected president.

Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen, who was denied a ticket by the Congress-affiliated NSUI, won the vice-president's post.

BJP hails 'splendid victory'

Union home minister Amit Shah hailed the victory saying "Heartfelt congratulations to all the dedicated workers of the council on the splendid victory of in the Delhi University Students' Union elections.

This victory reflects the unwavering trust of the youth in the council's ideology of "Nation First" and its commitment to student welfare.

I am fully confident that the council's workers, drawing new energy from this victory and following the ideals of Swami Vivekananda Ji, will continue to relentlessly advance the cause of student interests and nation-building."

BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Saturday congratulated the ABVP for its victory.

"Congratulations to all my young friends at Delhi University on ABVPâs historic victory in the DUSU elections! This victory reflects the youthâs continued faith in positive and constructive student politics, rooted in the spirit of Nation First, and their strong resolve to contribute to the vision of a âViksit Bharatâ.





My best wishes to the victorious candidates and everyone who worked tirelessly to make this victory possible," Nabin said in a post on X.

Defence minister Rajnath Singh also congratulated the ABVP on its victory in the Delhi University Students' Union elections.

"Heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all workers on the splendid success of @ABVPVoice in the Delhi University Students' Union elections. This victory is a symbol of the unwavering faith of the youth in the Nation First policy.

I am confident that ABVP will continue to work with the same dedication in commitment to student interests, national service, and nation-building. Heartfelt congratulations to the entire ABVP team and best wishes for a bright future!" the defence minister said in a post on X.

'Tampering with students' mandate will not be tolerated', says Congress

NSUI president Vinod Jakhar alleged that the Delhi University administration was supporting the ABVP and accused officials of attempting to influence the counting process in the Delhi University Students' Union elections.

Jakhar claimed that the lead held by NSUI's presidential candidate Vijay Shankar Meena was being gradually reduced and that the pace of counting was being deliberately slowed.

He said, âThe Delhi University administration has come out in support of ABVP! There have been continuous attempts at rigging and influencing the counting process. The lead that NSUI's candidate for the president's post, Vijay Shankar Meena, has held for a long time is being gradually whittled down, and the pace of counting is also being slowed. This tampering with the students' mandate will not be tolerated.â

World.title: Ecologists urge scientists and policymakers to study imminent ‘Super’ El Niño to prepare for the future
World.content:
As many as 188 of India’s scientists and ecologists jointly published an appeal to fellow researchers and field practitioners to prepare for the effects of upcoming El Niño — a global weather phenomenon that dampens the monsoon and leads to extreme hot and dry conditions in the subcontinent.

In the Pacific Ocean where El Niño originates, temperatures have steadily risen above the 0.5°C threshold, reaching +2.6°C in August 2026. Projections report possible anomalies of up to +4°C, which is higher than at any time in the past 1,000 years, based on reconstructions from coral cores, they said.

Over the upcoming months, the signatories warned, India’s natural systems are likely to experience a range of potentially devastating impacts as a result of El Niño. “These include widespread bleaching and mortality of coral, an increase in wildfires, and the death of large rainforest trees. With a high probability of drought and extreme heat conditions, this year’s El Niño is likely to be catastrophic for India’s farmers, fishers and shepherds as well. In addition, though, more subtle impacts on India’s nature — including delayed fruit production or changes in animal behaviour — could be equally important, but may be much less visible unless you are specifically looking for them,” they said.

The ‘Call to Action’ urges scientists to take advantage of the warning signs and mobilise as a community to document and study the impact of this event on India’s nature, arguing that better science and documentation are essential to preparing India for a climate resilient future.

Jayashree Ratnam, Scientist, National Centre for Biological Sciences, said in a release: “The coming year will be a litmus test for tropical forests and trees in India. Huge forest trees may appear indestructible, but in the Western Ghats, many of them are already near the limit of the heat they can tolerate. Large trees are especially susceptible to extended droughts. Trees in cities are also vulnerable because of the urban ‘heat island’ effect. It is vital to understand how the coming El Niño will impact trees and other plants — as these are the foundations on which all other life depends.”

“I have witnessed the devastating impacts of El Niños on India’s coral reefs before, and it is heartbreaking. Coral reefs can be remarkably resilient, but they need at least a decade after every major die-back of coral to show significant recovery. The last major El Niño was in 2024, and barely two years after that event, the projected scale and intensity of the heat wave that is currently headed our way is truly scary,” said Rohan Arthur, Marine Biologist with Nature Conservation Foundation.

Roxy Mathew Koll, Climate Scientist with the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, also said India’s monsoon season is closing with a rainfall deficit, but the impacts may not end there. “They can creep into the seasons ahead and cascade through depleted soil moisture and water storage, land and marine heatwaves, stressed crops and livelihoods, forest fires, coral bleaching and less visible ecological changes. This gives us a short but valuable window to act. We must document these changes as they unfold, but also safeguard the ecosystems that remain and reduce the pressures already weakening them. What we learn and protect during this El Niño can help India prepare for a warmer and more volatile future.”

What is the 2026-27 ‘Super’ El Nino?

El Niño is a periodic climatic event (every 2-7 years) that is triggered by changed ocean circulation and warming in the eastern Pacific Ocean. Its consequences vary in different parts of the world. In India, El Niño events are typically associated with higher temperatures and a delayed/reduced monsoon. Within the Indian Ocean, the El Niño interacts with another system, the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), which can either dampen or amplify El Niño conditions regionally, according to the signatories.

“Although the last El Niño was only two years ago (2024), all signs are that we will see another event this year, but much larger in magnitude. Since May 2026, sea surface temperatures in the Pacific have exceeded 0.5°C above normal (the threshold for declaring an El Niño event), and those temperatures have been rising steadily, reaching +2.6°C in August 2026. Projections report possible anomalies of up to +4°C, which is higher than at any time in the past 1,000 years, based on reconstructions from coral cores,” the document explained.

It added that the main effects of the El Niño are expected to be felt in the northern hemisphere (including India) from November 2026 onwards into the next year. Indian Meteorological Department bulletins project El Niño effects until at least March 2027 (when their projections end), and the effects are likely to continue well beyond then.

“Based on earlier (albeit less extreme) El Niño events, the Indian landmass is expected to experience substantially hot and dry conditions, and weak monsoons. The surrounding seas are likely to witness marine heatwaves. Of course, the intensities are likely to vary across the geography of the country, and it is difficult to predict the magnitude of impact across India’s ecosystems. Much will depend on how the IOD develops over the coming months,” it said

World.title: Flawed AI-linked intel almost led U.S. to board China ship: report
World.content:
The U.S. military came close to boarding a Chinese vessel in West Asia earlier this year based on a flawed intelligence report prepared with the help of artificial intelligence, CNN said Friday (September 19, 2026).

U.S. intelligence indicated the ship was carrying nuclear weapons-related components, leading American forces to prepare to intercept it, the broadcaster reported, citing four anonymous sources familiar with the incident.

But the operation was called off after officials determined that an AI chatbot used by an analyst had misidentified the material the ship was carrying.

CNN quoted one source as saying the intelligence report was "entirely false" but "almost started a war." It did not specify what the vessel was actually carrying or where it was bound.

U.S. Central Command — which is responsible for American forces in West Asia — did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the reported incident.

The CNN report comes after a furore erupted earlier this month when a researcher publicly resigned from leading AI firm Anthropic over fears that the technology could escape human control.

Another Anthropic employee, who did not resign, said publicly that "we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans," and that he thought the chances were greater than "10 percent within the next decade."

Despite the warnings, U.S. President Donald Trump and some of his key allies have voiced opposition to drastically curbing the development of artificial intelligence.

In a separate incident involving the US military and China, Politico reported Friday that F-35 jet parts — including a sensitive stealth canopy for a cockpit — were diverted to Hong Kong and are now missing, raising fears that Beijing had obtained sensitive American military technology.

The parts were headed from Australia to the United States for repairs when the diversion occurred, the U.S. outlet reported, adding that it was unclear why the parts were rerouted or where they are now.

A spokesperson for Lockheed Martin, which manages the F-35 supply chain, said the company could not discuss specific shipments because of "security reasons."

"Lockheed Martin follows all U.S. regulations established by the Department of War and regulated by the Defence Logistics Agency (DLA) regarding the shipment of aircraft components," the spokesperson said.

"Our teams handle every shipment with the utmost diligence and safeguards to ensure the integrity of the F-35 program and the security of our allied partners."

World.title: ‘System’ run by Modi prefers andhbhakts over students who ask questions, says Rahul Gandhi
World.content:
The “system” running the country does not want students as they raise questions, but wants only andhbhakts (blind followers), Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said in an address to students on Saturday (September 19, 2026). The Congress refers to staunch BJP followers as andhbhakts.

Speaking at the fifth ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ student interaction programme in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, Mr. Gandhi alleged that a “system” had captured the country and was against students and the education system. He said the “system” was being controlled by a handful of powerful people, but students posed a danger to it as they raised questions.

Mr. Gandhi said he had held the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in cities like Kota, Pune, Dehradun and Prayagraj, raising students’ issues such as paper leaks, institutional failure, infrastructural collapse and privatisation. “In Indore, we have decided that we will talk about the ‘system’ vs students today,” he said, addressing thousands of youth at Indore’s IDA ground.

“The system has various layers. At the top, there are six people. The system is run by [Prime Minister] Narendra Modi ji. The tasks of threatening and beating up students with a nail-studded baton and pellet guns are done by [Union Home Minister] Amit Shah ji; he is the enforcer,” Mr. Gandhi said, displaying pictures of several BJP and RSS leaders, top bureaucrats, industrialists and media and film personalities.

‘Top layer of the system’

The top layer of the alleged system, he said, included Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, and industrialists Gautam Adani and Mukesh Ambani.

The Congress MP further accused Mr. Doval of digital spying on people by tapping phones and social media.

“Ajit Doval says in informal conversation that ‘if you want to control India, you just have to control 500 people’. He has captured India’s communication. He gets phones tapped and provides information to Amit Shah ji and Narendra Modi ji. Doval is sitting in mine and your phones,” he says.

Mr. Gandhi also charged that RSS sarsanghchalak Mohan Bhagwat brought ideology to the table and in return, “crores of rupees are given to his organisation to run educational institutions”.

He alleged that industrialist Gautam Adani “finances” the system and “channels the money” earned through government contracts.

“All that money is channeled and given to the BJP for Narendra Modi ji’s marketing and to run the ‘system’,” he said.

‘Capture of institutions’

“Below this layer, there are different people who have captured every institution, like politics, business, judiciary, bureaucracy, education, media, entertainment and sports. The ‘system’ has placed its people in every institution,” he said.

“For example, the ‘system’ has given the entire contract of cricket to Amit Shah’s son [Jay Shah] despite the country having many cricket players. They have divided all the institutions among them like this,” he said.

Mr. Gandhi further said that the students posed a danger to the “system” as they questioned why institutions like judiciary, bureaucracy and the Election Commission “are not doing their jobs properly”.

“This is why the ‘system’ does not want students. It wants andhbhakts who are anti-students. It prepares and promotes andhbhakts. While students are curious, the andhbhakts are delusional and live in their own world. While students talk about love and respect, the andhbhakts spread hatred. While students are humble and listen to others, the andhbhakts are filled with arrogance. While students are fearless, the andhbhakts are cowards. While students respect women, the andhbhakts are patriarchal and attack women. While students are honest, the andhbhakts are dishonest and liars,” he said.

Mr. Gandhi claimed that those who run the “system” did not want their children to become andhbhkts and sent them to study abroad.

He also claimed that more than one lakh schools had been shut across the country and that 55% of them were in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh alone. He claimed that the Union government’s education budget allocation had come down from 4.6% of total budget outlayin 2014 to 2.6% in 2026.

Many students and government job aspirants who were called on to the stage raised issues faced in Madhya Pradesh, including delayed recruitment to government jobs, the holding of government vacancies due to the sub judice OBC reservation hike case and delay in holding nursing exams, which has prompted students to protest.

The family of Arpit Jaj, an 18-year-old student from Dewas who died in the Delhi building collapse earlier this month, also met Mr. Gandhi on the stage and alleged that their son had died due to the “system’s failure”.

“This is the cost of not having the infrastructure and cutting down on government’s [education] budget,” he said after meeting Jaj’s family.

Students vs andhbhakts

As Mr. Gandhi pitted the students against “andhbhakts”, he said that the students were the future of India, and no country could become strong without them.

“We want that the hope in your hearts that has broken comes back fast once again; you start believing in education, and the system; and the country should run with the force of your strengths and qualities — curiosity, honesty, compassion and love,” he said.

“The students can erase the hate and violence going on in the country. Only the students can do it; the andhbhakts can never erase it. We want an India of students, not of andhbhakts. We don’t want an India of arrogance, hate and violence. We want to hear your voice. Never forget that you are the future of this country,” Mr. Gandhi said, concluding his address.

Earlier, on Saturday (September 19, 2026) morning, several posters which appeared to mock Mr. Gandhi with words like ‘Jhooth Ki Goonj’ surfaced across Indore, adding to a list of controversies that erupted in the run-up to the event.

This prompted Congress national general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh to allege that the BJP government of Madhya Pradesh was “terrified” of the event and “tried every trick in the book to stop this program”.

World.title: Chirag Paswan launches Gen Z outreach to ‘counter’ Rahul Gandhi's campaign
World.content:
Union Minister and Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) leader Chirag Paswan will launch a Gen Z outreach campaign called ‘Youth Bole To’ later this month, with party insiders describing it as an attempt to counter Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s ongoing ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ events, in which the Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha raises issues pertaining to the youth.

Mr. Paswan’s campaign will kick off with an event in Patna on September 24, 2026, his party’s Bihar unit president, Surendra Vivek, announced on Saturday (September 19, 2026).

“The grand event, 'Youth Bole To', will be organised at the Veterinary Ground in Patna. At this event, our [party’s] national president Chirag Paswan ji, will engage in direct dialogue with the new generation of Bihar, particularly Gen Z," Mr. Vivek said.

He added, “The objective of the campaign is to provide a robust platform for young people to express their views openly. During the event, the youth will be able to interact directly with Chirag Paswan on various topics concerning their future, including education, employment, skill development, entrepreneurship, technology, and the challenges of the digital age.”

Party insiders said that through the campaign, Mr. Paswan is trying to make an impact in the 2027 Assembly election in Uttar Pradesh, where his party has already decided to contest all 403 seats. After Patna, the youth outreach campaign heads to U.P., with the next event set to be held in Prayagraj on September 27, followed by other cities in the State. According to the party insiders, Mr. Paswan is looking to project himself as a major leader of the youth.

Mr. Vivek said, “Chirag Paswan ji has consistently valued the aspirations and dreams of the youth, as well as their role in a changing India. At a time when the younger generation is playing a pivotal role in the country’s direction and development, the 'Youth Bole To’ event will offer an important opportunity for direct dialogue between the youth and the leadership.”

He further said that the youth were not merely the future, but also a vital force in the present, and that it was essential to understand their perspectives, suggestions, and concerns, and to integrate them into the mainstream of policy and development.

Mr. Vivek asked all party office-bearers, youth activists, and supporters to ensure the success of the event by securing maximum participation. He emphasised that this event was not just a gathering, but a significant initiative to listen to the youth, understand their aspirations, and establish a meaningful dialogue with them.

When The Hindu asked if the LJP (RV) sees Gen Z as its vote bank, Mr. Vivek said. “No, our party does not see the youth as a vote bank. It is our duty and responsibility to take care of all sections of people when we are in politics. Be it students' protests in Patna or Ranchi, our leader always extended his support to their grievances.”

World.title: Agri expo draws huge turnout of farmers in Madurai
World.content:
The three-day Agritech 2026 exhibition, which began on September 18 at the Ida Scudder auditorium in Velammal campus, drew a large number of farmers and general public from southern districts.

With over 200 stalls displaying gadgets, including drones which could sprinkle fertilizers, the expo had information regarding subsidies offered by the Union and State governments for various crops.

The Madurai East Assembly Constituency MLA S Karthikeyan, in his inaugural address, said that the Tamil Nadu government under the leadership of C. Joseph Vijay had announced numerous subsidies and reliefs to the farmers in the budget. The new government had also given waivers to the farmers despite financial crisis, which was due to the failure of the past governments.

The MLA said that the farmers should adopt new techniques and improve their yield which would give them higher returns. He assured to help the farmers and the associations as the elected person from Madurai.

Various leaders from the Tamil Nadu Chamber of Commerce and Industry, MADITSSIA, Agro Food Chamber and Vivasayigal Sangams addressed the sessions.

Tamil Nadu Agricultural University Extension Education Director P.P. Murugan said that in the changing climatic conditions being reported around the globe due to various reasons, the farmers should prepare themselves to face the challenges.

Instead of disappointment, they should come out successfully in such crisis. He also appealed to the farmers welfare associations to ensure that the farmers judiciously used the water for irrigation by taking to drip irrigation and other techniques.

After there was severe drop in farm labourers, the introduction of equipment like harvester machine and transplanters had come in handy for a majority of the progressive farmers to manage the situation. Likewise, they should be motivated to learn the nuances of newer technologies introduced and implemented in countries like Israel, Japan, Germany and the USA.

Agritech expo director Packiaraj said that in the last two days, over 12000 people from Madurai, Theni, Dindigul ,Virudhunagar and Sivaganga districts had visited the stalls which would conclude on Sunday.

World.title: Revanth reviews distribution of uniforms, essentials to government school students
World.content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on Saturday directed officials to formulate an advance action plan to ensure that school uniforms and other essential supplies are distributed to students on the very first day of the next academic year.

Reviewing the distribution of uniforms and educational supplies to students in government educational institutions, the Chief Minister emphasised the need for better planning in view of a likely increase in enrolment. Anticipating a 10% rise in the number of students in government schools, he instructed authorities to make adequate arrangements to meet the additional demand.

Mr. Reddy noted that parents had expressed satisfaction with the quality of the uniforms and other materials supplied this year. He, however, urged officials to make the uniforms more attractive by exploring a range of colour combinations and designs before finalising them for the next academic year. During the review meeting, officials informed the Chief Minister that the distribution of one set of uniforms to students in government schools, hostels and residential schools had been completed. The second set is expected to be distributed by the end of September. They added that students studying in Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) and Model Schools had already received both sets of uniforms.

Officials also briefed the Chief Minister on the supply of notebooks, stating that distribution to all students had been completed. The meeting reviewed the status of distribution of other essential items, including plates, glasses, bowls, spoons, cups, carpets, bedsheets and towels, to students in government hostels, residential schools, KGBVs and Model Schools.

State Government Adviser P. Sudarshan Reddy, MP Vem Narender Reddy, Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister K. Sridhar Rao, OSD Vemula Srinivasulu, and senior officials from various departments attended the meeting.

World.title: Telangana High Court awards one-month jail term to police officer in contempt case
World.content:
Justice K. Sujana of the Telangana High Court sentenced police officer A. Krishnaiah, who went on sick leave while serving as L.B. Nagar Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) of Malkajgiri commissionerate, to undergo one-month imprisonment, convicting him in a contempt of court case. The judge also imposed a fine of ₹2,000 on the officer.

The judge, however, suspended operation of the sentence till October 19 providing an opportunity to Krishnaiah to go for an appeal following the request of Public Prosecutor for Home Palle Nageshwar Rao. The contempt petition was filed by Katta Vamshi Krishna contending that Krishnaiah arrested him in a case of dowry death despite a specific order issued by the HC granting him protection from arrest.

The Bench of Justice K. Sujana on April 21 passed an order not to arrest the petitioner till April 23 and further extended the order on April 27. However, Krishnaiah, who was the investigating officer, arrested the petitioner on April 28 and produced him before the local court which rejected remand of the petitioner on learning that HC had passed protection from arrest order in the case.

“It was incumbent upon him to ascertain whether the said protection had been extended..”, the judge said. The officer cannot contend that he was unaware of the orders passed by the court, the judge said.

World.title: BJP trying to intimidate marginalised groups by coercive tactics, alleges Akhilesh
World.content:
The Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday (September 19, 2026) accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which heads the government both at the Centre and Uttar Pradesh, of threatening marginalised groups through force and coercive tactics. The remarks came a day after a vehicle of the party’s MP Laxmikant alias Pappu Nishad was allegedly damaged in a stone-pelting incident during a Ganesh idol immersion procession in a village in Sant Kabir Nagar district.

“By targeting the leaders and public representatives of the Lodhi community and the Nishad community at times, BJP members and the BJP government are trying to intimidate the PDA [pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and alpsankhyak (minorities)] society by force”, Mr. Yadav said in a post on X.

With just months to go for the election to the Uttar Pradesh Assembly, Mr. Yadav said that the BJP, which faced a setback in the State in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, wants to overcome the disappointment of its “major defeat” by resorting to “coercive” tactics instead of democratic ones. “The BJP’s negative politics will no longer work. If the BJP loses this time, it will never return”, he said in his post.

On Friday night, the SP MP was safely evacuated by the police after a mob allegedly surrounded his vehicle and smashed its window. The matter started when the music system owner and organisers of idol immersion for Ganesh Chaturthi had an altercation following which outraged members of the ‘Puja Samiti’ sat on the road in protest.

The MP’s vehicle, which was passing through the area at the time, reportedly grazed a person from the crowd, leading to the attack. “I was returning after meeting flood victims and other people. I was stuck in a traffic jam at the crossing. Just then, slogans of ‘Pappu Nishad murdabad’ were raised. Seeing the party flag, people began hurling bricks and stones at the vehicle,” alleged the MP. The police have registered a case in the matter.

Members ‘exposed’

The SP president also said that the Ram Temple donation theft case and attacks on the revered Shankaracharya have exposed “irreligious” BJP members and the allies, turning the sanatan society against the party and “ending its communal politics” “Now, in an effort to divide the loot among themselves, they are busy exposing each other’s secrets of corruption and dishonesty,“ he said.

Mr. Yadav added that the SP is committed to creating a “brotherly nation” by establishing the “reign of social justice”. “This will give rise to a new vision, and a progressive ‘neo-India’ based on the positive thinking of youth... where no one will be victimised, unhappy, or humiliated”, he said. “The weak, exploited, deprived, and oppressed in every society will have the opportunity to flourish on the basis of equality”, he added.

World.title: Smoke visible near Riyadh airport after Saudi Arabia issues all-clear
World.content:
A large plume of smoke was visible near Riyadh’s main airport on Saturday after booms were heard and Saudi Arabia sent alerts overnight warning of potential danger around the capital, amid an escalation in attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels.

This is the first time since Yemen’s long-standing civil war resumed that it has threatened the Saudi capital, further shaking a global economy already under pressure by nearly seven months of war between the United States and Iran.

Reuters video and photographs showed a huge pillar of black smoke rising in the area, with the airport highway, main terminal building and other facilities in the foreground. At one point in the video, flames were visible rising from behind what appeared to be fuel tanks.

Aircraft tracking website FlightRadar24 reported major issues at the Saudi capital’s Riyadh King Khalid International Airport, including cancellations and delays.

The airport was listed under the site’s maximum disruption index of 5.0, meaning the airport was seeing “major problems with long delays and several cancelled flights”.

There was no immediate comment from the Saudi government’s media office in response to Reuters’ questions about the smoke and the overnight alerts.

Saudi civil defence sent the alerts by phone overnight for potential danger in Riyadh and the city of Al-Kharj east of the capital, before issuing an all-clear on Saturday morning.

“The area is under a hostile aerial threat,” said a message received just before 3:00am by Riyadh residents, urging them to stay indoors.

AFP journalists then heard two explosions, before the Saudi civil defence agency lifted the alert half an hour later. A Reuters journalist in Riyadh’s Olaya area also heard booms before the all-clear was sent.

“I heard the alarm, then my windows shook,” a Riyadh resident, 27, living in the city’s north, told AFP. “It was definitely scary. I was not expecting this.”

Another resident described the attack as “terrifying”.

“I was extremely anxious — especially because, unlike previous times, the ‘all-clear’ signal didn’t come right away,” the central Riyadh resident said.

Saudi Arabia has not commented on the threat mentioned in the warnings sent overnight to residents of several regions and has not identified where it originated from.

Although some alerts had been issued in Riyadh this year after the start of the US-Iran war, these were the first since the escalation began with the Houthis in July.

The incident comes days after Riyadh accused the Houthis of targeting Makkah on Wednesday, denouncing it as a “cowardly terrorist attack” on the holy city, which welcomes millions of pilgrims each year.

Houthis strongly denied the accusation, calling it a “worn-out lie”.

Houthi attacks

The Houthis, who control the most populous parts of Yemen and much of the north, have been launching attacks towards Saudi Arabia since declaring a naval blockade against Riyadh in July, with strikes targeting Saudi vessels in the Red Sea.

The attacks have created new threats to global oil supplies, putting at risk trade via Bab al-Mandab — the main alternative Red Sea route for Gulf exports — while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains blockaded.

The Houthis insist there is no threat to shipping in the sea lane — except for Saudi ships, from the world’s leading crude exporter.

On Friday, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had foiled unspecified “criminal attempts” in the Yemeni capital Sanaa, blaming Saudi Arabia and vowing a response.

The group, which seized Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast in a lightning advance this month, says the Saudi Air Force has conducted hundreds of airstrikes against it in recent days.

The UN Security Council (UNSC) in a statement on Friday “condemned in the strongest terms continued Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including attacks impacting civilian and energy infrastructure, which have resulted in the injury of civilians, including women and children”.

In the statement, the UNSC also condemned “Houthi military escalation in Yemen”.

The US, according to Axios, last week refused to strike the Houthis at Saudi Arabia’s request.

On Thursday, Washington approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets to the kingdom to help Riyadh “deter current and future threats”, the US State Department said.

The attack targeting Riyadh comes as the Houthis improve their defences in newly conquered territory along Yemen’s Red Sea coastline, with members of the group telling AFP they have been installing radar and digging tunnels.

The United Nations said on Friday that the renewed fighting had displaced more than 112,000 people while nearly 3,000 others had fled across the sea to Djibouti.

The war in Yemen broke out in 2014 when the Houthis seized control of the capital Sanaa and other regions, triggering a military intervention led by Saudi Arabia in March 2015.

The fragile truce reached in 2022 between the warring parties collapsed in July, when the Houthis defied Riyadh’s control of Yemeni airspace by allowing an Iranian aircraft to land in Yemen.

World.title: Kohat Police Lines attack: 8 terrorists killed as overnight clearance operation concludes
World.content:
PESHAWAR: Police said on Saturday that an overnight clearance operation following the deadly two-pronged assault near a mosque in Kohat district’s old Police Lines had been completed, saying that a total of eight terrorists were killed.

After detonating an explosives-laden vehicle near a mosque in old Police Lines during Friday prayers, terrorists stormed the compound and attacked police facilities, martyring at least 21 and injuring over 100.

The death toll rose to 23 on Saturday, including 17 policemen and six civilians, police and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) officials confirmed.

In an official handout, KP police said on Saturday that eight terrorists were killed in retaliatory action by police and security forces.

It said that the operation had concluded, adding that Elite Force commandos, CTD teams, and security forces had cleared key parts of the buildings.

According to the statement, KP Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed was present at the scene. It added that the operation was led by the CTD additional IG, the Kohat regional police officer and the Kohat district police officer. It said that the Kohat general officer commanding was also present.

“Law enforcement agencies achieved success following an overnight operation,” it said.

The statement said IG Hameed commended the officers who participated in the operation and announced rewards for them.

“Police, CTD, and security forces fought valiantly; these brave personnel are the pride of the nation,” he said.

“The terrorists’ nefarious designs have been thwarted, and we will ensure their complete elimination,” he said.

Army personnel stand amid the rubble following an explosion inside the police headquarters at Kohat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on September 18, 2026. — AFP

A CTD statement earlier said that its additional IG was injured in a grenade attack by terrorists during the operation. According to the statement, the terrorists had entered the Special Branch building after the suicide attack on the mosque.

The statement said the CTD additional IG had been on the frontline since Friday afternoon, supervising the ongoing operation against Fitna al-Khawarij along with police personnel.

The state uses the term Fitna al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

It said the additional IG sustained a hand injury in a grenade attack carried out by the terrorists during the operation. After receiving first aid, he returned to the frontline to supervise the operation and boost the morale of the personnel, the statement added.

While the KP police stated the number of terrorists killed as eight, a statement by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi put it at seven.

In the statement, Naqvi paid tribute to the security forces for eliminating “all seven” attackers.

The interior minister said he was proud of all the brave personnel who participated in the operation.

He added that the martyrs of the blast set the “highest example of duty by sacrificing their lives” and their sacrifices will be remembered.

Relief efforts conclude

Rescue 1122 also completed its relief and rescue operation on Saturday, with 24 vehicles — including ambulances, rescue vehicles and recovery vehicles — taking part in the efforts.

In a statement, Rescue 1122 said Kohat District Emergency Officer Noorul Amin Khattak monitored the rescue operation, in which more than 60 personnel took part.

Rescuers and vehicles from other districts, including Karak and Hangu, also assisted in the relief efforts.

Seven of the injured were referred to Peshawar for further treatment, with five of them taken to Lady Reading Hospital and two to Hayatabad Medical Complex.

Rescue 1122 spokesperson Bilal Ahmed Faizi noted that the personnel effectively conducted the relief and rescue efforts in “extremely tough, sensitive and dangerous conditions” while demonstrating excellent professional skills.

‘Pakistan has will, capability to protect its citizens’

The Ministry of Information strongly condemned the terrorist attack on civilians and police officials offering Friday prayers in Kohat, saying Pakistan had repeatedly raised concerns with the Afghan Taliban over the use of Afghan territory by terrorist groups to plan and carry out attacks inside the country.

In a statement, the ministry said the presence of terrorist sanctuaries and recruitment and support networks in Afghanistan posed a direct threat to Pakistan’s security. It said these concerns had repeatedly been conveyed to the Afghan Taliban regime and its interlocutors, urging them to dismantle the networks instead of deflecting responsibility.

The ministry also criticised Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid for threatening Pakistan with a “crushing response”, saying the Afghan Taliban should address the terrorist networks operating under their patronage. It said Pakistan had noted the Afghan Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ condemnation of the Kohat attack and expression of sympathy for the victims’ families, but regretted that the statement did not mention terrorism.

The ministry said condemnation should be accompanied by “concrete action”, calling on the Afghan Taliban to take credible, verifiable and sustained measures to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries and disrupt recruitment and training networks.

“Pakistan has both the will and the capability to eliminate terrorist threats wherever they are and will take all necessary measures, in accordance with international law, to protect its citizens, territory and sovereignty.”

It added Pakistan remained committed to dialogue and constructive engagement but would take all necessary measures, in accordance with international law, to protect its citizens, territory and sovereignty, and urged the international community to press the Afghan Taliban to take action against terrorist groups.

KP CM visits injured, bereaved families

Separately, Chief Minister Sohail Afridi visited those injured in the blast and the families of those martyred, KP Information Minister Shafi Jan said.

CM Afridi directed the relevant authorities to provide the wounded with the best possible medical facilities, and extended his condolences to the bereaved families.

“He assured the affected families that the government stands with them and they will be provided with every possible support during this difficult time,” the statement said.

CM Afridi had sought a detailed report on the incident on Friday, saying the targeting of innocent citizens was “deeply regrettable and unacceptable”.

“The nation’s morale cannot be dampened by cowardly acts of terrorism,” he had said in a statement issued by his office following the blast.

The attack was claimed by the Hafiz Gul Bahadur-led Ittehadul Mujahideen.

Funeral prayers for 15 of the martyred police personnel were offered in Kohat on Friday evening, after which their bodies were transported to their native districts of Kohat, Karak, Lakki Marwat, Bannu and Mardan in Rescue 1122 ambulances.

Among the slain were SP Traffic Akbar Shinwari, head of the paediatric department at DHQ Hospital Dr Israel Orakzai, and Special Branch and CTD officials.

It may be recalled that in 2010, 20 people, mostly relatives of policemen, were killed and more than 90 injured in a remote-controlled bomb blast inside a police colony located just behind the Kohat Police Lines. The explosion had taken place in Ramazan during Iftar.

World.title: 'No one can minus Imran': Senate opp leader says only PTI founder can postpone Sept 27 Islamabad march
World.content:
Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas on Saturday said only PTI founder Imran Khan had the authority to postpone his party’s countrywide protest planned for September 27.

The PTI has called for a nationwide protest , including a “long march” to Islamabad, to demand the release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) opposition alliance, which Abbas is a key leader of, has assured the PTI of its support for the protest.

A post on Abbas’ X account on Saturday claimed that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had called on him and that the latter was informed only Imran could postpone the September 27 protest.

“No one can minus Imran,” he wrote.

TTAP Spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousufzai, speaking to Dawn, claimed that the meeting was held on September 14 on Naqvi’s request.

He added that Abbas and PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan attended the meeting on the opposition’s side.

Responding to queries after a press conference at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa House in Islamabad, Abbas said: “He (Naqvi) came to meet [us]. We have stated our stance and they will find out … that no individual can postpone the September 27 march without a meeting with Imran Khan sahib.”

He asserted, “Imran Khan cannot be minused; we will not let Imran Khan sahib be minused. Therefore, no issue can be resolved without a meeting with Imran Khan sahib.”

During the press conference, Abbas said providing basic facilities to the people and protecting their constitutional rights were major issues. He said that even a senior federal minister had acknowledged that the country’s system had “collapsed”.

TTAP leader and former Sindh governor Mohammad Zubair said there was a wide gap between the lifestyle of the ruling elite and the economic difficulties faced by ordinary citizens. He claimed that poverty, unemployment and inflation had increased compared with four and a half years ago. He said electricity prices had risen two to threefold, while people had made sacrifices in the hope that economic conditions would improve.

PTI leader and former KP finance minister Taimur Saleem Jhagra criticised government spending, questioning the reported purchase of a jet costing Rs10 billion and expenditure on official and private travel. He said every rupee of public money should be accounted for and questioned why relief was not being provided to people facing rising fuel prices.

On Friday, days after the meeting reportedly took place, Naqvi declared that the government would stop anyone from marching towards the federal capital “in every possible way”.

He further warned of contempt of court proceedings against those who violated the recent ruling by the Islamabad High Court (IHC), wherein it termed any activity resulting in infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights as a violation of the Constitution.

“The question is not whether a political party is entitled to protest. It plainly is, subject always to the Constitution and law,” the judgment observed.

KP CM meets Achakzai, Abbas

Abbas’ remarks come after earlier in the day, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi met him and NA Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai to discuss the PTI’s upcoming protest.

In a post on X, TTAP said the KP CM held an “important meeting” with Abbas and Achakzai, who is also the TTAP chairman. Yousafzai was also present on the occasion.

“Detailed political consultations regarding the call for September 27 were held during the meeting, and various aspects of the future course of action, political strategy, and advancing the democratic struggle in an effective manner were discussed,” the statement said.

The politicians consulted on taking forward the protest call as an “effective and organised political struggle for upholding the supremacy of the Constitution, democratic rights, provincial rights, and the protection of the public mandate”.

The trio had also met on Thursday, shortly after CM Afridi concluded his visit to Punjab, where the upcoming protest was among the topics discussed.

As part of the PTI’s preparations, the KP CM toured Sindh and Punjab to mobilise supporters for the protest.

During his visit to the PML-N-led Punjab, Afridi not only alleged he was “ abducted ” by authorities in Lahore and later “thrown” by the roadside, but also claimed a man was sent to kill him.

The Punjab government had swiftly refuted the claims of arrest, while the Wazirabad police clarified that the man accused by Afridi was a police constable deployed on security duty for the KP CM.

World.title: Govt, JI talks end inconclusively as Islamabad seeks delay in long march over security threats
World.content:
LAHORE: The fifth round of talks between the government and the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) concluded on Saturday, with the government seeking the postponement of the party’s planned long march due to security threats.

The government delegation included Federal Minister for Planning Ahsan Iqbal, Rana Sanaullah and Punjab Minister Khawaja Salman Rafique.

The JI delegation comprised Deputy Emir Liaquat Baloch, Acting Secretary General Nazir Ahmad Janjua, Special Assistant to the JI Emir Umair Idrees, JI Lahore Emir Ziauddin Ansari and Information Secretary Shakeel Ahmad Tarrabi.

During the talks, the government delegation requested the JI to postpone the long march in view of security threats.

However, Baloch said the long march would remain necessary until the levy imposed on the public was withdrawn.

The government levies Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. The JI has been staging regular sit-ins in Lahore, Peshawar, Karachi and dozens of other locations across the country since August 16 to protest the levy.

The government delegation assured the JI that extraordinary relief would soon be provided to the people. It also said the government was under pressure from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and that an IMF delegation was expected to visit Pakistan shortly.

Baloch said the government must take practical steps to address the people’s demands; otherwise, the JI would definitely proceed with its protest and long march.

He said that, as per the schedule, the “Super Long March” under the leadership of the JI emir would begin from Karachi on Sunday.

Talks between the JI and the government began on Sept 7 and have so far comprised four inconclusive rounds. The fifth round on Saturday also ended without an agreement.

‘No turning back’

Earlier, the party dug its heels in over its planned march, refusing to call it off unless the government abolishes the petroleum levy, with party chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman announcing that protest caravans from across the country would begin moving toward the capital on Sunday.

“If the rulers cannot abolish the levy, we cannot call off our march,” Rehman said at a press conference in Mansoorah, setting the stage for a potential standoff with the authorities.

The government, equipped with a recent Islamabad High Court (IHC) ruling against activities that curtail the freedom of movement, is determined to prevent rallies from disrupting traffic and the normal flow of life in the federal capital.

Rehman promised peaceful protest and warned the government not to take any action against the protesters.

“A public rally will be held in Karachi on Saturday night, before the caravans set out for Islamabad on September 20,” he said.

The JI chief urged the government to present a concrete proposal for abolishing the petroleum levy, noting the party had already rejected the government’s fuel relief package as inadequate.

Under the government’s current relief scheme, eligible motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqi rickshaws and cars up to 800cc are to receive a subsidy of Rs100 per litre, subject to specified monthly limits.

Rehman said relief was not a favour but a right of the people, accusing the government of avoiding structural measures to reduce the burden on consumers, saying petroleum prices had a direct impact on the cost of essential commodities across the country.

He claimed that up to Rs107 per litre was being collected as petroleum levy on petrol, in addition to other taxes.

The JI chief criticised the government for failing to curb corruption and what he described as “excessive official expenditure”, saying officials should reduce their own spending instead of asking the people to make sacrifices.

To absorb the economic impact of renewed tensions in the Middle East, the government has reintroduced austerity measures, reducing fuel provision for official vehicles by 50 per cent for a period of three months.

Islamabad march

Rehman noted that the JI’s protest movement had entered its 35th day, with more than 25 sit-ins continuing across the country. He said the party had held peaceful demonstrations in 42 cities and claimed that the movement had now become a national issue.

“We are marching for the people with their support. There is no question of turning back,” he said, insisting that the number of sit-ins was being gradually reduced as part of the JI’s strategy for the Islamabad march.

The JI chief said the government had again contacted the party for talks, but repeatedly sought more time.

“If the government does not listen to talks, it will have to listen to public pressure,” he said.

On the PTI’s protest planned for September 27 for its incarcerated founder Imran Khan, Rehman said peaceful protest was a constitutional right of every political party and that containers should not be placed to block PTI demonstrations.

He said the JI supported the PTI’s right to peaceful protest, while the PTI had also supported the JI’s right to do so.

Economic policies criticised

On negotiations, Rehman said the government had repeatedly asked the JI to submit suggestions, although, he argued, it was the government’s responsibility to address public grievances.

He recalled that his party had already presented proposals during previous rounds of talks, but the government did not accept them.

Rehman also criticised the government’s economic policies, calling for a reduction in interest rates and questioning the State Bank of Pakistan’s autonomy. He argued that the government’s role in appointments to the central bank raised questions about its independence.

He further accused the government of using the International Monetary Fund (IMF) as an excuse for withholding relief from the public while continuing what he described as lavish official expenditure.

Citing foreign travel by senior officials and expenses incurred at official meetings, the JI chief called on Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz to sell her official aircraft, which he valued at Rs11 billion.

Turning to the sugar and wheat sectors, the party chief alleged that powerful groups and cartels were influencing government decisions on imports and exports, further alleging farmers were not receiving adequate prices for wheat and sugarcane, contributing to higher food prices.

He also criticised payments to independent power producers (IPPs), saying Rs1.8 trillion was being paid in capacity payments. He further questioned payments to regasification plants despite what he described as gas shortages.

JI Acting Secretary General Nazir Ahmad Janjua, Vice Emir Dr Usama Razi and Deputy Secretary Azhar Iqbal Hassan were also present at the press conference.

On Friday, Rehman claimed the party’s protest movement aimed to press the government for immediate economic relief, asserting that the national exchequer could save between Rs3 trillion and Rs4 trillion if the authorities adopted the party’s proposed fiscal reforms.

World.title: Denmark hails 'binding' Greenland deal with Trump
World.content:
Denmark on Saturday hailed a “binding” deal announced by US President Donald Trump to give Washington “permanent control“ over Greenland’s security and bar Russian and Chinese bases from the Arctic territory.

Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has repeatedly insisted that Washington needed to control Greenland for strategic reasons, alarming NATO ally Denmark and sparking fierce pushback from the alliance.

Denmark and Greenland — an autonomous Danish territory — both hailed the agreement and said they would sign it on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York next week.

“A long period of uncertainty will hopefully be replaced by a binding agreement that strengthens security in the Arctic and North Atlantic,” Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said in a social media post on Saturday.

The deal respected Denmark’s “red lines” and was “important” in light of a changed security situation, he said.

While the terms are still unclear, Denmark maintains that its sovereignty remains intact.

Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said the agreement with Washington “recognises the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the Greenlandic people’s right to self-determination”.

It was “good for NATO and Europe”, she said.

Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said the deal “recognises Greenland’s interests” and “strengthens” its security.

In Greenland’s capital Nuuk, residents had mixed feelings.

“I don’t know exactly what the agreement is or what has been signed. But whenever the US and Trump are mentioned, I have mixed feelings. I’m not entirely comfortable with how much attention Greenland has right now,” Soren Kreutzmann, a 29-year-old hairdresser, told AFP.

“We hope the leaders have made a good agreement, because our country needs to be protected, both from the air and sea. Denmark had not given that enough attention for many years,” said Bibbi Kleist Jepsen, a 64-year-old pedagogue.

Trump hailed the deal as an “’Infinite Life’ Agreement, there is no end!”. Washington would immediately start building up a large military presence in the territory, he added.

“From now on, no US adversary can EVER have a base in Greenland, have a military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval.”

While Trump presented the deal as a major triumph, Danish commentators said he had likely gained little.

They noted that, under a 1951 defence pact updated in 2004, Washington was already able to ramp up its military presence on the island provided it informs Denmark and Greenland in advance.

“Shhh. Don’t tell Trump that it’s the Kingdom of Denmark that has prevailed,” US correspondent Jacob Heinel Jensen wrote in Danish newspaper Berlingske on Saturday.

Ulrik Pram Gad, a researcher at the Danish Institute for International Studies, said Trump “obviously didn’t get in this agreement what he originally set out to have, that is, sovereign control over all of Greenland as a part of the United States”.

China, Russia concerns

Trump has repeatedly warned of Russia and China trying to establish a foothold in Greenland as a strategic battle unfolds for supremacy in a warming Arctic. The State Department left no doubt that they would not be allowed to do so.

“This agreement guarantees that China and Russia cannot have a base in Greenland, they cannot send troops to Greenland, and the necessary mechanisms are in place to prevent investment in sensitive sectors,” a State Department official said.

Gad noted that while Russia had little interest in Greenland, China was investing in extractive industries to get a foothold in the Arctic.

“The US is worried that any kind of Chinese footprint could be turned into military assets,” he said.

Cautioning that the details of the deal remained unknown, Gad said “the worrisome thing here is this exclusive access for the US to build bases in Greenland and how that involves NATO allies from Europe.

“Trump has been flirting with breaking up the NATO alliance… If Europe is an adversary, how would that position Europe, Denmark and Greenland in that situation?”

Furthermore, “if the US can also veto European investments in Greenland, that would be highly controversial.”

Several media outlets have reported that Washington wants to open three new military bases in southern Greenland, in addition to the Pituffik base it already has in the north of the territory.

At the height of the crisis, Trump would not rule out using force to seize the territory of 57,000 inhabitants, sowing anxiety within the EU and NATO.

Tensions have since eased. In an apparent move to assuage Trump, NATO launched a mission to bolster security in the Arctic.

World.title: Trump lists 25 'top achievements' as midterms loom
World.content:
President Donald Trump claimed he halted all refugee admissions and made English the official language of the United States in a long list of what he called his top achievements, as difficult midterm elections loom.

Trump is scrambling to boost his low approval ratings ahead of November’s vote, with polls showing the unpopular war in Iran and the fuel and other price rises it has caused are hurting his Republican Party.

Polls say the party could well lose control of the House and perhaps even the Senate, a setback which would pose a major challenge for Trump and his America-first agenda in the last two years of his second term.

Trump said Friday he “achieved the most secure border in history” in a lengthy social media post on Truth Social that focused on immigration, foreign policy and the economy.

“ZERO illegal aliens admitted to the United States in the past 16 months,” he wrote, adding that his administration had slashed refugee admissions from “dangerous places”.

Trump has presided over an often violent immigration crackdown which involves frequent deportations and shipping people whom the US cannot legally send home to third countries, which are sometimes compensated with money.

He also claimed the US had “obliterated Iran’s nuclear enrichment capacity” to ensure the Islamic republic “will NEVER have a nuclear weapon”. This was one of Trump’s often-changing justifications for going to war in February.

The US-Israeli strikes on Tehran have rocked the global economy and engulfed the Middle East in war, proving a quagmire for a president who promised not to get America involved in any more foreign wars.

Trump also flaunted hefty tariffs slapped on US trading partners, which he said were to “bring back American manufacturing”.

World.title: DPM Dar directs inclusion of all operational fuel stations in PM’s relief scheme
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Saturday directed that all operational fuel stations be brought onto the system under the prime minister’s fuel relief scheme, while permanently closed stations and those dealing exclusively in diesel be removed from the list.

He issued the directives while chairing a meeting of the National Steering Committee on Fuel Subsidy to review the implementation of the scheme, according to a statement issued by his office.

“Every fuel station which is open and operating” should be brought onto the system, while stations found permanently closed or dealing exclusively in diesel should be identified and removed from the list, the statement quoted him as saying.

The committee was informed that an overwhelming majority of fuel stations across the country were now operational on the system and that citizens were redeeming fuel tokens.

Registration is continuing nationwide via SMS to 9771.

The committee also approved the redemption of fuel tokens via SMS at stations in areas without internet connectivity. Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) and the provinces were asked to furnish lists of such stations so that they could be brought onto the scheme without delay.

The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) informed the committee that all payment claims received over the past three days had been settled in full, with claims received each day processed on the same day.

Dar appreciated the efforts of the provincial administrations and the cooperation extended by the SBP, stressing that “the relief must continue to reach the intended beneficiaries without hindrance”.

PM Shehbaz on Sep 13 announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Under the scheme, owners of motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqis, three-wheelers and vehicles with engines of up to 800cc will receive a Rs100 per litre relief on petrol.

On Friday, PM Shehbaz approved a revised structure for the public under the fuel relief scheme currently in vogue across the country, expanding it to include more two- and three-wheelers, and easing weekly limits to offer motorists more flexibility in how they use the support.

He directed that motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws up to 20 years old should also be included in the scheme.

Renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have resulted in disruption of major oil supply routes, have caused fuel prices to rise in the past two months.

In addition to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz due to the US-Iran war, trade via Bab al-Mandab — which has become a vital route for Saudi oil exports in recent months — is also facing a rising threat from Houthi rebels.

The subsidy scheme faced snags on Thursday, the first day of its nationwide rollout, as many petrol pumps declined to honour the digital app, claiming they lacked the system needed to provide petrol at Rs100 per litre less.

World.title: LHC directs foreign ministry to process pleas over detention of 2 PTI-linked Pakistanis in UAE
World.content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has directed the secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) to process and decide within 15 days representations concerning the detention of two Pakistani citizens and PTI-affiliated individuals in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram issued the directions in written orders on Sept 14 on two separate petitions filed by the families of Syed Salman Raza Zaidi and Muhammad Junaid Jahangir through Barrister Abuzar Salman Niazi.

According to the petitions, Zaidi went missing from his residence in Sharjah on Sept 27, 2024, and was subsequently taken into custody by UAE authorities.

His wife, Faryal Zainab, told the court that despite nearly two years having passed, she had not been provided with clear information about the charges against her husband, the judicial proceedings, any sentence imposed on him or the complete court record.

In the second petition, Muhammad Ibrahim, Jahangir’s father, said his son was allegedly detained at Dubai airport on Sept 24, 2024, upon his return from Saudi Arabia.

The petitions challenged the alleged failure of the federal government and the Foreign Office to provide effective consular protection and legal assistance to the two men.

Barrister Niazi told the court that representations regarding the detention of both citizens had been submitted to the foreign secretary but had not been processed.

The petitioners sought legal and consular assistance for the two men, access to their judicial records and diplomatic steps for their return to Pakistan. They also sought a report on the steps taken by the state in the matter.

After examining the petitions and the documents attached to them, Justice Khurram directed the foreign secretary to process the representations concerning the detention of Zaidi and Jahangir in the UAE, if they were still pending, in accordance with the law and expeditiously.

The court directed that the representations be decided preferably within 15 days of receipt of a certified copy of its orders.

The judge disposed of both petitions with these directions.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment.
